text: A large mobile network operating company is building a machine learning model to predict customers who are likely to unsubscribe from the service. The company plans to offer an incentive for these customers as the cost of churn is far greater than the cost of the incentive. The model produces the following confusion matrix after evaluating on a test dataset of 100 customers: Based on the model evaluation results, why is this a viable model for production?

choices.A: The model is 86% accurate and the cost incurred by the company as a result of false negatives is less than the false positives.
choices.B: The precision of the model is 86%, which is less than the accuracy of the model.
choices.C: The model is 86% accurate and the cost incurred by the company as a result of false positives is less than the false negatives.
choices.D: The precision of the model is 86%, which is greater than the accuracy of the model.

explanation:
Key Concept: Evaluate a churn classifier using both the confusion matrix and the business cost of each error.

A. The model is 86% accurate and the cost incurred by the company as a result of false negatives is less than the false positives. — Accuracy is 86%, but the stated cost relationship is reversed: losing a customer costs more than offering an unnecessary incentive.

B. The precision of the model is 86%, which is less than the accuracy of the model. — Precision is 10/(10+10) = 50%, not 86%. Accuracy is (10+76)/100 = 86%.

C. The model is 86% accurate and the cost incurred by the company as a result of false positives is less than the false negatives. — Conditionally supported: accuracy is 86%, and an unnecessary incentive costs less per case than missed churn. Overall profitability still requires actual costs.

D. The precision of the model is 86%, which is greater than the accuracy of the model. — Precision is 50%, below the 86% accuracy. Both the stated precision and the comparison are incorrect.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is designing a system for improving sales for a company. The objective is to use the large amount of information the company has on users' behavior and product preferences to predict which products users would like based on the users' similarity to other users. What should the Specialist do to meet this objective?

choices.A: Build a content-based filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR
choices.B: Build a collaborative filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR.
choices.C: Build a model-based filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR
choices.D: Build a combinative filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR

explanation:
Key Concept: Collaborative filtering recommends items using similarities in users' historical interactions.

A. Build a content-based filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR — Content-based filtering compares item attributes with an individual user's interests; it does not directly use similar users' preferences.

B. Build a collaborative filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR. — The requirement explicitly uses similarity between users, which collaborative filtering learns from user–item interactions in Spark ML.

C. Build a model-based filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR — Model-based describes an implementation family that can include collaborative filtering; it does not identify the required recommendation approach as directly as B.

D. Build a combinative filtering recommendation engine with Apache Spark ML on Amazon EMR — A combined approach is unnecessary here. The question specifically requests recommendations based on other similar users.

text: A Mobile Network Operator is building an analytics platform to analyze and optimize a company's operations using Amazon Athena and Amazon S3. The source systems send data in .CSV format in real time. The Data Engineering team wants to transform the data to the Apache Parquet format before storing it on Amazon S3. Which solution takes the LEAST effort to implement?

choices.A: Ingest .CSV data using Apache Kafka Streams on Amazon EC2 instances and use Kafka Connect S3 to serialize data as Parquet
choices.B: Ingest .CSV data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use Amazon Glue to convert data into Parquet.
choices.C: Ingest .CSV data using Apache Spark Structured Streaming in an Amazon EMR cluster and use Apache Spark to convert data into Parquet.
choices.D: Ingest .CSV data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to convert data into Parquet.

explanation:
Key Concept: A streaming ETL service must parse the input format before producing columnar Parquet output.

A. Ingest .CSV data using Apache Kafka Streams on Amazon EC2 instances and use Kafka Connect S3 to serialize data as Parquet — A self-managed Kafka deployment and connector require more configuration and operations than a managed Glue streaming job.

B. Ingest .CSV data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use Amazon Glue to convert data into Parquet. — Glue streaming ETL can read CSV records from Kinesis Data Streams, transform them, and write Parquet to S3.

C. Ingest .CSV data using Apache Spark Structured Streaming in an Amazon EMR cluster and use Apache Spark to convert data into Parquet. — Spark on EMR can perform this conversion, but requires cluster and streaming application management.

D. Ingest .CSV data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to convert data into Parquet. — Firehose's built-in Parquet conversion expects JSON input. CSV needs an additional transformation step that this option omits.

text: A city wants to monitor its air quality to address the consequences of air pollution. A Machine Learning Specialist needs to forecast the air quality in parts per million of contaminates for the next 2 days in the city. As this is a prototype, only daily data from the last year is available. Which model is MOST likely to provide the best results in Amazon SageMaker?

choices.A: Use the Amazon SageMaker k-Nearest-Neighbors (kNN) algorithm on the single time series consisting of the full year of data with a predictor_type of regressor.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Random Cut Forest (RCF) on the single time series consisting of the full year of data.
choices.C: Use the Amazon SageMaker Linear Learner algorithm on the single time series consisting of the full year of data with a predictor_type of regressor.
choices.D: Use the Amazon SageMaker Linear Learner algorithm on the single time series consisting of the full year of data with a predictor_type of classifier.

explanation:
Key Concept: Forecasting a numeric pollutant concentration is a regression problem; time-based features must be constructed from the history.

A. Use the Amazon SageMaker k-Nearest-Neighbors (kNN) algorithm on the single time series consisting of the full year of data with a predictor_type of regressor. — kNN can regress, but nearest-neighbor predictions do not naturally extrapolate trends. It is less suitable than the regression baseline offered here.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker Random Cut Forest (RCF) on the single time series consisting of the full year of data. — Random Cut Forest detects anomalous observations; it does not directly forecast future concentration values.

C. Use the Amazon SageMaker Linear Learner algorithm on the single time series consisting of the full year of data with a predictor_type of regressor. — Linear Learner in regression mode predicts a continuous target and provides a reasonable baseline for the small daily dataset, using lag/calendar features.

D. Use the Amazon SageMaker Linear Learner algorithm on the single time series consisting of the full year of data with a predictor_type of classifier. — Classification predicts discrete categories, whereas the requested output is a numeric concentration in parts per million.

text: A Data Engineer needs to build a model using a dataset containing customer credit card information How can the Data Engineer ensure the data remains encrypted and the credit card information is secure?

choices.A: Use a custom encryption algorithm to encrypt the data and store the data on an Amazon SageMaker instance in a VPC. Use the SageMaker DeepAR algorithm to randomize the credit card numbers.
choices.B: Use an IAM policy to encrypt the data on the Amazon S3 bucket and Amazon Kinesis to automatically discard credit card numbers and insert fake credit card numbers.
choices.C: Use an Amazon SageMaker launch configuration to encrypt the data once it is copied to the SageMaker instance in a VPC. Use the SageMaker principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm to reduce the length of the credit card numbers.
choices.D: Use AWS KMS to encrypt the data on Amazon S3 and Amazon SageMaker, and redact the credit card numbers from the customer data with AWS Glue.

explanation:
Key Concept: Encryption protects stored data, while redaction removes sensitive identifiers from the training dataset.

A. Use a custom encryption algorithm to encrypt the data and store the data on an Amazon SageMaker instance in a VPC. Use the SageMaker DeepAR algorithm to randomize the credit card numbers. — DeepAR forecasts time series; it does not anonymize credit card numbers. Custom encryption also adds unnecessary implementation risk and work.

B. Use an IAM policy to encrypt the data on the Amazon S3 bucket and Amazon Kinesis to automatically discard credit card numbers and insert fake credit card numbers. — IAM controls authorization rather than encrypting data. Kinesis does not automatically replace sensitive fields with fake values.

C. Use an Amazon SageMaker launch configuration to encrypt the data once it is copied to the SageMaker instance in a VPC. Use the SageMaker principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm to reduce the length of the credit card numbers. — PCA reduces feature dimensions; shortening an identifier does not securely redact it. A launch configuration is not the proposed data-protection mechanism.

D. Use AWS KMS to encrypt the data on Amazon S3 and Amazon SageMaker, and redact the credit card numbers from the customer data with AWS Glue. — KMS-backed encryption protects S3 and SageMaker storage, and a Glue transformation can detect and redact the credit card fields before training.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is using an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance in a private subnet of a corporate VPC. The ML Specialist has important data stored on the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance's Amazon EBS volume, and needs to take a snapshot of that EBS volume. However, the ML Specialist cannot find the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance's EBS volume or Amazon EC2 instance within the VPC. Why is the ML Specialist not seeing the instance visible in the VPC?

choices.A: Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on the EC2 instances within the customer account, but they run outside of VPCs.
choices.B: Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on the Amazon ECS service within customer accounts.
choices.C: Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on EC2 instances running within AWS service accounts.
choices.D: Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on AWS ECS instances running within AWS service accounts.

explanation:
Key Concept: Managed SageMaker notebook compute is hosted in a service account, with VPC connectivity provided through network interfaces.

A. Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on the EC2 instances within the customer account, but they run outside of VPCs. — The managed notebook's EC2 instance is not an EC2 resource owned by the customer account, so it is absent from that account's instance inventory.

B. Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on the Amazon ECS service within customer accounts. — A notebook instance is not an ECS service deployed into the customer's account.

C. Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on EC2 instances running within AWS service accounts. — Its EC2 compute and associated managed storage reside in a SageMaker service account; connecting it to a customer VPC does not transfer ownership.

D. Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are based on AWS ECS instances running within AWS service accounts. — The underlying notebook resource is EC2 compute, not an ECS instance running in the service account.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is building a model that will perform time series forecasting using Amazon SageMaker. The Specialist has finished training the model and is now planning to perform load testing on the endpoint so they can configure Auto Scaling for the model variant. Which approach will allow the Specialist to review the latency, memory utilization, and CPU utilization during the load test?

choices.A: Review SageMaker logs that have been written to Amazon S3 by leveraging Amazon Athena and Amazon QuickSight to visualize logs as they are being produced.
choices.B: Generate an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard to create a single view for the latency, memory utilization, and CPU utilization metrics that are outputted by Amazon SageMaker.
choices.C: Build custom Amazon CloudWatch Logs and then leverage Amazon ES and Kibana to query and visualize the log data as it is generated by Amazon SageMaker.
choices.D: Send Amazon CloudWatch Logs that were generated by Amazon SageMaker to Amazon ES and use Kibana to query and visualize the log data.

explanation:

A. Review SageMaker logs that have been written to Amazon S3 by leveraging Amazon Athena and Amazon QuickSight to visualize logs as they are being produced. — This assumes an S3 log export and additional analytics services, instead of using the endpoint metrics already published to CloudWatch.

B. Generate an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard to create a single view for the latency, memory utilization, and CPU utilization metrics that are outputted by Amazon SageMaker. — A CloudWatch dashboard can display ModelLatency, CPUUtilization, and MemoryUtilization together while the endpoint is under load.

C. Build custom Amazon CloudWatch Logs and then leverage Amazon ES and Kibana to query and visualize the log data as it is generated by Amazon SageMaker. — Custom log ingestion and an OpenSearch/Kibana stack add unnecessary work for metrics that SageMaker already emits.

D. Send Amazon CloudWatch Logs that were generated by Amazon SageMaker to Amazon ES and use Kibana to query and visualize the log data. — CloudWatch Logs contain log events, not automatically the endpoint's utilization metric series. Forwarding logs does not replace the metric dashboard.

text: A manufacturing company has structured and unstructured data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A Machine Learning Specialist wants to use SQL to run queries on this data. Which solution requires the LEAST effort to be able to query this data?

choices.A: Use AWS Data Pipeline to transform the data and Amazon RDS to run queries.
choices.B: Use AWS Glue to catalogue the data and Amazon Athena to run queries.
choices.C: Use AWS Batch to run ETL on the data and Amazon Aurora to run the queries.
choices.D: Use AWS Lambda to transform the data and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to run queries.

explanation:
Key Concept: Athena queries supported data formats in S3 using table metadata from the Glue Data Catalog.

A. Use AWS Data Pipeline to transform the data and Amazon RDS to run queries. — Transforming and loading the data into RDS adds an ETL pipeline and a database when the data can be queried in S3.

B. Use AWS Glue to catalogue the data and Amazon Athena to run queries. — Glue supplies schemas and table metadata; Athena executes SQL against the S3 data without provisioning a database or query cluster.

C. Use AWS Batch to run ETL on the data and Amazon Aurora to run the queries. — Batch processing plus an Aurora database adds compute orchestration and a separate data-loading step.

D. Use AWS Lambda to transform the data and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to run queries. — Kinesis Data Analytics targets streaming analytics; it is not the simplest query service for an existing S3 dataset.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is developing a custom video recommendation model for an application. The dataset used to train this model is very large with millions of data points and is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket. The Specialist wants to avoid loading all of this data onto an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance because it would take hours to move and will exceed the attached 5 GB Amazon EBS volume on the notebook instance. Which approach allows the Specialist to use all the data to train the model?

choices.A: Load a smaller subset of the data into the SageMaker notebook and train locally. Confirm that the training code is executing and the model parameters seem reasonable. Initiate a SageMaker training job using the full dataset from the S3 bucket using Pipe input mode.
choices.B: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance with an AWS Deep Learning AMI and attach the S3 bucket to the instance. Train on a small amount of the data to verify the training code and hyperparameters. Go back to Amazon SageMaker and train using the full dataset
choices.C: Use AWS Glue to train a model using a small subset of the data to confirm that the data will be compatible with Amazon SageMaker. Initiate a SageMaker training job using the full dataset from the S3 bucket using Pipe input mode.
choices.D: Load a smaller subset of the data into the SageMaker notebook and train locally. Confirm that the training code is executing and the model parameters seem reasonable. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance with an AWS Deep Learning AMI and attach the S3 bucket to train the full dataset.

explanation:
Key Concept: A managed training job reads its own training input; a notebook does not need to hold the full dataset.

A. Load a smaller subset of the data into the SageMaker notebook and train locally. Confirm that the training code is executing and the model parameters seem reasonable. Initiate a SageMaker training job using the full dataset from the S3 bucket using Pipe input mode. — Test the code locally on a sample, then launch a separate training job with Pipe mode to stream the full S3 dataset.

B. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance with an AWS Deep Learning AMI and attach the S3 bucket to the instance. Train on a small amount of the data to verify the training code and hyperparameters. Go back to Amazon SageMaker and train using the full dataset — An S3 bucket is not an EBS volume that can simply be attached to EC2. This also adds an unnecessary intermediate training environment.

C. Use AWS Glue to train a model using a small subset of the data to confirm that the data will be compatible with Amazon SageMaker. Initiate a SageMaker training job using the full dataset from the S3 bucket using Pipe input mode. — Glue is an ETL service, not the proposed custom-model training environment. The sample should validate the actual training code.

D. Load a smaller subset of the data into the SageMaker notebook and train locally. Confirm that the training code is executing and the model parameters seem reasonable. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance with an AWS Deep Learning AMI and attach the S3 bucket to train the full dataset. — Moving full training to self-managed EC2 adds infrastructure work and again assumes that an S3 bucket can be attached like a disk.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist has completed a proof of concept for a company using a small data sample, and now the Specialist is ready to implement an end- to-end solution in AWS using Amazon SageMaker. The historical training data is stored in Amazon RDS. Which approach should the Specialist use for training a model using that data?

choices.A: Write a direct connection to the SQL database within the notebook and pull data in
choices.B: Push the data from Microsoft SQL Server to Amazon S3 using an AWS Data Pipeline and provide the S3 location within the notebook.
choices.C: Move the data to Amazon DynamoDB and set up a connection to DynamoDB within the notebook to pull data in.
choices.D: Move the data to Amazon ElastiCache using AWS DMS and set up a connection within the notebook to pull data in for fast access.

explanation:

A. Write a direct connection to the SQL database within the notebook and pull data in — A notebook SQL connection can retrieve a sample, but this option does not establish the repeatable RDS-to-S3 training data pipeline requested.

B. Push the data from Microsoft SQL Server to Amazon S3 using an AWS Data Pipeline and provide the S3 location within the notebook. — In the historical architecture described by the question, Data Pipeline copies RDS data to S3, which supplies the managed training job's input.

C. Move the data to Amazon DynamoDB and set up a connection to DynamoDB within the notebook to pull data in. — Moving relational training records to DynamoDB adds migration work and does not provide the intended S3 training input.

D. Move the data to Amazon ElastiCache using AWS DMS and set up a connection within the notebook to pull data in for fast access. — ElastiCache is a cache, not a durable training-data destination for this proposed DMS workflow. The extra migration does not solve the requirement.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist receives customer data for an online shopping website. The data includes demographics, past visits, and locality information. The Specialist must develop a machine learning approach to identify the customer shopping patterns, preferences, and trends to enhance the website for better service and smart recommendations. Which solution should the Specialist recommend?

choices.A: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for the given collection of discrete data to identify patterns in the customer database.
choices.B: A neural network with a minimum of three layers and random initial weights to identify patterns in the customer database.
choices.C: Collaborative filtering based on user interactions and correlations to identify patterns in the customer database.
choices.D: Random Cut Forest (RCF) over random subsamples to identify patterns in the customer database.

explanation:
Key Concept: Recommendation systems can learn customer preferences from patterns of shared user–item interactions.

A. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for the given collection of discrete data to identify patterns in the customer database. — LDA discovers latent topics in documents; it is not the direct approach for recommendations from customer interaction histories.

B. A neural network with a minimum of three layers and random initial weights to identify patterns in the customer database. — An arbitrary layer count and initialization do not define a recommendation strategy or connect the network to the required user–item relationships.

C. Collaborative filtering based on user interactions and correlations to identify patterns in the customer database. — Collaborative filtering uses correlations in customer interactions to recommend products that similar users prefer.

D. Random Cut Forest (RCF) over random subsamples to identify patterns in the customer database. — Random Cut Forest identifies anomalous observations, rather than learning personalized item recommendations.

explanation:

A. The model predicts both the trend and the seasonality well — Both curves rise over time and show aligned recurring peaks and dips. The forecast still has a level offset, so this does not imply accurate absolute values.

B. The model predicts the trend well, but not the seasonality. — The forecast's recurring peaks and dips follow the observed pattern, so seasonality is represented as well as trend.

choices.B: Logistic regression
choices.C: Support vector machine (SVM) with non-linear kernel
choices.D: Single perceptron with tanh activation function

explanation:
Key Concept: A nonlinear decision boundary is needed when one class occupies the center and the other surrounds it.

A. Long short-term memory (LSTM) model with scaled exponential linear unit (SELU) — The plot describes two tabular features, not a sequence. An LSTM with SELU is not the direct solution to the circular separation.

B. Logistic regression — Ordinary logistic regression on these two original features produces a linear boundary, which cannot isolate the central circular class.

C. Support vector machine (SVM) with non-linear kernel — An SVM with a nonlinear kernel, such as RBF, can learn a curved boundary around the central class shown in the plot.

D. Single perceptron with tanh activation function — A single perceptron's decision boundary remains linear in its inputs, even with tanh activation; it cannot represent the circular separation.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist at a company sensitive to security is preparing a dataset for model training. The dataset is stored in Amazon S3 and contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII). The dataset: • Must be accessible from a VPC only. • Must not traverse the public internet. How can these requirements be satisfied?

choices.A: Create a VPC endpoint and apply a bucket access policy that restricts access to the given VPC endpoint and the VPC.
choices.B: Create a VPC endpoint and apply a bucket access policy that allows access from the given VPC endpoint and an Amazon EC2 instance.
choices.C: Create a VPC endpoint and use Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) to allow traffic between only the given VPC endpoint and an Amazon EC2 instance.
choices.D: Create a VPC endpoint and use security groups to restrict access to the given VPC endpoint and an Amazon EC2 instance

explanation:
Key Concept: A private network route and an S3 bucket policy are both needed to restrict where object access originates.

A. Create a VPC endpoint and apply a bucket access policy that restricts access to the given VPC endpoint and the VPC. — The VPC endpoint provides private S3 connectivity, while a bucket policy using SourceVpce or SourceVpc can deny requests from other paths.

B. Create a VPC endpoint and apply a bucket access policy that allows access from the given VPC endpoint and an Amazon EC2 instance. — An allow statement for one endpoint or EC2 caller does not by itself enforce the requirement that all other access paths be denied.

C. Create a VPC endpoint and use Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) to allow traffic between only the given VPC endpoint and an Amazon EC2 instance. — NACLs filter subnet traffic; they do not enforce an S3 bucket-wide restriction against access from outside the designated VPC.

D. Create a VPC endpoint and use security groups to restrict access to the given VPC endpoint and an Amazon EC2 instance — Security groups control attached network interfaces, not all access to the S3 bucket. The bucket policy restriction is still missing.

text: During mini-batch training of a neural network for a classification problem, a Data Scientist notices that training accuracy oscillates. What is the MOST likely cause of this issue?

choices.A: The class distribution in the dataset is imbalanced.
choices.B: Dataset shuffling is disabled.
choices.C: The batch size is too big.
choices.D: The learning rate is very high.

explanation:
Key Concept: The learning rate determines the size of gradient updates and can destabilize optimization when it is too large.

A. The class distribution in the dataset is imbalanced. — Class imbalance mainly affects class-wise learning and evaluation; it does not directly explain repeated overshooting during parameter updates.

B. Dataset shuffling is disabled. — Not shuffling can introduce ordered-batch effects, but excessive learning rate is the more direct cause of oscillatory optimization in this question.

C. The batch size is too big. — A larger batch usually reduces gradient noise. It is not the most likely explanation for the stated oscillation.

D. The learning rate is very high. — Large gradient steps can repeatedly jump across a useful region of the loss surface, causing unstable accuracy during mini-batch training.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is packaging a custom ResNet model into a Docker container so the company can leverage Amazon SageMaker for training. The Specialist is using Amazon EC2 P3 instances to train the model and needs to properly configure the Docker container to leverage the NVIDIA GPUs. What does the Specialist need to do?

choices.B: Build the Docker container to be NVIDIA-Docker compatible.
choices.C: Organize the Docker container's file structure to execute on GPU instances.
choices.D: Set the GPU flag in the Amazon SageMaker CreateTrainingJob request body.

explanation:

A. Bundle the NVIDIA drivers with the Docker image. — SageMaker provides the host drivers. Bundling a competing driver installation in the image is not the required GPU container configuration.

C. Organize the Docker container's file structure to execute on GPU instances. — Directory layout alone does not provide GPU runtime compatibility or access to NVIDIA devices.

D. Set the GPU flag in the Amazon SageMaker CreateTrainingJob request body. — CreateTrainingJob selects a GPU instance type; it does not expose a generic GPU flag that makes an incompatible container work.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is building a logistic regression model that will predict whether or not a person will order a pizza. The Specialist is trying to build the optimal model with an ideal classification threshold. What model evaluation technique should the Specialist use to understand how different classification thresholds will impact the model's performance?

choices.A: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve
choices.B: Misclassification rate
choices.C: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)
choices.D: L1 norm

explanation:
Key Concept: ROC curves show the trade-off between true-positive and false-positive rates across classification thresholds.

A. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve — Sweeping the threshold produces the ROC curve, allowing comparison of sensitivity and false-positive rate at different operating points.

B. Misclassification rate — A misclassification rate summarizes errors at one chosen threshold; it does not show the full threshold trade-off by itself.

C. Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) — RMSE measures numeric prediction error and is not the standard visualization of binary classification threshold behavior.

D. L1 norm — The L1 norm is a vector magnitude or regularization term, not an evaluation curve across classification thresholds.

text: An interactive online dictionary wants to add a widget that displays words used in similar contexts. A Machine Learning Specialist is asked to provide word features for the downstream nearest neighbor model powering the widget. What should the Specialist do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create one-hot word encoding vectors.
choices.B: Produce a set of synonyms for every word using Amazon Mechanical Turk.
choices.C: Create word embedding vectors that store edit distance with every other word.
choices.D: Download word embeddings pre-trained on a large corpus.

explanation:
Key Concept: Word embeddings encode distributional context in a vector space suitable for semantic nearest-neighbor search.

A. Create one-hot word encoding vectors. — One-hot vectors give distinct words orthogonal representations and do not encode contextual similarity.

B. Produce a set of synonyms for every word using Amazon Mechanical Turk. — A manually collected synonym list does not supply the required continuous vector features and needs substantial labeling effort.

C. Create word embedding vectors that store edit distance with every other word. — Edit distance measures spelling changes, not semantic context. An embedding is not a table of edit distances to all words.

D. Download word embeddings pre-trained on a large corpus. — Pretrained embeddings already capture relationships learned from a large corpus and can directly supply vectors to the nearest-neighbor model.

text: A retail chain has been ingesting purchasing records from its network of 20,000 stores to Amazon S3 using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. To support training an improved machine learning model, training records will require new but simple transformations, and some attributes will be combined. The model needs to be retrained daily. Given the large number of stores and the legacy data ingestion, which change will require the LEAST amount of development effort?

choices.A: Require that the stores to switch to capturing their data locally on AWS Storage Gateway for loading into Amazon S3, then use AWS Glue to do the transformation.
choices.B: Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster running Apache Spark with the transformation logic, and have the cluster run each day on the accumulating records in Amazon S3, outputting new/transformed records to Amazon S3.
choices.C: Spin up a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances with the transformation logic, have them transform the data records accumulating on Amazon S3, and output the transformed records to Amazon S3.

Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster running Apache Spark with the transformation logic, and have the cluster run each day on the accumulating records in Amazon S3, outputting new/transformed records to Amazon S3. — An EMR Spark job can transform the data, but adds cluster and application management for simple transformations.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is building a convolutional neural network (CNN) that will classify 10 types of animals. The Specialist has built a series of layers in a neural network that will take an input image of an animal, pass it through a series of convolutional and pooling layers, and then finally pass it through a dense and fully connected layer with 10 nodes. The Specialist would like to get an output from the neural network that is a probability distribution of how likely it is that the input image belongs to each of the 10 classes. Which function will produce the desired output?

choices.A: Dropout
choices.B: Smooth L1 loss
choices.C: Softmax
choices.D: Rectified linear units (ReLU)

explanation:
Key Concept: Softmax converts multiclass logits into nonnegative values that sum to one.

A. Dropout — Dropout randomly disables activations during training to reduce overfitting; it does not create the output probability distribution.

B. Smooth L1 loss — Smooth L1 is a loss function for numeric errors, not a multiclass output normalization function.

C. Softmax — Applying softmax to the 10 output logits produces a normalized probability distribution over the 10 animal classes.

D. Rectified linear units (ReLU) — ReLU clips negative activations but does not normalize the 10 outputs to sum to one.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist trained a regression model, but the first iteration needs optimizing. The Specialist needs to understand whether the model is more frequently overestimating or underestimating the target. choices.B: Residual plots
choices.C: Area under the curve
choices.D: Confusion matrix

explanation:
Key Concept: Residuals retain the direction of prediction error; aggregate squared-error metrics discard that sign.

A. Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) — RMSE squares residuals, so equally large overestimates and underestimates contribute identically.

B. Residual plots — A residual plot shows positive and negative errors. With residual defined as actual minus predicted, negative residuals indicate overestimation.

C. Area under the curve — AUC evaluates ranking or classification performance and does not reveal the sign of regression errors.

D. Confusion matrix — A confusion matrix summarizes discrete classification outcomes, not continuous target overestimation and underestimation.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is creating a new natural language processing application that processes a dataset comprised of 1 million sentences. The aim is to then run Word2Vec to generate embeddings of the sentences and enable different types of predictions. Here is an example from the dataset: "The quck BROWN FOX jumps over the lazy dog.` Which of the following are the operations the Specialist needs to perform to correctly sanitize and prepare the data in a repeatable manner? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Perform part-of-speech tagging and keep the action verb and the nouns only.
choices.B: Normalize all words by making the sentence lowercase.
choices.C: Remove stop words using an English stopword dictionary.
choices.D: Correct the typography on "quck" to "quick."
choices.E: One-hot encode all words in the sentence.
choices.F: Tokenize the sentence into words.

explanation:
Key Concept: Repeatable token normalization reduces inconsistent vocabulary representations before word-embedding training.

A. Perform part-of-speech tagging and keep the action verb and the nouns only. — Keeping only verbs and nouns discards much of the context that a word-embedding model learns from; it is not a required preparation step.

B. Normalize all words by making the sentence lowercase. — Lowercasing merges capitalization variants such as BROWN and brown into the same vocabulary item when case is not informative.

C. Remove stop words using an English stopword dictionary. — A fixed stopword dictionary provides a repeatable filtering rule. Its use should still depend on whether those words matter to the downstream task.

D. Correct the typography on "quck" to "quick." — Fixing this one typo manually does not define a repeatable operation over a million sentences. A validated automated spelling policy could be useful, but is not specified.

E. One-hot encode all words in the sentence. — Word2Vec learns dense vectors from tokens and context. Explicit one-hot vectors are not the requested text-cleaning step.

F. Tokenize the sentence into words. — Tokenization converts each sentence into the word units needed to build the vocabulary and context windows for Word2Vec.

text: A company is using Amazon Polly to translate plaintext documents to speech for automated company announcements. However, company acronyms are being mispronounced in the current documents. How should a Machine Learning Specialist address this issue for future documents?

choices.A: Convert current documents to SSML with pronunciation tags.
choices.B: Create an appropriate pronunciation lexicon.
choices.C: Output speech marks to guide in pronunciation.
choices.D: Use Amazon Lex to preprocess the text files for pronunciation

explanation:
Key Concept: A Polly pronunciation lexicon defines reusable pronunciations or substitutions for specific words and acronyms.

A. Convert current documents to SSML with pronunciation tags. — SSML can fix individual documents, but editing current documents does not create a reusable acronym pronunciation resource for future input.

B. Create an appropriate pronunciation lexicon. — A pronunciation lexicon applies consistent acronym handling whenever it is selected during synthesis, avoiding repeated edits to future documents.

C. Output speech marks to guide in pronunciation. — Speech marks describe timing and alignment in synthesized speech; they do not specify how an acronym should be pronounced.

D. Use Amazon Lex to preprocess the text files for pronunciation — Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces and is not the pronunciation customization mechanism for Polly.

text: An insurance company is developing a new device for vehicles that uses a camera to observe drivers' behavior and alert them when they appear distracted. The company created approximately 10,000 training images in a controlled environment that a Machine Learning Specialist will use to train and evaluate machine learning models. During the model evaluation, the Specialist notices that the training error rate diminishes faster as the number of epochs increases and the model is not accurately inferring on the unseen test images. Which of the following should be used to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Add vanishing gradient to the model.
choices.B: Perform data augmentation on the training data.
choices.C: Make the neural network architecture complex.
choices.D: Use gradient checking in the model.
choices.E: Add L2 regularization to the model.

explanation:
Key Concept: A widening training–test performance gap indicates overfitting; increase data diversity or regularize the model.

A. Add vanishing gradient to the model. — Vanishing gradients are an optimization problem, not a technique to add for better generalization.

B. Perform data augmentation on the training data. — Appropriate image augmentation exposes the model to varied views and conditions, reducing dependence on the controlled training setup.

C. Make the neural network architecture complex. — Increasing model complexity can make memorization easier and worsen the existing generalization gap.

D. Use gradient checking in the model. — Gradient checking validates derivative calculations; it does not directly regularize a correctly implemented model.

E. Add L2 regularization to the model. — L2 penalizes large weights, limiting overly complex fits and helping the model generalize to unseen driver images.

text: When submitting Amazon SageMaker training jobs using one of the built-in algorithms, which common parameters MUST be specified? (Choose three.)

choices.A: The training channel identifying the location of training data on an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.B: The validation channel identifying the location of validation data on an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.C: The IAM role that Amazon SageMaker can assume to perform tasks on behalf of the users.
choices.D: Hyperparameters in a JSON array as documented for the algorithm used.
choices.E: The Amazon EC2 instance class specifying whether training will be run using CPU or GPU.
choices.F: The output path specifying where on an Amazon S3 bucket the trained model will persist.

explanation:
Key Concept: CreateTrainingJob requires execution, compute, and output settings; algorithm-specific input requirements make the requested three-answer key incomplete.

A. The training channel identifying the location of training data on an Amazon S3 bucket. — Built-in supervised training normally needs a training-data channel. This is one plausible requirement, contributing to the ambiguity of selecting only three.

B. The validation channel identifying the location of validation data on an Amazon S3 bucket. — A validation channel is optional for many algorithms and jobs; it is not a universal requirement.

C. The IAM role that Amazon SageMaker can assume to perform tasks on behalf of the users. — RoleArn supplies the execution role assumed by SageMaker. It is a required training-job API parameter.

D. Hyperparameters in a JSON array as documented for the algorithm used. — Hyperparameter requirements vary by algorithm, and the API represents them as a string map, not the universal JSON array described here.

E. The Amazon EC2 instance class specifying whether training will be run using CPU or GPU. — A training job needs ResourceConfig, including the instance type and count. This is another required setting beyond the proposed three-answer limit.

F. The output path specifying where on an Amazon S3 bucket the trained model will persist. — OutputDataConfig specifies the model artifact output location. Together with input, role, and compute settings, it makes the question's fixed count problematic.

text: A monitoring service generates 1 TB of scale metrics record data every minute. A Research team performs queries on this data using Amazon Athena. The queries run slowly due to the large volume of data, and the team requires better performance. How should the records be stored in Amazon S3 to improve query performance?

choices.A: CSV files
choices.B: Parquet files
choices.C: Compressed JSON
choices.D: RecordIO

explanation:
Key Concept: Columnar storage reduces bytes scanned when analytical queries read only a subset of columns.

A. CSV files — CSV is row-oriented text, so Athena generally reads and parses more data than with a suitable columnar format.

B. Parquet files — Parquet stores columns separately and supports compression and metadata-based pruning, reducing I/O for Athena analytical queries.

C. Compressed JSON — Compression shrinks JSON but does not give it Parquet's columnar access and pruning advantages.

D. RecordIO — RecordIO is a record-oriented training format, not the appropriate columnar storage format for Athena SQL analytics.

text: Machine Learning Specialist is working with a media company to perform classification on popular articles from the company's website. The company is using random forests to classify how popular an article will be before it is published. A sample of the data being used is below. choices.D: Normalization transformation

explanation:
Key Concept: One-hot encoding represents each category with a separate binary indicator column.

B. One-hot encoding — Create one indicator for each weekday, setting that day's value to 1 and the others to 0.

C. Tokenization — Tokenization splits text into units; it does not generate the requested binary categorical feature columns.

text: A gaming company has launched an online game where people can start playing for free, but they need to pay if they choose to use certain features. The company needs to build an automated system to predict whether or not a new user will become a paid user within 1 year. The company has gathered a labeled dataset from 1 million users. The training dataset consists of 1,000 positive samples (from users who ended up paying within 1 year) and 999,000 negative samples (from users who did not use any paid features). Each data sample consists of 200 features including user age, device, location, and play patterns. Using this dataset for training, the Data Science team trained a random forest model that converged with over 99% accuracy on the training set. However, the prediction results on a test dataset were not satisfactory Which of the following approaches should the Data Science team take to mitigate this issue? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Add more deep trees to the random forest to enable the model to learn more features.
choices.B: Include a copy of the samples in the test dataset in the training dataset.
choices.C: Generate more positive samples by duplicating the positive samples and adding a small amount of noise to the duplicated data.
choices.D: Change the cost function so that false negatives have a higher impact on the cost value than false positives.
choices.E: Change the cost function so that false positives have a higher impact on the cost value than false negatives.

explanation:
Key Concept: Extreme class imbalance can produce high accuracy even when the model misses nearly every positive example.

A. Add more deep trees to the random forest to enable the model to learn more features. — Deeper trees add capacity but do not correct the minority class's tiny contribution to training and may increase overfitting.

B. Include a copy of the samples in the test dataset in the training dataset. — Copying test data into training causes leakage and destroys the validity of the held-out evaluation.

C. Generate more positive samples by duplicating the positive samples and adding a small amount of noise to the duplicated data. — Oversampling the positive class increases its training representation; any added noise must preserve valid feature values and avoid contaminating the test set.

D. Change the cost function so that false negatives have a higher impact on the cost value than false positives. — Increasing the false-negative penalty makes missed future paying users more costly, encouraging the model to learn the rare positive class.

E. Change the cost function so that false positives have a higher impact on the cost value than false negatives. — Penalizing false positives more strongly encourages conservative positive predictions, usually worsening the failure to detect the minority class.

text: A Data Scientist is developing a machine learning model to predict future patient outcomes based on information collected about each patient and their treatment plans. The model should output a continuous value as its prediction. The data available includes labeled outcomes for a set of 4,000 patients. The study was conducted on a group of individuals over the age of 65 who have a particular disease that is known to worsen with age. Initial models have performed poorly. While reviewing the underlying data, the Data Scientist notices that, out of 4,000 patient observations, there are 450 where the patient age has been input as 0. The other features for these observations appear normal compared to the rest of the sample population How should the Data Scientist correct this issue?

choices.A: Drop all records from the dataset where age has been set to 0.
choices.B: Replace the age field value for records with a value of 0 with the mean or median value from the dataset
choices.C: Drop the age feature from the dataset and train the model using the rest of the features.
choices.D: Use k-means clustering to handle missing features

explanation:
Key Concept: Invalid placeholder values should be treated as missing data and imputed using valid training observations.

A. Drop all records from the dataset where age has been set to 0. — Dropping 450 otherwise useful records discards more than 11% of the dataset and is unnecessary when only age is invalid.

B. Replace the age field value for records with a value of 0 with the mean or median value from the dataset — Replace zero ages with a mean or median calculated from valid ages in the training split, preserving the other useful information in those records.

C. Drop the age feature from the dataset and train the model using the rest of the features. — Age is relevant because the disease worsens with age; removing the entire feature loses signal from all 4,000 patients.

D. Use k-means clustering to handle missing features — k-means is a clustering algorithm, not a complete missing-value treatment by itself; it also requires a suitable numeric representation to run.

text: A Data Science team is designing a dataset repository where it will store a large amount of training data commonly used in its machine learning models. As Data Scientists may create an arbitrary number of new datasets every day, the solution has to scale automatically and be cost-effective. Also, it must be possible to explore the data using SQL. Which storage scheme is MOST adapted to this scenario?

choices.A: Store datasets as files in Amazon S3.
choices.B: Store datasets as files in an Amazon EBS volume attached to an Amazon EC2 instance.
choices.C: Store datasets as tables in a multi-node Amazon Redshift cluster.
choices.D: Store datasets as global tables in Amazon DynamoDB.

explanation:
Key Concept: S3 provides scalable dataset storage, while Athena supplies SQL access over cataloged files.

A. Store datasets as files in Amazon S3. — An S3 data lake accommodates many datasets without managing database capacity; Glue metadata and Athena make those files queryable with SQL.

B. Store datasets as files in an Amazon EBS volume attached to an Amazon EC2 instance. — EBS is attached block storage with provisioned capacity and an EC2 dependency, adding management and scaling work.

C. Store datasets as tables in a multi-node Amazon Redshift cluster. — A provisioned Redshift cluster adds warehouse capacity and loading management when the requirement is a flexible, inexpensive dataset repository.

D. Store datasets as global tables in Amazon DynamoDB. — DynamoDB global tables target replicated key-value access; they are not the natural storage layer for arbitrary analytical training datasets.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist deployed a model that provides product recommendations on a company's website. Initially, the model was performing very well and resulted in customers buying more products on average. However, within the past few months, the Specialist has noticed that the effect of product recommendations has diminished and customers are starting to return to their original habits of spending less. The Specialist is unsure of what happened, as the model has not changed from its initial deployment over a year ago. Which method should the Specialist try to improve model performance?

choices.A: The model needs to be completely re-engineered because it is unable to handle product inventory changes.
choices.B: The model's hyperparameters should be periodically updated to prevent drift.
choices.C: The model should be periodically retrained from scratch using the original data while adding a regularization term to handle product inventory changes
choices.D: The model should be periodically retrained using the original training data plus new data as product inventory changes.

explanation:
Key Concept: A model trained on stale observations can lose relevance as products and user behavior change.

A. The model needs to be completely re-engineered because it is unable to handle product inventory changes. — A performance decline does not establish that the architecture must be replaced; stale training data should be investigated first.

B. The model's hyperparameters should be periodically updated to prevent drift. — Changing hyperparameters without incorporating new observations does not teach the model about new products or preferences.

C. The model should be periodically retrained from scratch using the original data while adding a regularization term to handle product inventory changes — Retraining only on the original dataset preserves the same stale information, even if regularization changes.

D. The model should be periodically retrained using the original training data plus new data as product inventory changes. — Adding recent interactions and inventory data allows retraining to reflect current behavior, followed by validation before deploying the updated model.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist working for an online fashion company wants to build a data ingestion solution for the company's Amazon S3-based data lake. The Specialist wants to create a set of ingestion mechanisms that will enable future capabilities comprised of: • Real-time analytics • Interactive analytics of historical data • Clickstream analytics • Product recommendations Which services should the Specialist use?

choices.A: AWS Glue as the data catalog; Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for real-time data insights; Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for delivery to Amazon ES for clickstream analytics; Amazon EMR to generate personalized product recommendations
choices.B: Amazon Athena as the data catalog: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for near-real-time data insights; Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for clickstream analytics; AWS Glue to generate personalized product recommendations

choices.D: Amazon Athena as the data catalog; Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for historical data insights; Amazon DynamoDB streams for clickstream analytics; AWS Glue to generate personalized product recommendations

explanation:

A. AWS Glue as the data catalog; Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for real-time data insights; Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for delivery to Amazon ES for clickstream analytics; Amazon EMR to generate personalized product recommendations — In the historical architecture, Glue supplies catalog metadata, Kinesis processes live events, Firehose delivers to Elasticsearch, and EMR runs recommendation workloads.

B. Amazon Athena as the data catalog: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for near-real-time data insights; Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for clickstream analytics; AWS Glue to generate personalized product recommendations — Athena is a query engine rather than the catalog itself, and Glue alone is not the stated personalized recommendation engine.

C. AWS Glue as the data catalog; Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for historical data insights; Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose for delivery to Amazon ES for clickstream analytics; Amazon EMR to generate personalized product recommendations — Kinesis streaming analytics addresses incoming data; assigning it the role of querying historical S3 datasets misplaces that responsibility.

D. Amazon Athena as the data catalog; Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for historical data insights; Amazon DynamoDB streams for clickstream analytics; AWS Glue to generate personalized product recommendations — Athena is not the catalog, DynamoDB Streams captures DynamoDB table changes, and Glue does not by itself produce the proposed recommendations.

text: A company is observing low accuracy while training on the default built-in image classification algorithm in Amazon SageMaker. The Data Science team wants to use an Inception neural network architecture instead of a ResNet architecture. Which of the following will accomplish this? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Customize the built-in image classification algorithm to use Inception and use this for model training.
choices.B: Create a support case with the SageMaker team to change the default image classification algorithm to Inception.
choices.C: Bundle a Docker container with TensorFlow Estimator loaded with an Inception network and use this for model training.
choices.D: Use custom code in Amazon SageMaker with TensorFlow Estimator to load the model with an Inception network, and use this for model training.
choices.E: Download and apt-get install the inception network code into an Amazon EC2 instance and use this instance as a Jupyter notebook in Amazon SageMaker.

explanation:
Key Concept: SageMaker framework scripts and custom containers allow an architecture that differs from a fixed built-in algorithm.

A. Customize the built-in image classification algorithm to use Inception and use this for model training. — The built-in algorithm's supported architecture cannot simply be replaced with Inception through its normal configuration.

B. Create a support case with the SageMaker team to change the default image classification algorithm to Inception. — An AWS Support request does not make a customer's chosen architecture the built-in service default.

C. Bundle a Docker container with TensorFlow Estimator loaded with an Inception network and use this for model training. — A compatible custom TensorFlow container can package and train the required Inception architecture on SageMaker.

D. Use custom code in Amazon SageMaker with TensorFlow Estimator to load the model with an Inception network, and use this for model training. — A TensorFlow Estimator can run a custom training script that constructs or loads Inception, avoiding the built-in ResNet restriction.

E. Download and apt-get install the inception network code into an Amazon EC2 instance and use this instance as a Jupyter notebook in Amazon SageMaker. — Installing code on a separate EC2 machine does not turn that instance into a SageMaker managed notebook or configure a managed Inception training job.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist built an image classification deep learning model. However, the Specialist ran into an overfitting problem in which the training and testing accuracies were 99% and 75%, respectively. How should the Specialist address this issue and what is the reason behind it?

choices.A: The learning rate should be increased because the optimization process was trapped at a local minimum.
choices.B: The dropout rate at the flatten layer should be increased because the model is not generalized enough.
choices.C: The dimensionality of dense layer next to the flatten layer should be increased because the model is not complex enough.
choices.D: The epoch number should be increased because the optimization process was terminated before it reached the global minimum.

explanation:
Key Concept: High training accuracy with much lower test accuracy indicates that the model is not generalizing well.

A. The learning rate should be increased because the optimization process was trapped at a local minimum. — Increasing the learning rate targets optimization behavior, not the demonstrated overfitting gap, and can make training unstable.

B. The dropout rate at the flatten layer should be increased because the model is not generalized enough. — More dropout randomly removes activations during training, discouraging co-adaptation and providing regularization against memorization.

C. The dimensionality of dense layer next to the flatten layer should be increased because the model is not complex enough. — Increasing the dense layer's size adds parameters and can worsen overfitting when training accuracy is already very high.

D. The epoch number should be increased because the optimization process was terminated before it reached the global minimum. — Training for more epochs can further memorize the training set; it does not directly resolve poor test performance.

text: A Machine Learning team uses Amazon SageMaker to train an Apache MXNet handwritten digit classifier model using a research dataset. The team wants to receive a notification when the model is overfitting. Auditors want to view the Amazon SageMaker log activity report to ensure there are no unauthorized API calls. What should the Machine Learning team do to address the requirements with the least amount of code and fewest steps?

choices.A: Implement an AWS Lambda function to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to Amazon S3. Add code to push a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Create an alarm in CloudWatch with Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting.
choices.B: Use AWS CloudTrail to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to Amazon S3. Add code to push a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Create an alarm in CloudWatch with Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting.
choices.C: Implement an AWS Lambda function to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to AWS CloudTrail. Add code to push a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Create an alarm in CloudWatch with Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting.
choices.D: Use AWS CloudTrail to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to Amazon S3. Set up Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting

explanation:
Key Concept: Audit logging and model-quality alerting require separate telemetry and notification mechanisms.

A. Implement an AWS Lambda function to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to Amazon S3. Add code to push a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Create an alarm in CloudWatch with Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting. — CloudTrail already captures SageMaker API activity, so implementing a Lambda-based audit logger adds unnecessary code.

B. Use AWS CloudTrail to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to Amazon S3. Add code to push a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Create an alarm in CloudWatch with Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting. — CloudTrail supplies the API audit trail; a custom overfitting metric, CloudWatch alarm, and SNS notification provide the requested training alert.

C. Implement an AWS Lambda function to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to AWS CloudTrail. Add code to push a custom metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Create an alarm in CloudWatch with Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting. — A Lambda function is unnecessary for recording supported SageMaker API events in CloudTrail and adds steps without improving this workflow.

D. Use AWS CloudTrail to log Amazon SageMaker API calls to Amazon S3. Set up Amazon SNS to receive a notification when the model is overfitting — SNS can deliver a message, but it does not detect overfitting by itself. This option omits the metric and alarm or equivalent detection logic.

choices.C: Create a new feature space using principal component analysis (PCA)
choices.D: Apply the Pearson correlation coefficient.

explanation:
Key Concept: Correlated predictors can destabilize linear-model coefficients; PCA creates orthogonal components in a reduced feature space.

A. Perform one-hot encoding on highly correlated features. — One-hot encoding represents categories and can add columns; it does not remove correlation among existing numeric features.

B. Use matrix multiplication on highly correlated features. — Unspecified matrix multiplication does not guarantee decorrelation or a useful lower-dimensional representation.

C. Create a new feature space using principal component analysis (PCA) — PCA projects the data onto orthogonal directions, allowing redundant dimensions to be removed before fitting the linear model.

D. Apply the Pearson correlation coefficient. — Pearson correlation measures relationships but does not itself transform or remove the correlated predictors.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is implementing a full Bayesian network on a dataset that describes public transit in New York City. One of the random variables is discrete, and represents the number of minutes New Yorkers wait for a bus given that the buses cycle every 10 minutes, with a mean of 3 minutes. Which prior probability distribution should the ML Specialist use for this variable?

choices.A: Poisson distribution
choices.B: Uniform distribution
choices.C: Normal distribution
choices.D: Binomial distribution

explanation:
Key Concept: A prior distribution must match the variable's support and the assumptions about the process generating it.

A. Poisson distribution — Poisson models nonnegative event counts with unbounded support. Calling elapsed waiting minutes discrete does not establish a Poisson process.

B. Uniform distribution — Uniform waiting on a regular 10-minute interval would require uniformly timed arrivals and would have mean 5, conflicting with the stated mean 3.

C. Normal distribution — An ordinary normal distribution allows negative and arbitrarily large waits and does not match a bounded discrete waiting variable without modifications.

D. Binomial distribution — A binomial distribution requires a fixed number of Bernoulli trials and a success probability. Those assumptions are absent, so no unique prior is determined.

text: A Data Science team within a large company uses Amazon SageMaker notebooks to access data stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The IT Security team is concerned that internet-enabled notebook instances create a security vulnerability where malicious code running on the instances could compromise data privacy. The company mandates that all instances stay within a secured VPC with no internet access, and data communication traffic must stay within the AWS network. How should the Data Science team configure the notebook instance placement to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Place the Amazon SageMaker endpoint and S3 buckets within the same VPC.
choices.B: Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Use IAM policies to grant access to Amazon S3 and Amazon SageMaker.
choices.C: Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Ensure the VPC has S3 VPC endpoints and Amazon SageMaker VPC endpoints attached to it.
choices.D: Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Ensure the VPC has a NAT gateway and an associated security group allowing only outbound connections to Amazon S3 and Amazon SageMaker.

explanation:
Key Concept: Private subnets require private service endpoints when internet egress is disabled.

A. Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Place the Amazon SageMaker endpoint and S3 buckets within the same VPC. — An S3 bucket is not placed inside a VPC. A private subnet alone does not provide private connectivity to the S3 and SageMaker APIs.

B. Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Use IAM policies to grant access to Amazon S3 and Amazon SageMaker. — IAM authorization does not create a network route to S3 or SageMaker services.

C. Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Ensure the VPC has S3 VPC endpoints and Amazon SageMaker VPC endpoints attached to it. — S3 and SageMaker VPC endpoints provide private service access. Direct internet access must also be disabled to satisfy the stated isolation policy.

D. Associate the Amazon SageMaker notebook with a private subnet in a VPC. Ensure the VPC has a NAT gateway and an associated security group allowing only outbound connections to Amazon S3 and Amazon SageMaker. — A NAT gateway provides outbound internet connectivity, contradicting the no-internet requirement; security groups do not attach directly to NAT gateways.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist has created a deep learning neural network model that performs well on the training data but performs poorly on the test data. Which of the following methods should the Specialist consider using to correct this? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Decrease regularization.
choices.B: Increase regularization.
choices.C: Increase dropout.
choices.D: Decrease dropout.
choices.E: Increase feature combinations.
choices.F: Decrease feature combinations.

explanation:
Key Concept: Overfitting means the learned function fits training-specific patterns that do not generalize.

A. Decrease regularization. — Less regularization gives the model more freedom to fit noise, worsening the described training–test gap.

B. Increase regularization. — Stronger regularization constrains the fitted model and can reduce dependence on training-specific patterns.

C. Increase dropout. — Increasing dropout discourages reliance on particular activations and can improve generalization.

D. Decrease dropout. — Reducing dropout removes a regularization mechanism and can make memorization easier.

E. Increase feature combinations. — Additional feature interactions increase representational complexity and can worsen overfitting without evidence that more capacity is needed.

F. Decrease feature combinations. — Reducing unnecessary feature combinations limits model complexity and can reduce memorization of accidental training relationships.

text: A Data Scientist needs to create a serverless ingestion and analytics solution for high-velocity, real-time streaming data. The ingestion process must buffer and convert incoming records from JSON to a query-optimized, columnar format without data loss. The output datastore must be highly available, and Analysts must be able to run SQL queries against the data and connect to existing business intelligence dashboards. Which solution should the Data Scientist build to satisfy the requirements?

choices.A: Create a schema in the AWS Glue Data Catalog of the incoming data format. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to stream the data and transform the data to Apache Parquet or ORC format using the AWS Glue Data Catalog before delivering to Amazon S3. Have the Analysts query the data directly from Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena, and connect to BI tools using the Athena Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connector.
choices.B: Write each JSON record to a staging location in Amazon S3. Use the S3 Put event to trigger an AWS Lambda function that transforms the data into Apache Parquet or ORC format and writes the data to a processed data location in Amazon S3. Have the Analysts query the data directly from Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena, and connect to BI tools using the Athena Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connector.
choices.C: Write each JSON record to a staging location in Amazon S3. Use the S3 Put event to trigger an AWS Lambda function that transforms the data into Apache Parquet or ORC format and inserts it into an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database. Have the Analysts query and run dashboards from the RDS database.
choices.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to ingest the streaming data and perform real-time SQL queries to convert the records to Apache Parquet before delivering to Amazon S3. Have the Analysts query the data directly from Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena and connect to BI tools using the Athena Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connector.

explanation:
Key Concept: Firehose buffers streaming JSON and converts it to columnar S3 data using a Glue schema; Athena provides SQL access.

A. Create a schema in the AWS Glue Data Catalog of the incoming data format. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to stream the data and transform the data to Apache Parquet or ORC format using the AWS Glue Data Catalog before delivering to Amazon S3. Have the Analysts query the data directly from Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena, and connect to BI tools using the Athena Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connector. — The managed Firehose–S3 path supplies buffering and format conversion, while Athena and JDBC connect the stored dataset to SQL users and BI tools.

B. Write each JSON record to a staging location in Amazon S3. Use the S3 Put event to trigger an AWS Lambda function that transforms the data into Apache Parquet or ORC format and writes the data to a processed data location in Amazon S3. Have the Analysts query the data directly from Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena, and connect to BI tools using the Athena Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connector. — Per-record S3 events and custom Lambda conversion add code, retries, and many small files instead of using built-in buffered delivery.

C. Write each JSON record to a staging location in Amazon S3. Use the S3 Put event to trigger an AWS Lambda function that transforms the data into Apache Parquet or ORC format and inserts it into an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database. Have the Analysts query and run dashboards from the RDS database. — This adds a database-loading pipeline and confuses columnar file output with relational inserts; it is not the requested managed S3 analytics flow.

D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to ingest the streaming data and perform real-time SQL queries to convert the records to Apache Parquet before delivering to Amazon S3. Have the Analysts query the data directly from Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena and connect to BI tools using the Athena Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) connector. — Streaming SQL is not the built-in JSON-to-Parquet delivery mechanism described. Firehose directly provides that managed conversion and delivery feature.

text: An online reseller has a large, multi-column dataset with one column missing 30% of its data. A Machine Learning Specialist believes that certain columns in the dataset could be used to reconstruct the missing data. Which reconstruction approach should the Specialist use to preserve the integrity of the dataset?

choices.A: Listwise deletion
choices.B: Last observation carried forward
choices.C: Multiple imputation
choices.D: Mean substitution

explanation:
Key Concept: Multiple imputation estimates missing values from relationships among observed variables and reflects uncertainty across completed datasets.

A. Listwise deletion — Listwise deletion discards records with missing values, potentially losing 30% of otherwise useful observations and introducing selection bias.

B. Last observation carried forward — Carrying the last value forward assumes ordered observations and temporal continuity, neither of which is provided here.

C. Multiple imputation — Multiple imputation uses the other informative columns to estimate missing entries, preserving relationships more effectively than a single constant fill.

D. Mean substitution — A single mean ignores relationships with other columns and artificially reduces variation in the imputed feature.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is training a model to identify the make and model of vehicles in images. The Specialist wants to use transfer learning and an existing model trained on images of general objects. The Specialist collated a large custom dataset of pictures containing different vehicle makes and models. What should the Specialist do to initialize the model to re-train it with the custom data?

choices.A: Initialize the model with random weights in all layers including the last fully connected layer.
choices.B: Initialize the model with pre-trained weights in all layers and replace the last fully connected layer.
choices.C: Initialize the model with random weights in all layers and replace the last fully connected layer.
choices.D: Initialize the model with pre-trained weights in all layers including the last fully connected layer.

explanation:
Key Concept: Transfer learning reuses pretrained feature extraction and adapts the output head to the new labels.

A. Initialize the model with random weights in all layers including the last fully connected layer. — Randomizing every layer discards the learned visual features and turns the task into training from scratch.

B. Initialize the model with pre-trained weights in all layers and replace the last fully connected layer. — Keep pretrained weights for reusable visual features, then replace the final layer with an output head sized for the vehicle make/model classes.

C. Initialize the model with random weights in all layers and replace the last fully connected layer. — Replacing the head does not recover the benefit lost by randomizing all pretrained feature-extraction layers.

D. Initialize the model with pre-trained weights in all layers including the last fully connected layer. — The original final layer predicts the old general-object classes, which do not match the new vehicle labels.
