text: An office security agency conducted a successful pilot using 100 cameras installed at key locations within the main office. Images from the cameras were uploaded to Amazon S3 and tagged using Amazon Rekognition, and the results were stored in Amazon ES. The agency is now looking to expand the pilot into a full production system using thousands of video cameras in its office locations globally. The goal is to identify activities performed by non-employees in real time Which solution should the agency consider?

choices.A: Use a proxy server at each local office and for each camera, and stream the RTSP feed to a unique Amazon Kinesis Video Streams video stream. On each stream, use Amazon Rekognition Video and create a stream processor to detect faces from a collection of known employees, and alert when non-employees are detected.
choices.B: Use a proxy server at each local office and for each camera, and stream the RTSP feed to a unique Amazon Kinesis Video Streams video stream. On each stream, use Amazon Rekognition Image to detect faces from a collection of known employees and alert when non-employees are detected.
choices.C: Install AWS DeepLens cameras and use the DeepLens_Kinesis_Video module to stream video to Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for each camera. On each stream, use Amazon Rekognition Video and create a stream processor to detect faces from a collection on each stream, and alert when non-employees are detected.
choices.D: Install AWS DeepLens cameras and use the DeepLens_Kinesis_Video module to stream video to Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for each camera. On each stream, run an AWS Lambda function to capture image fragments and then call Amazon Rekognition Image to detect faces from a collection of known employees, and alert when non-employees are detected.

explanation:
Key Concept: Streaming face search combines Kinesis Video Streams with a Rekognition Video processor and a known-face collection.

A. Use a proxy server at each local office and for each camera, and stream the RTSP feed to a unique Amazon Kinesis Video Streams video stream. On each stream, use Amazon Rekognition Video and create a stream processor to detect faces from a collection of known employees, and alert when non-employees are detected. — This reuses existing RTSP cameras and managed video face search. Application logic can flag nonmatches; it must handle uncertain matches rather than equating every nonmatch with an intruder.

B. Use a proxy server at each local office and for each camera, and stream the RTSP feed to a unique Amazon Kinesis Video Streams video stream. On each stream, use Amazon Rekognition Image to detect faces from a collection of known employees and alert when non-employees are detected. — Rekognition Image processes individual images, not a Kinesis video stream through the proposed streaming face-search processor.

C. Install AWS DeepLens cameras and use the DeepLens_Kinesis_Video module to stream video to Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for each camera. On each stream, use Amazon Rekognition Video and create a stream processor to detect faces from a collection on each stream, and alert when non-employees are detected. — Replacing thousands of existing cameras adds unnecessary hardware work. DeepLens is also a retired product rather than a current expansion path.

D. Install AWS DeepLens cameras and use the DeepLens_Kinesis_Video module to stream video to Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for each camera. On each stream, run an AWS Lambda function to capture image fragments and then call Amazon Rekognition Image to detect faces from a collection of known employees, and alert when non-employees are detected. — Camera replacement plus custom frame extraction and Lambda processing adds more effort than the managed streaming integration.

text: A company's Machine Learning Specialist needs to improve the training speed of a time-series forecasting model using TensorFlow. The training is currently implemented on a single-GPU machine and takes approximately 23 hours to complete. The training needs to be run daily. The model accuracy is acceptable, but the company anticipates a continuous increase in the size of the training data and a need to update the model on an hourly, rather than a daily, basis. The company also wants to minimize coding effort and infrastructure changes. What should the Machine Learning Specialist do to the training solution to allow it to scale for future demand?

choices.A: Do not change the TensorFlow code. Change the machine to one with a more powerful GPU to speed up the training.
choices.B: Change the TensorFlow code to implement a Horovod distributed framework supported by Amazon SageMaker. Parallelize the training to as many machines as needed to achieve the business goals.
choices.C: Switch to using a built-in AWS SageMaker DeepAR model. Parallelize the training to as many machines as needed to achieve the business goals.
choices.D: Move the training to Amazon EMR and distribute the workload to as many machines as needed to achieve the business goals.

explanation:
Key Concept: Distributed data-parallel training scales an existing model across additional compute rather than relying only on a larger single GPU.

A. Do not change the TensorFlow code. Change the machine to one with a more powerful GPU to speed up the training. — A larger GPU offers limited vertical scaling and may not accommodate growing data and an hourly training target.

B. Change the TensorFlow code to implement a Horovod distributed framework supported by Amazon SageMaker. Parallelize the training to as many machines as needed to achieve the business goals. — Horovod can distribute the existing TensorFlow training across SageMaker workers, preserving the model while adding a scalable parallel training approach.

C. Switch to using a built-in AWS SageMaker DeepAR model. Parallelize the training to as many machines as needed to achieve the business goals. — Replacing the proven model with DeepAR changes its behavior and validation requirements; built-in DeepAR is not the stated arbitrary multi-instance scaling solution.

D. Move the training to Amazon EMR and distribute the workload to as many machines as needed to achieve the business goals. — Moving the entire training workflow to EMR adds platform changes beyond adapting the existing SageMaker TensorFlow training.

text: Which of the following metrics should a Machine Learning Specialist generally use to compare/evaluate machine learning classification models against each other?

choices.A: Recall
choices.B: Misclassification rate
choices.C: Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)
choices.D: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)

explanation:
Key Concept: ROC-AUC compares a classifier's ranking of positive and negative examples across decision thresholds.

A. Recall — Recall measures positive-class coverage at a chosen operating point and ignores false positives, so it is incomplete for this broad comparison.

B. Misclassification rate — Misclassification rate depends on the chosen threshold and can hide poor minority-class performance in imbalanced data.

C. Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) — MAPE measures relative numeric prediction error and is not a standard classification metric.

D. Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) — ROC-AUC provides a threshold-independent ranking comparison. The final metric should still reflect class imbalance and business costs; AUC is not universally sufficient.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is required to build a supervised image-recognition model to identify a cat. The ML Specialist performs some tests and records the following results for a neural network-based image classifier: Total number of images available = 1,000 Test set images = 100 (constant test set) The ML Specialist notices that, in over 75% of the misclassified images, the cats were held upside down by their owners. Which techniques can be used by the ML Specialist to improve this specific test error?

choices.A: Increase the training data by adding variation in rotation for training images.
choices.B: Increase the number of epochs for model training
choices.C: Increase the number of layers for the neural network.
choices.D: Increase the dropout rate for the second-to-last layer.

explanation:
Key Concept: Augmentation should target the input variations associated with observed model failures.

A. Increase the training data by adding variation in rotation for training images. — Label-preserving rotations add the upside-down orientations missing from training, directly addressing the dominant error pattern.

B. Increase the number of epochs for model training — More epochs on the same orientations do not supply examples of upside-down cats and may increase overfitting.

C. Increase the number of layers for the neural network. — Additional layers increase capacity but do not directly correct the missing orientation coverage.

D. Increase the dropout rate for the second-to-last layer. — Dropout regularizes the model, but targeted rotation augmentation more directly addresses the identified source of errors.

text: A data scientist has explored and sanitized a dataset in preparation for the modeling phase of a supervised learning task. The statistical dispersion can vary widely between features, sometimes by several orders of magnitude. Before moving on to the modeling phase, the data scientist wants to ensure that the prediction performance on the production data is as accurate as possible. Which sequence of steps should the data scientist take to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Apply random sampling to the dataset. Then split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets.
choices.B: Split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets. Then rescale the training set and apply the same scaling to the validation and test sets.
choices.C: Rescale the dataset. Then split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets.
choices.D: Split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets. Then rescale the training set, the validation set, and the test set independently.

explanation:
Key Concept: Fit preprocessing parameters only on training data and reuse the same transformation for every later dataset.

A. Apply random sampling to the dataset. Then split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets. — Random sampling and splitting do not resolve feature scales that differ by orders of magnitude.

B. Split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets. Then rescale the training set and apply the same scaling to the validation and test sets. — Splitting first prevents leakage; fitting a scaler on training data and reusing it maintains consistent feature meaning in validation, test, and production.

C. Rescale the dataset. Then split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets. — Fitting scaling statistics before splitting exposes the transformation to validation and test information.

D. Split the dataset into training, validation, and test sets. Then rescale the training set, the validation set, and the test set independently. — Independent scaling gives the same raw value different representations across datasets and does not reproduce the training transformation.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is working with a large cybersecurity company that manages security events in real time for companies around the world. The cybersecurity company wants to design a solution that will allow it to use machine learning to score malicious events as anomalies on the data as it is being ingested. The company also wants be able to save the results in its data lake for later processing and analysis. What is the MOST efficient way to accomplish these tasks?

choices.A: Ingest the data using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, and use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics Random Cut Forest (RCF) for anomaly detection. Then use Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the results to Amazon S3.
choices.B: Ingest the data into Apache Spark Streaming using Amazon EMR, and use Spark MLlib with k-means to perform anomaly detection. Then store the results in an Apache Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) using Amazon EMR with a replication factor of three as the data lake.
choices.C: Ingest the data and store it in Amazon S3. Use AWS Batch along with the AWS Deep Learning AMIs to train a k-means model using TensorFlow on the data in Amazon S3.
choices.D: Ingest the data and store it in Amazon S3. Have an AWS Glue job that is triggered on demand transform the new data. Then use the built-in Random Cut Forest (RCF) model within Amazon SageMaker to detect anomalies in the data.

explanation:
Key Concept: Streaming anomaly scoring must run on arriving events, while durable storage preserves data for later analysis.

A. Ingest the data using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, and use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics Random Cut Forest (RCF) for anomaly detection. Then use Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the results to Amazon S3. — The historical Kinesis SQL RCF function scores the stream, and Firehose delivers results to S3. The retired SQL service requires a different architecture for new deployments.

B. Ingest the data into Apache Spark Streaming using Amazon EMR, and use Spark MLlib with k-means to perform anomaly detection. Then store the results in an Apache Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) using Amazon EMR with a replication factor of three as the data lake. — Self-managed Spark streaming and HDFS add substantial operations; HDFS replication is not a substitute for the requested durable S3 data lake.

C. Ingest the data and store it in Amazon S3. Use AWS Batch along with the AWS Deep Learning AMIs to train a k-means model using TensorFlow on the data in Amazon S3. — Batch processing after writing to S3 does not score events as they arrive.

D. Ingest the data and store it in Amazon S3. Have an AWS Glue job that is triggered on demand transform the new data. Then use the built-in Random Cut Forest (RCF) model within Amazon SageMaker to detect anomalies in the data. — An on-demand Glue job followed by inference is a batch-oriented flow rather than the stated continuous scoring path.

choices.D: Scikit-leam term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) vectorizer

text: Machine Learning Specialist is building a model to predict future employment rates based on a wide range of economic factors. While exploring the data, the Specialist notices that the magnitude of the input features vary greatly. The Specialist does not want variables with a larger magnitude to dominate the model. What should the Specialist do to prepare the data for model training?

choices.A: Apply quantile binning to group the data into categorical bins to keep any relationships in the data by replacing the magnitude with distribution.
choices.B: Apply the Cartesian product transformation to create new combinations of fields that are independent of the magnitude.
choices.C: Apply normalization to ensure each field will have a mean of 0 and a variance of 1 to remove any significant magnitude.
choices.D: Apply the orthogonal sparse bigram (OSB) transformation to apply a fixed-size sliding window to generate new features of a similar magnitude.

explanation:
Key Concept: Standardization puts numeric features on comparable scales using statistics fitted to the training data.

A. Apply quantile binning to group the data into categorical bins to keep any relationships in the data by replacing the magnitude with distribution. — Quantile bins discard within-bin numeric detail and are not required merely to remove scale differences.

B. Apply the Cartesian product transformation to create new combinations of fields that are independent of the magnitude. — Feature cross-products create interactions and can amplify scale differences rather than remove them.

C. Apply normalization to ensure each field will have a mean of 0 and a variance of 1 to remove any significant magnitude. — Subtract each feature's training mean and divide by its training standard deviation, producing zero-mean, unit-variance features when variance is nonzero.

D. Apply the orthogonal sparse bigram (OSB) transformation to apply a fixed-size sliding window to generate new features of a similar magnitude. — Orthogonal sparse bigrams construct text features; they are unrelated to scaling continuous economic measurements.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist must build out a process to query a dataset on Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena. The dataset contains more than 800,000 records stored as plaintext CSV files. Each record contains 200 columns and is approximately 1.5 MB in size. Most queries will span 5 to 10 columns only. How should the Machine Learning Specialist transform the dataset to minimize query runtime?

choices.A: Convert the records to Apache Parquet format.
choices.B: Convert the records to JSON format.
choices.C: Convert the records to GZIP CSV format.
choices.D: Convert the records to XML format.

explanation:
Key Concept: Column pruning is especially valuable when queries read only a few columns from very wide records.

A. Convert the records to Apache Parquet format. — Parquet's columnar layout lets Athena read the requested 5–10 columns instead of scanning all 200 as row-oriented text.

B. Convert the records to JSON format. — JSON remains row-oriented and typically adds structural text, so it does not provide the same column-pruning benefit.

C. Convert the records to GZIP CSV format. — GZIP reduces CSV size but retains row-oriented parsing and can also limit file splitting for parallel reads.

D. Convert the records to XML format. — XML adds a verbose row/document structure rather than efficient columnar access.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is developing a daily ETL workflow containing multiple ETL jobs. The workflow consists of the following processes: * Start the workflow as soon as data is uploaded to Amazon S3. * When all the datasets are available in Amazon S3, start an ETL job to join the uploaded datasets with multiple terabyte-sized datasets already stored in Amazon S3. * Store the results of joining datasets in Amazon S3. * If one of the jobs fails, send a notification to the Administrator. Which configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use AWS Lambda to trigger an AWS Step Functions workflow to wait for dataset uploads to complete in Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue to join the datasets. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an SNS notification to the Administrator in the case of a failure.
choices.B: Develop the ETL workflow using AWS Lambda to start an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. Use a lifecycle configuration script to join the datasets and persist the results in Amazon S3. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an SNS notification to the Administrator in the case of a failure.
choices.C: Develop the ETL workflow using AWS Batch to trigger the start of ETL jobs when data is uploaded to Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue to join the datasets in Amazon S3. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an SNS notification to the Administrator in the case of a failure.
choices.D: Use AWS Lambda to chain other Lambda functions to read and join the datasets in Amazon S3 as soon as the data is uploaded to Amazon S3. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an SNS notification to the Administrator in the case of a failure.

explanation:
Key Concept: Orchestrate dependencies separately from distributed ETL execution and failure notification.

A. Use AWS Lambda to trigger an AWS Step Functions workflow to wait for dataset uploads to complete in Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue to join the datasets. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an SNS notification to the Administrator in the case of a failure. — Step Functions can wait and coordinate the arrivals, Glue performs the large joins, and monitored failures can trigger CloudWatch/SNS notifications.

Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an SNS notification to the Administrator in the case of a failure. — A notebook lifecycle script is not a robust distributed ETL orchestration platform for multi-terabyte joins and dependent jobs.

text: A large consumer goods manufacturer has the following products on sale: * 34 different toothpaste variants * 48 different toothbrush variants * 43 different mouthwash variants The entire sales history of all these products is available in Amazon S3. Currently, the company is using custom-built autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models to forecast demand for these products. The company wants to predict the demand for a new product that will soon be launched. Which solution should a Machine Learning Specialist apply?

choices.B: Train an Amazon SageMaker DeepAR algorithm to forecast demand for the new product.

choices.D: Train a custom XGBoost model to forecast demand for the new product.

explanation:
Key Concept: DeepAR learns shared temporal patterns across related product series rather than fitting each product entirely independently.

A. Train a custom ARIMA model to forecast demand for the new product. — A standalone ARIMA model for a brand-new product lacks its own demand history and does not automatically transfer patterns from related products.

B. Train an Amazon SageMaker DeepAR algorithm to forecast demand for the new product. — DeepAR can learn from related product histories and relevant features. Forecasting a new product still requires suitable context/covariates; it is not a guarantee of arbitrary zero-history forecasting.

D. Train a custom XGBoost model to forecast demand for the new product. — A custom XGBoost forecasting pipeline needs engineered temporal features and training design; DeepAR provides the more direct cross-series forecasting approach.

choices.A: Define security group(s) to allow all HTTP inbound/outbound traffic and assign those security group(s) to the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance.
choices.B: Configure the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance to have access to the VPC. Grant permission in the KMS key policy to the notebook's KMS role.
choices.C: Assign an IAM role to the Amazon SageMaker notebook with S3 read access to the dataset. Grant permission in the KMS key policy to that role.
choices.D: Assign the same KMS key used to encrypt data in Amazon S3 to the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance.

explanation:
Key Concept: Reading an SSE-KMS object requires both S3 object permission and permission to use the encryption key.

A. Define security group(s) to allow all HTTP inbound/outbound traffic and assign those security group(s) to the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. — Permissive HTTP network rules do not grant S3 or KMS authorization and unnecessarily widen network access.

B. Configure the Amazon SageMaker notebook instance to have access to the VPC. Grant permission in the KMS key policy to the notebook's KMS role. — VPC access alone does not authorize object retrieval, and the relevant identity is the notebook execution role rather than an unspecified KMS role.

text: A Data Scientist needs to migrate an existing on-premises ETL process to the cloud. The current process runs at regular time intervals and uses PySpark to combine and format multiple large data sources into a single consolidated output for downstream processing. The Data Scientist has been given the following requirements to the cloud solution: • Combine multiple data sources. • Reuse existing PySpark logic. • Run the solution on the existing schedule. • Minimize the number of servers that will need to be managed. Which architecture should the Data Scientist use to build this solution?

choices.A: Write the raw data to Amazon S3. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to submit a Spark step to a persistent Amazon EMR cluster based on the existing schedule. Use the existing PySpark logic to run the ETL job on the EMR cluster. Output the results to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use.
choices.B: Write the raw data to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue ETL job to perform the ETL processing against the input data. Write the ETL job in PySpark to leverage the existing logic. Create a new AWS Glue trigger to trigger the ETL job based on the existing schedule. Configure the output target of the ETL job to write to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use.
choices.C: Write the raw data to Amazon S3. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to run on the existing schedule and process the input data from Amazon S3. Write the Lambda logic in Python and implement the existing PySpark logic to perform the ETL process. Have the Lambda function output the results to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use.
choices.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to stream the input data and perform real-time SQL queries against the stream to carry out the required transformations within the stream. Deliver the output results to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use.

explanation:
Key Concept: Glue runs managed Spark ETL jobs and supports scheduled execution without a persistent customer-managed cluster.

A. Write the raw data to Amazon S3. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to submit a Spark step to a persistent Amazon EMR cluster based on the existing schedule. Use the existing PySpark logic to run the ETL job on the EMR cluster. Output the results to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use. — A persistent EMR cluster can reuse Spark code but requires more cluster management and ongoing provisioned resources.

B. Write the raw data to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue ETL job to perform the ETL processing against the input data. Write the ETL job in PySpark to leverage the existing logic. Create a new AWS Glue trigger to trigger the ETL job based on the existing schedule. Configure the output target of the ETL job to write to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use. — A scheduled Glue PySpark job reuses the transformation logic, joins the S3 inputs, and writes the consolidated output without managing servers.

C. Write the raw data to Amazon S3. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to run on the existing schedule and process the input data from Amazon S3. Write the Lambda logic in Python and implement the existing PySpark logic to perform the ETL process. Have the Lambda function output the results to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use. — Lambda is not a distributed Spark runtime for combining these large datasets and has execution-resource limits.

D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to stream the input data and perform real-time SQL queries against the stream to carry out the required transformations within the stream. Deliver the output results to a "processed" location in Amazon S3 that is accessible for downstream use. — A streaming SQL rewrite changes both the batch schedule and the existing PySpark implementation, adding unnecessary migration work.

text: A Data Scientist is building a model to predict customer churn using a dataset of 100 continuous numerical features. The Marketing team has not provided any insight about which features are relevant for churn prediction. The Marketing team wants to interpret the model and see the direct impact of relevant features on the model outcome. While training a logistic regression model, the Data Scientist observes that there is a wide gap between the training and validation set accuracy. Which methods can the Data Scientist use to improve the model performance and satisfy the Marketing team's needs? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Add L1 regularization to the classifier
choices.B: Add features to the dataset
choices.C: Perform recursive feature elimination
choices.D: Perform t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)
choices.E: Perform linear discriminant analysis

explanation:
Key Concept: Feature selection can reduce overfitting while preserving the original features needed for coefficient interpretation.

A. Add L1 regularization to the classifier — L1 regularization can shrink some logistic-regression coefficients to zero, selecting a sparse set of interpretable predictors.

B. Add features to the dataset — Adding features without evidence of missing signal increases complexity and can worsen the observed generalization gap.

C. Perform recursive feature elimination — Recursive feature elimination removes less useful original features and retains a subset whose model coefficients remain interpretable.

D. Perform t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) — t-SNE creates nonlinear visualization coordinates, obscuring direct effects of the original features and not serving this interpretable classifier requirement.

E. Perform linear discriminant analysis — Linear discriminant analysis projects features into combinations; those transformed axes do not preserve the requested direct original-feature effects as clearly.

The Data Scientist on this project would like to speed up the model training time without losing a lot of information from the original dataset. Which feature engineering technique should the Data Scientist use to meet the objectives?

choices.A: Run self-correlation on all features and remove highly correlated features
choices.B: Normalize all numerical values to be between 0 and 1
choices.C: Use an autoencoder or principal component analysis (PCA) to replace original features with new features
choices.D: Cluster raw data using k-means and use sample data from each cluster to build a new dataset

explanation:
Key Concept: Dimensionality reduction compresses redundant input information into fewer features, reducing training work and potentially overfitting.

A. Run self-correlation on all features and remove highly correlated features — Self-correlation of a feature with itself is always one; this wording does not define a useful redundancy-removal method.

B. Normalize all numerical values to be between 0 and 1 — Rescaling features changes their magnitudes but leaves the number of highly correlated columns unchanged.

C. Use an autoencoder or principal component analysis (PCA) to replace original features with new features — PCA or an autoencoder can represent the data in fewer dimensions while retaining substantial structure; choose the retained capacity through validation.

D. Cluster raw data using k-means and use sample data from each cluster to build a new dataset — Sampling rows from clusters reduces observations rather than feature dimensionality and can discard useful examples without solving column redundancy.

text: A Data Scientist is training a multilayer perception (MLP) on a dataset with multiple classes. The target class of interest is unique compared to the other classes within the dataset, but it does not achieve and acceptable recall metric. The Data Scientist has already tried varying the number and size of the MLP's hidden layers, which has not significantly improved the results. A solution to improve recall must be implemented as quickly as possible. Which techniques should be used to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Gather more data using Amazon Mechanical Turk and then retrain
choices.B: Train an anomaly detection model instead of an MLP
choices.C: Train an XGBoost model instead of an MLP
choices.D: Add class weights to the MLP's loss function and then retrain

explanation:
Key Concept: Class weighting changes how strongly errors on a target class influence the training loss.

A. Gather more data using Amazon Mechanical Turk and then retrain — Collecting and labeling more examples takes time, while the question asks for a quick change to the existing model.

B. Train an anomaly detection model instead of an MLP — An anomaly detector changes the task and model, rather than directly improving target-class recall in the current classifier.

C. Train an XGBoost model instead of an MLP — Switching algorithms requires new tuning and does not automatically correct the target class's insufficient loss contribution.

D. Add class weights to the MLP's loss function and then retrain — Increasing the target class's weight penalizes its misclassification more strongly, directly encouraging better recall with a small training change.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is applying a linear least squares regression model to a dataset with 1,000 records and 50 features. Prior to training, the ML Specialist notices that two features are perfectly linearly dependent. Why could this be an issue for the linear least squares regression model?

choices.A: It could cause the backpropagation algorithm to fail during training
choices.B: It could create a singular matrix during optimization, which fails to define a unique solution
choices.C: It could modify the loss function during optimization, causing it to fail during training
choices.D: It could introduce non-linear dependencies within the data, which could invalidate the linear assumptions of the model

explanation:
Key Concept: Perfectly dependent columns cause rank deficiency and non-unique ordinary least-squares coefficients.

A. It could cause the backpropagation algorithm to fail during training — Ordinary least squares does not require neural-network backpropagation; rank deficiency is the relevant mathematical issue.

B. It could create a singular matrix during optimization, which fails to define a unique solution — The normal-equation matrix becomes singular, so a unique coefficient vector cannot be recovered by ordinary inversion without additional constraints.

C. It could modify the loss function during optimization, causing it to fail during training — Feature dependence does not change the definition of the least-squares loss; it creates multiple coefficient solutions with the same fitted values.

D. It could introduce non-linear dependencies within the data, which could invalidate the linear assumptions of the model — The relationship described is exactly linear, not evidence that nonlinear dependencies were introduced.

text: Given the following confusion matrix for a movie classification model, what is the true class frequency for Romance and the predicted class frequency for Adventure?

choices.A: The true class frequency for Romance is 77.56% and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is 20.85%
choices.B: The true class frequency for Romance is 57.92% and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is 13.12%
choices.C: The true class frequency for Romance is 0.78 and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is (0.47-0.32)
choices.D: The true class frequency for Romance is 77.56% × 0.78 and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is 20.85% × 0.32

explanation:
Key Concept: True class frequency is a row total; predicted class frequency is a column total in this matrix.

A. The true class frequency for Romance is 77.56% and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is 20.85% — 77.56% is the predicted Romance total, and 20.85% is the true Adventure total; both use the wrong axis.

B. The true class frequency for Romance is 57.92% and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is 13.12% — The Romance row total is 57.92%, while the Adventure column total is 13.12%, exactly matching the requested frequencies.

C. The true class frequency for Romance is 0.78 and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is (0.47-0.32) — 0.78 and 0.32 are F1 values in the displayed summary, not class frequencies; subtracting F1 values does not produce a frequency.

D. The true class frequency for Romance is 77.56% × 0.78 and the predicted class frequency for Adventure is 20.85% × 0.32 — Multiplying marginal percentages by F1 scores has no basis for computing the requested true or predicted class frequencies.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist wants to bring a custom algorithm to Amazon SageMaker. The Specialist implements the algorithm in a Docker container supported by Amazon SageMaker. How should the Specialist package the Docker container so that Amazon SageMaker can launch the training correctly?

choices.A: Modify the bash_profile file in the container and add a bash command to start the training program
choices.B: Use CMD config in the Dockerfile to add the training program as a CMD of the image
choices.C: Configure the training program as an ENTRYPOINT named train
choices.D: Copy the training program to directory /opt/ml/train

explanation:
Key Concept: SageMaker launches a training container with a train argument, so its entrypoint must start or dispatch the training program.

A. Modify the bash_profile file in the container and add a bash command to start the training program — A shell profile is not a reliable container startup mechanism because the training launch does not require an interactive login shell.

B. Use CMD config in the Dockerfile to add the training program as a CMD of the image — SageMaker supplies its training command and can override CMD; relying only on CMD does not define the required training entrypoint behavior.

C. Configure the training program as an ENTRYPOINT named train — Use an ENTRYPOINT that launches training or handles the train argument. The executable need not literally be named train; handling the launch contract is what matters.

D. Copy the training program to directory /opt/ml/train — Copying a program into /opt/ml/train does not configure Docker to execute it or handle SageMaker's training argument.

text: A Data Scientist needs to analyze employment data. The dataset contains approximately 10 million observations on people across 10 different features. During the preliminary analysis, the Data Scientist notices that income and age distributions are not normal. While income levels shows a right skew as expected, with fewer individuals having a higher income, the age distribution also shows a right skew, with fewer older individuals participating in the workforce. Which feature transformations can the Data Scientist apply to fix the incorrectly skewed data? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Cross-validation
choices.B: Numerical value binning
choices.C: High-degree polynomial transformation
choices.D: Logarithmic transformation
choices.E: One hot encoding

explanation:
Key Concept: Transformations can reduce the influence of right-skewed numeric features; non-normality alone does not necessarily indicate bad data.

A. Cross-validation — Cross-validation evaluates generalization and does not transform feature distributions.

B. Numerical value binning — Binning represents values by ranges, reducing sensitivity to extreme magnitudes when that representation is useful for the model.

C. High-degree polynomial transformation — High-degree polynomial terms can magnify large values and worsen the effect of an already long right tail.

D. Logarithmic transformation — A logarithmic transform compresses large positive values and can reduce right skew; zeros and negative values require appropriate handling.

E. One hot encoding — One-hot encoding represents categories and is not, by itself, a transformation that corrects a continuous distribution's skew.

text: A web-based company wants to improve its conversion rate on its landing page. Using a large historical dataset of customer visits, the company has repeatedly trained a multi-class deep learning network algorithm on Amazon SageMaker. However, there is an overfitting problem: training data shows 90% accuracy in predictions, while test data shows 70% accuracy only. The company needs to boost the generalization of its model before deploying it into production to maximize conversions of visits to purchases. Which action is recommended to provide the HIGHEST accuracy model for the company's test and validation data?

choices.A: Increase the randomization of training data in the mini-batches used in training
choices.B: Allocate a higher proportion of the overall data to the training dataset
choices.C: Apply L1 or L2 regularization and dropouts to the training
choices.D: Reduce the number of layers and units (or neurons) from the deep learning network

explanation:
Key Concept: Regularization targets a model that fits training data much better than held-out data.

A. Increase the randomization of training data in the mini-batches used in training — Shuffling improves batch composition, but does not directly constrain the excess fitting capacity causing the generalization gap.

B. Allocate a higher proportion of the overall data to the training dataset — The dataset is already large; reallocating held-out observations may weaken evaluation and does not directly regularize the model.

C. Apply L1 or L2 regularization and dropouts to the training — L1/L2 penalties and dropout constrain memorization while preserving the architecture, addressing the stated overfitting directly.

D. Reduce the number of layers and units (or neurons) from the deep learning network — Reducing capacity can also help, but may discard useful representation. It is an alternative to validate, rather than proof of the highest accuracy from the supplied information.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is given a structured dataset on the shopping habits of a company's customer base. The dataset contains thousands of columns of data and hundreds of numerical columns for each customer. The Specialist wants to identify whether there are natural groupings for these columns across all customers and visualize the results as quickly as possible. choices.A: Embed the numerical features using the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) algorithm and create a scatter plot.
choices.B: Run k-means using the Euclidean distance measure for different values of k and create an elbow plot.
choices.C: Embed the numerical features using the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) algorithm and create a line graph.
choices.D: Run k-means using the Euclidean distance measure for different values of k and create box plots for each numerical column within each cluster.

explanation:
Key Concept: A low-dimensional scatter plot can reveal local neighborhoods in a high-dimensional feature representation.

A. Embed the numerical features using the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) algorithm and create a scatter plot. — t-SNE maps numerical feature vectors into a low-dimensional layout that can be inspected for visible groups; such groups still need validation.

B. Run k-means using the Euclidean distance measure for different values of k and create an elbow plot. — An elbow plot helps choose a k-means cluster count but does not show the individual observations' neighborhood structure.

C. Embed the numerical features using the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) algorithm and create a line graph. — A line graph suggests an ordering and connections between observations that the embedding does not define.

D. Run k-means using the Euclidean distance measure for different values of k and create box plots for each numerical column within each cluster. — Many per-feature box plots require more analysis and do not provide a single direct view of the high-dimensional grouping structure.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is planning to create a long-running Amazon EMR cluster. The EMR cluster will have 1 master node, 10 core nodes, and 20 task nodes. choices.D: Both core and task nodes

explanation:

C. Any of the task nodes — Task nodes add processing capacity without storing HDFS blocks, making them the preferred Spot tier for this architecture.

The company wants to predict when an engine is going to have a problem, so it can notify drivers in advance to get engine maintenance. The engine data is loaded into a data lake for training. text: A company wants to predict the sale prices of houses based on available historical sales data. The target variable in the company's dataset is the sale price. The features include parameters such as the lot size, living area measurements, non-living area measurements, number of bedrooms, number of bathrooms, year built, and postal code. The company wants to use multi-variable linear regression to predict house sale prices. Which step should a machine learning specialist take to remove features that are irrelevant for the analysis and reduce the model's complexity?

choices.A: Plot a histogram of the features and compute their standard deviation. Remove features with high variance.
choices.B: Plot a histogram of the features and compute their standard deviation. Remove features with low variance.
choices.C: Build a heatmap showing the correlation of the dataset against itself. Remove features with low mutual correlation scores.
choices.D: Run a correlation check of all features against the target variable. Remove features with low target variable correlation scores.

explanation:
Key Concept: Feature screening for a linear predictor should consider association with its target, not simply feature scale.

A. Plot a histogram of the features and compute their standard deviation. Remove features with high variance. — High variance can reflect different measurement units or useful signal; it is not evidence that a feature is irrelevant.

B. Plot a histogram of the features and compute their standard deviation. Remove features with low variance. — Low variance may identify nearly constant fields, but does not generally establish their relationship to the sale-price target.

C. Build a heatmap showing the correlation of the dataset against itself. Remove features with low mutual correlation scores. — Low correlation with other predictors can mean a feature provides independent useful information, rather than being irrelevant.

D. Run a correlation check of all features against the target variable. Remove features with low target variable correlation scores. — Target correlation provides a simple screen for linear relevance. Validate removals because weak marginal correlation can still hide conditional predictive value.

text: A health care company is planning to use neural networks to classify their X-ray images into normal and abnormal classes. The labeled data is divided into a training set of 1,000 images and a test set of 200 images. The initial training of a neural network model with 50 hidden layers yielded 99% accuracy on the training set, but only 55% accuracy on the test set. What changes should the Specialist consider to solve this issue? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Choose a higher number of layers
choices.B: Choose a lower number of layers
choices.C: Choose a smaller learning rate
choices.D: Enable dropout
choices.E: Include all the images from the test set in the training set
choices.F: Enable early stopping

explanation:
Key Concept: A very deep network trained on a small image dataset can memorize training examples rather than generalize.

A. Choose a higher number of layers — Adding layers increases capacity despite the evidence that the existing model already overfits.

B. Choose a lower number of layers — Reducing depth limits capacity and can improve generalization from only 1,000 training images.

C. Choose a smaller learning rate — A smaller learning rate changes optimization speed; it does not directly remedy the large train–test gap.

D. Enable dropout — Dropout regularizes hidden representations and discourages dependence on training-specific feature combinations.

E. Include all the images from the test set in the training set — Using test images in training leaks evaluation information and prevents an honest estimate of generalization.

F. Enable early stopping — Early stopping selects a checkpoint before validation performance deteriorates, avoiding additional fitting of training noise.

text: This graph shows the training and validation loss against the epochs for a neural network. The network being trained is as follows: • Two dense layers, one output neuron • 100 neurons in each layer • 100 epochs Random initialization of weights Which technique can be used to improve model performance in terms of accuracy in the validation set?

choices.B: Random initialization of weights with appropriate seed
choices.C: Increasing the number of epochs
choices.D: Adding another layer with the 100 neurons

explanation:
Key Concept: When validation loss rises while training loss falls, later epochs are worsening generalization.

A. Early stopping — Stop near the best validation-loss checkpoint, before the rise after roughly epoch 60, and restore those weights.

C. Increasing the number of epochs — More epochs continue the region where validation error is rising, so they are likely to worsen the shown problem.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is attempting to build a linear regression model. Given the displayed residual plot only, what is the MOST likely problem with the model?

choices.A: Linear regression is inappropriate. The residuals do not have constant variance.
choices.B: Linear regression is inappropriate. The underlying data has outliers.
choices.C: Linear regression is appropriate. The residuals have a zero mean.
choices.D: Linear regression is appropriate. The residuals have constant variance.

explanation:
Key Concept: Heteroscedasticity means that residual variability changes with the predictor or fitted value.

A. Linear regression is inappropriate. The residuals do not have constant variance. — The residual spread grows at higher x values, violating constant-variance assumptions of the basic homoscedastic linear-regression model; a transform or weighted/robust treatment may be needed.

B. Linear regression is inappropriate. The underlying data has outliers. — Some residuals are large, but the systematic widening is stronger evidence of nonconstant variance than isolated outliers alone.

C. Linear regression is appropriate. The residuals have a zero mean. — Residuals near zero at some locations do not establish that the constant-variance model is appropriate.

D. Linear regression is appropriate. The residuals have constant variance. — The high-x residuals are much more dispersed than low-x residuals, directly contradicting constant variance.

text: A large company has developed a BI application that generates reports and dashboards using data collected from various operational metrics. The company wants to provide executives with an enhanced experience so they can use natural language to get data from the reports. The company wants the executives to be able ask questions using written and spoken interfaces. Which combination of services can be used to build this conversational interface? (Choose three.)

choices.C: Amazon Lex
choices.D: Amazon Polly
choices.E: Amazon Comprehend
choices.F: Amazon Transcribe

explanation:
Key Concept: Conversational input, speech conversion, and intent handling overlap across these services, so three mandatory services are not uniquely determined.

A. Alexa for Business — Alexa for Business was an enterprise voice-interface option, but it is historical and not necessary for every written-and-spoken BI interface.

B. Amazon Connect — Connect supplies contact-center channels and can integrate with Lex, but a contact center is not required by the BI application description.

C. Amazon Lex — Lex directly supports conversational text and speech, making it a plausible central service without establishing two additional mandatory choices.

text: A machine learning specialist works for a fruit processing company and needs to build a system that categorizes apples into three types. The specialist has collected a dataset that contains 150 images for each type of apple and applied transfer learning on a neural network that was pretrained on ImageNet with this dataset. The company requires at least 85% accuracy to make use of the model. After an exhaustive grid search, the optimal hyperparameters produced the following: • 68% accuracy on the training set • 67% accuracy on the validation set What can the machine learning specialist do to improve the system's accuracy?

choices.A: Upload the model to an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance and use the Amazon SageMaker HPO feature to optimize the model's hyperparameters.
choices.B: Add more data to the training set and retrain the model using transfer learning to reduce the bias.
choices.C: Use a neural network model with more layers that are pretrained on ImageNet and apply transfer learning to increase the variance.
choices.D: Train a new model using the current neural network architecture.

explanation:
Key Concept: Similarly low training and validation accuracy suggest underfitting or insufficient representation rather than classic overfitting.

A. Upload the model to an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance and use the Amazon SageMaker HPO feature to optimize the model's hyperparameters. — Another hyperparameter search does not directly fix a representation limitation after an exhaustive search has already been performed.

B. Add more data to the training set and retrain the model using transfer learning to reduce the bias. — More examples mainly help variance and coverage; they do not reliably reduce the high bias suggested by poor training accuracy.

C. Use a neural network model with more layers that are pretrained on ImageNet and apply transfer learning to increase the variance. — A more expressive pretrained network can improve representation and reduce underfitting, provided fine-tuning and validation confirm the gain.

D. Train a new model using the current neural network architecture. — Repeating the same architecture without a meaningful change does not address the observed capacity or representation limitation.

text: A company uses camera images of the tops of items displayed on store shelves to determine which items were removed and which ones still remain. After several hours of data labeling, the company has a total of 1,000 hand-labeled images covering 10 distinct items. The training results were poor. Which machine learning approach fulfills the company's long-term needs?

choices.A: Convert the images to grayscale and retrain the model
choices.B: Reduce the number of distinct items from 10 to 2, build the model, and iterate
choices.C: Attach different colored labels to each item, take the images again, and build the model
choices.D: Augment training data for each item using image variants like inversions and translations, build the model, and iterate.

explanation:
Key Concept: Label-preserving image augmentation increases variation when labeled examples are scarce.

A. Convert the images to grayscale and retrain the model — Grayscale conversion can remove useful product color information and does not address the limited variety of training examples.

B. Reduce the number of distinct items from 10 to 2, build the model, and iterate — Reducing the task to two items fails the long-term requirement to recognize all ten products.

C. Attach different colored labels to each item, take the images again, and build the model — Changing every physical product and recollecting images creates an operational dependency instead of learning from natural product appearance.

D. Augment training data for each item using image variants like inversions and translations, build the model, and iterate. — Translations and other valid image variations broaden training coverage for each item, improving robustness while keeping the original recognition task.

text: A Data Scientist is developing a binary classifier to predict whether a patient has a particular disease on a series of test results. The Data Scientist has data on 400 patients randomly selected from the population. The disease is seen in 3% of the population. Which cross-validation strategy should the Data Scientist adopt?

choices.A: A k-fold cross-validation strategy with k=5
choices.B: A stratified k-fold cross-validation strategy with k=5
choices.C: A k-fold cross-validation strategy with k=5 and 3 repeats
choices.D: An 80/20 stratified split between training and validation

explanation:
Key Concept: Stratified folds preserve representation of a rare class during cross-validation.

A. A k-fold cross-validation strategy with k=5 — Ordinary random folds may contain very few or no positive cases when the disease rate is only 3%.

B. A stratified k-fold cross-validation strategy with k=5 — Stratified five-fold cross-validation distributes the small number of positive cases across folds, making each evaluation more representative.

C. A k-fold cross-validation strategy with k=5 and 3 repeats — Repeating unstratified folds does not ensure that the rare class is adequately represented in each fold.

D. An 80/20 stratified split between training and validation — A stratified holdout preserves class proportions but provides only one split; it is not the requested cross-validation approach.

text: A technology startup is using complex deep neural networks and GPU compute to recommend the company's products to its existing customers based upon each customer's habits and interactions. The solution currently pulls each dataset from an Amazon S3 bucket before loading the data into a TensorFlow model pulled from the company's Git repository that runs locally. This job then runs for several hours while continually outputting its progress to the same S3 bucket. The job can be paused, restarted, and continued at any time in the event of a failure, and is run from a central queue. Senior managers are concerned about the complexity of the solution's resource management and the costs involved in repeating the process regularly. They ask for the workload to be automated so it runs once a week, starting Monday and completing by the close of business Friday. Which architecture should be used to scale the solution at the lowest cost?

choices.A: Implement the solution using AWS Deep Learning Containers and run the container as a job using AWS Batch on a GPU-compatible Spot Instance
choices.B: Implement the solution using a low-cost GPU-compatible Amazon EC2 instance and use the AWS Instance Scheduler to schedule the task
choices.C: Implement the solution using AWS Deep Learning Containers, run the workload using AWS Fargate running on Spot Instances, and then schedule the task using the built-in task scheduler
choices.D: Implement the solution using Amazon ECS running on Spot Instances and schedule the task using the ECS service scheduler

explanation:
Key Concept: Checkpointable queued GPU jobs with flexible completion windows can use managed batch scheduling on interruptible capacity.

A. Implement the solution using AWS Deep Learning Containers and run the container as a job using AWS Batch on a GPU-compatible Spot Instance — Batch manages queues and compute provisioning, while GPU-capable Spot instances reduce cost. Saved checkpoints let interrupted jobs resume within the weekly window.

B. Implement the solution using a low-cost GPU-compatible Amazon EC2 instance and use the AWS Instance Scheduler to schedule the task — Scheduling a single EC2 instance's uptime does not provide the same managed job queue, retries, or elastic GPU capacity.

C. Implement the solution using AWS Deep Learning Containers, run the workload using AWS Fargate running on Spot Instances, and then schedule the task using the built-in task scheduler — Fargate does not provide the GPU resource required by this TensorFlow workload.

D. Implement the solution using Amazon ECS running on Spot Instances and schedule the task using the ECS service scheduler — An ECS service scheduler maintains service tasks; it is less direct than Batch job scheduling for queued, finite, restartable GPU work.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is working for an online retailer that wants to run analytics on every customer visit, processed through a machine learning pipeline. The data needs to be ingested by Amazon Kinesis Data Streams at up to 100 transactions per second, and the JSON data blob is 100 KB in size. What is the MINIMUM number of shards in Kinesis Data Streams the Specialist should use to successfully ingest this data?

choices.A: 1 shards
choices.B: 10 shards
choices.C: 100 shards
choices.D: 1,000 shards

explanation:
Key Concept: Provisioned stream capacity must satisfy both records-per-second and bytes-per-second limits, with appropriate partition-key distribution.

A. 1 shards — One standard shard's 1 MB/s write capacity is insufficient for roughly 10 MB/s of incoming payloads.

B. 10 shards — 100 records/s × 100 KB is about 10 MB/s; ten standard 1 MB/s shards meet the stated minimum byte throughput, assuming evenly distributed writes.

C. 100 shards — The record count does not require one shard per record; this greatly exceeds the capacity implied by the stated load.

D. 1,000 shards — A thousand shards are unnecessary for the requested throughput and would not represent the minimum.

text: A Machine Learning Specialist is deciding between building a naive Bayesian model or a full Bayesian network for a classification problem. The Specialist computes the Pearson correlation coefficients between each feature and finds that their absolute values range between 0.1 to 0.95. Which model describes the underlying data in this situation?

choices.A: A naive Bayesian model, since the features are all conditionally independent.
choices.B: A full Bayesian network, since the features are all conditionally independent.
choices.C: A naive Bayesian model, since some of the features are statistically dependent.
choices.D: A full Bayesian network, since some of the features are statistically dependent.

explanation:
Key Concept: Naive Bayes assumes feature independence conditional on the class, which differs from marginal Pearson correlation.

A. A naive Bayesian model, since the features are all conditionally independent. — The supplied correlations do not establish conditional independence; strong marginal correlation can still arise through a shared class label.

B. A full Bayesian network, since the features are all conditionally independent. — A full Bayesian network can represent dependencies, but this explanation incorrectly asserts that all features are conditionally independent.

C. A naive Bayesian model, since some of the features are statistically dependent. — Ordinary Naive Bayes does not explicitly model feature-to-feature dependence conditional on the class, so this is not a valid justification for it.

D. A full Bayesian network, since some of the features are statistically dependent. — This is the intended answer if relevant conditional dependencies exist. However, marginal correlation alone does not prove that condition, so the key remains qualified.

text: A Data Scientist is building a linear regression model and will use resulting p-values to evaluate the statistical significance of each coefficient. Upon inspection of the dataset, the Data Scientist discovers that most of the features are normally distributed. The plot of one feature in the dataset is shown in the graphic. What transformation should the Data Scientist apply to satisfy the statistical assumptions of the linear regression model?

choices.A: Exponential transformation
choices.B: Logarithmic transformation
choices.C: Polynomial transformation
choices.D: Sinusoidal transformation

explanation:
Key Concept: A log transform can reduce right skew, but linear regression does not require normally distributed input features.

A. Exponential transformation — Exponentiation generally magnifies a positive right tail, and does not address the question's mistaken predictor-normality premise.

B. Logarithmic transformation — Logarithms can compress a positive right-skewed feature. That may help modeling, but it does not by itself establish the residual assumptions needed for coefficient inference.

C. Polynomial transformation — Polynomial features model nonlinear relationships and may magnify skew; they do not generally make a predictor normal.

D. Sinusoidal transformation — A sinusoidal transform is appropriate for certain cyclic structures, not generic right-skew correction or validation of regression assumptions.

text: A data scientist is developing a pipeline to ingest streaming web traffic data. The data scientist needs to implement a process to identify unusual web traffic patterns as part of the pipeline. The patterns will be used downstream for alerting and incident response. The data scientist has access to unlabeled historic data to use, if needed. The solution needs to do the following: • Calculate an anomaly score for each web traffic entry. Adapt unusual event identification to changing web patterns over time. Which approach should the data scientist implement to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use historic web traffic data to train an anomaly detection model using the Amazon SageMaker Random Cut Forest (RCF) built-in model. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream to process the incoming web traffic data. Attach a preprocessing AWS Lambda function to perform data enrichment by calling the RCF model to calculate the anomaly score for each record.
choices.B: Use historic web traffic data to train an anomaly detection model using the Amazon SageMaker built-in XGBoost model. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream to process the incoming web traffic data. Attach a preprocessing AWS Lambda function to perform data enrichment by calling the XGBoost model to calculate the anomaly score for each record.
choices.C: Collect the streaming data using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Map the delivery stream as an input source for Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Write a SQL query to run in real time against the streaming data with the k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) SQL extension to calculate anomaly scores for each record using a tumbling window.
choices.D: Collect the streaming data using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Map the delivery stream as an input source for Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Write a SQL query to run in real time against the streaming data with the Amazon Random Cut Forest (RCF) SQL extension to calculate anomaly scores for each record using a sliding window.

explanation:
Key Concept: A streaming anomaly detector must adapt to recent observations rather than remain fixed on historical training data.

A. Use historic web traffic data to train an anomaly detection model using the Amazon SageMaker Random Cut Forest (RCF) built-in model. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream to process the incoming web traffic data. Attach a preprocessing AWS Lambda function to perform data enrichment by calling the RCF model to calculate the anomaly score for each record. — An RCF model trained once on history can score records, but the option omits retraining or another mechanism to adapt to changing patterns.

B. Use historic web traffic data to train an anomaly detection model using the Amazon SageMaker built-in XGBoost model. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream to process the incoming web traffic data. Attach a preprocessing AWS Lambda function to perform data enrichment by calling the XGBoost model to calculate the anomaly score for each record. — The proposed XGBoost workflow lacks labeled anomaly targets and does not define an adaptive unsupervised detector.

C. Collect the streaming data using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Map the delivery stream as an input source for Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Write a SQL query to run in real time against the streaming data with the k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) SQL extension to calculate anomaly scores for each record using a tumbling window. — The historical SQL anomaly function was RCF, not the described kNN extension; tumbling windows also reset rather than maintain the proposed sliding context.

D. Collect the streaming data using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Map the delivery stream as an input source for Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Write a SQL query to run in real time against the streaming data with the Amazon Random Cut Forest (RCF) SQL extension to calculate anomaly scores for each record using a sliding window. — Historically, streaming RCF used recent observations to update anomaly scoring while processing incoming events. text: A Data Scientist received a set of insurance records, each consisting of a record ID, the final outcome among 200 categories, and the date of the final outcome. Some partial information on claim contents is also provided, but only for a few of the 200 categories. For each outcome category, there are hundreds of records distributed over the past 3 years. The Data Scientist wants to predict how many claims to expect in each category from month to month, a few months in advance. What type of machine learning model should be used?

choices.A: Classification month-to-month using supervised learning of the 200 categories based on claim contents.
choices.B: Reinforcement learning using claim IDs and timestamps where the agent will identify how many claims in each category to expect from month to month.
choices.C: Forecasting using claim IDs and timestamps to identify how many claims in each category to expect from month to month.
choices.D: Classification with supervised learning of the categories for which partial information on claim contents is provided, and forecasting using claim IDs and timestamps for all other categories.

explanation:
Key Concept: Aggregate outcomes into monthly counts per category, then forecast each category's future count series.

A. Classification month-to-month using supervised learning of the 200 categories based on claim contents. — Classifying individual claims is a different target from predicting the number of claims that will occur next month.

B. Reinforcement learning using claim IDs and timestamps where the agent will identify how many claims in each category to expect from month to month. — There is no sequential action/reward environment requiring reinforcement learning.

C. Forecasting using claim IDs and timestamps to identify how many claims in each category to expect from month to month. — Dates and category labels allow monthly count series to be built and forecast; claim IDs identify records rather than serving as meaningful numeric predictors.

D. Classification with supervised learning of the categories for which partial information on claim contents is provided, and forecasting using claim IDs and timestamps for all other categories. — Splitting categories by availability of text features changes the task unnecessarily; the required output is a count forecast for every category.

text: A company that promotes healthy sleep patterns by providing cloud-connected devices currently hosts a sleep tracking application on AWS. The application collects device usage information from device users. The company's Data Science team is building a machine learning model to predict if and when a user will stop utilizing the company's devices. Predictions from this model are used by a downstream application that determines the best approach for contacting users. The Data Science team is building multiple versions of the machine learning model to evaluate each version against the company's business goals. To measure long-term effectiveness, the team wants to run multiple versions of the model in parallel for long periods of time, with the ability to control the portion of inferences served by the models. Which solution satisfies these requirements with MINIMAL effort?

choices.A: Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker. Create multiple Amazon SageMaker endpoints, one for each model. Programmatically control invoking different models for inference at the application layer.
choices.B: Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker. Create an Amazon SageMaker endpoint configuration with multiple production variants. Programmatically control the portion of the inferences served by the multiple models by updating the endpoint configuration.
choices.C: Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker Neo to take into account different types of medical devices. Programmatically control which model is invoked for inference based on the medical device type.
choices.D: Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker. Create a single endpoint that accesses multiple models. Use Amazon SageMaker batch transform to control invoking the different models through the single endpoint.

explanation:
Key Concept: SageMaker production variants support weighted traffic allocation among model versions behind one endpoint.

A. Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker. Create multiple Amazon SageMaker endpoints, one for each model. Programmatically control invoking different models for inference at the application layer. — Separate endpoints work but require application-level routing and more endpoint management.

B. Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker. Create an Amazon SageMaker endpoint configuration with multiple production variants. Programmatically control the portion of the inferences served by the multiple models by updating the endpoint configuration. — Multiple production variants share one endpoint, and variant weights control the inference split; weights/capacity can be adjusted without writing a custom router.

C. Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker Neo to take into account different types of medical devices. Programmatically control which model is invoked for inference based on the medical device type. — Neo compiles models for deployment targets; it is not the mechanism for weighted long-running model experiments.

D. Build and host multiple models in Amazon SageMaker. Create a single endpoint that accesses multiple models. Use Amazon SageMaker batch transform to control invoking the different models through the single endpoint. — Batch Transform runs offline inference jobs and does not route live traffic between models behind an endpoint.

text: An agricultural company is interested in using machine learning to detect specific types of weeds in a 100-acre grassland field. Currently, the company uses tractor-mounted cameras to capture multiple images of the field as 10 × 10 grids. The company also has a large training dataset that consists of annotated images of popular weed classes like broadleaf and non-broadleaf docks. The company wants to build a weed detection model that will detect specific types of weeds and the location of each type within the field. Once the model is ready, it will be hosted on Amazon SageMaker endpoints. The model will perform real-time inferencing using the images captured by the cameras. Which approach should a Machine Learning Specialist take to obtain accurate predictions?

choices.A: Prepare the images in RecordIO format and upload them to Amazon S3. Use Amazon SageMaker to train, test, and validate the model using an image classification algorithm to categorize images into various weed classes.
choices.B: Prepare the images in Apache Parquet format and upload them to Amazon S3. Use Amazon SageMaker to train, test, and validate the model using an object- detection single-shot multibox detector (SSD) algorithm.
choices.C: Prepare the images in RecordIO format and upload them to Amazon S3. Use Amazon SageMaker to train, test, and validate the model using an object- detection single-shot multibox detector (SSD) algorithm.
choices.D: Prepare the images in Apache Parquet format and upload them to Amazon S3. Use Amazon SageMaker to train, test, and validate the model using an image classification algorithm to categorize images into various weed classes.

explanation:

A. Prepare the images in RecordIO format and upload them to Amazon S3. B. Prepare the images in Apache Parquet format and upload them to Amazon S3. Use Amazon SageMaker to train, test, and validate the model using an object- detection single-shot multibox detector (SSD) algorithm. — The built-in SSD input contract does not accept arbitrary Parquet image records as proposed.

D. Prepare the images in Apache Parquet format and upload them to Amazon S3. Use Amazon SageMaker to train, test, and validate the model using an image classification algorithm to categorize images into various weed classes. — This combines the wrong task output with an unsupported proposed image input format.

text: A manufacturer is operating a large number of factories with a complex supply chain relationship where unexpected downtime of a machine can cause production to stop at several factories. A data scientist wants to analyze sensor data from the factories to identify equipment in need of preemptive maintenance and then dispatch a service team to prevent unplanned downtime. The sensor readings from a single machine can include up to 200 data points including temperatures, voltages, vibrations, RPMs, and pressure readings. To collect this sensor data, the manufacturer deployed Wi-Fi and LANs across the factories. Even though many factory locations do not have reliable or high- speed internet connectivity, the manufacturer would like to maintain near-real-time inference capabilities. Which deployment architecture for the model will address these business requirements?

choices.A: Deploy the model in Amazon SageMaker. Run sensor data through this model to predict which machines need maintenance.
choices.B: Deploy the model on AWS IoT Greengrass in each factory. Run sensor data through this model to infer which machines need maintenance.
choices.C: Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker batch transformation job. Generate inferences in a daily batch report to identify machines that need maintenance.
choices.D: Deploy the model in Amazon SageMaker and use an IoT rule to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Consume a DynamoDB stream from the table with an AWS Lambda function to invoke the endpoint.

explanation:
Key Concept: Local edge inference maintains low latency when cloud connectivity is unreliable.

A. Deploy the model in Amazon SageMaker. Run sensor data through this model to predict which machines need maintenance. — A cloud endpoint depends on successful network communication for each inference, conflicting with the unreliable internet connections.

B. Deploy the model on AWS IoT Greengrass in each factory. Run sensor data through this model to infer which machines need maintenance. — A compatible model deployed through Greengrass can process sensor data inside each factory, maintaining inference without a continuous cloud round trip.

C. Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker batch transformation job. Generate inferences in a daily batch report to identify machines that need maintenance. — Daily batch reports do not meet the near-real-time maintenance detection requirement.

D. Deploy the model in Amazon SageMaker and use an IoT rule to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Consume a DynamoDB stream from the table with an AWS Lambda function to invoke the endpoint. — The DynamoDB/Lambda/cloud-endpoint chain still needs internet connectivity and adds network hops rather than enabling local inference.
