text: A Machine Learning Specialist is designing a scalable data storage solution for Amazon SageMaker. There is an existing TensorFlow-based model implemented as a train.py script that relies on static training data that is currently stored as TFRecords. Which method of providing training data to Amazon SageMaker would meet the business requirements with the LEAST development overhead?

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker script mode and use train.py unchanged. Point the Amazon SageMaker training invocation to the local path of the data without reformatting the training data.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker script mode and use train.py unchanged. Put the TFRecord data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Point the Amazon SageMaker training invocation to the S3 bucket without reformatting the training data.
choices.C: Rewrite the train.py script to add a section that converts TFRecords to protobuf and ingests the protobuf data instead of TFRecords.
choices.D: Prepare the data in the format accepted by Amazon SageMaker. Use AWS Glue or AWS Lambda to reformat and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket.

explanation:
Key Concept: SageMaker framework script mode can use existing TensorFlow data formats instead of requiring a built-in algorithm's serialization.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker script mode and use train.py unchanged. Point the Amazon SageMaker training invocation to the local path of the data without reformatting the training data. — A local notebook path is not directly available to a remote training instance unless the data is uploaded or otherwise made accessible.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker script mode and use train.py unchanged. Put the TFRecord data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Point the Amazon SageMaker training invocation to the S3 bucket without reformatting the training data. — Store the TFRecords in S3 and use TensorFlow script mode, preserving the existing parsing logic; configure the script to use the provided training-channel path.

C. Rewrite the train.py script to add a section that converts TFRecords to protobuf and ingests the protobuf data instead of TFRecords. — Converting an already supported TFRecord dataset adds development work and is unnecessary for TensorFlow script mode.

D. Prepare the data in the format accepted by Amazon SageMaker. Use AWS Glue or AWS Lambda to reformat and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. — There is no single universal SageMaker input format requiring this ETL rewrite; the existing TensorFlow reader can consume TFRecords.

text: A retail company is using Amazon Personalize to provide personalized product recommendations for its customers during a marketing campaign. explanation:

C. Implement a new solution using the built-in factorization machines (FM) algorithm in Amazon SageMaker. — Replacing Personalize with a custom model adds work without directly fixing the lack of fresh training/interaction information.

D. Add event type and event value fields to the interactions dataset in Amazon Personalize. — Adding columns to old interaction records does not create the missing post-launch user behavior data.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist wants to secure calls to the Amazon SageMaker Service API. The specialist has configured Amazon VPC with a VPC interface endpoint for the Amazon SageMaker Service API and is attempting to secure traffic from specific sets of instances and IAM users. The VPC is configured with a single public subnet. Which combination of steps should the ML specialist take to secure the traffic? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Add a VPC endpoint policy to allow access to the IAM users.
choices.B: Modify the users' IAM policy to allow access to Amazon SageMaker Service API calls only.
choices.C: Modify the security group on the endpoint network interface to restrict access to the instances.
choices.D: Modify the ACL on the endpoint network interface to restrict access to the instances.
choices.E: Add a SageMaker Runtime VPC endpoint interface to the VPC.

explanation:
Key Concept: Interface endpoint security combines principal-level policy with network access controls on endpoint interfaces.

A. Add a VPC endpoint policy to allow access to the IAM users. — An endpoint policy can restrict which IAM principals and actions may use that endpoint, alongside normal IAM authorization.

B. Modify the users' IAM policy to allow access to Amazon SageMaker Service API calls only. — Restricting actions in user IAM policies does not identify the permitted source instances or replace a restrictive endpoint policy.

C. Modify the security group on the endpoint network interface to restrict access to the instances. — The endpoint ENI's security group can allow connections only from designated instance security groups or network ranges.

D. Modify the ACL on the endpoint network interface to restrict access to the instances. — Network ACLs apply to subnets, not directly to individual endpoint network interfaces as stated.

E. Add a SageMaker Runtime VPC endpoint interface to the VPC. — The Runtime endpoint serves inference calls; adding it does not secure access to the already configured SageMaker Service API endpoint.

text: An e commerce company wants to launch a new cloud-based product recommendation feature for its web application. Due to data localization regulations, any sensitive data must not leave its on-premises data center, and the product recommendation model must be trained and tested using nonsensitive data only. Data transfer to the cloud must use IPsec. The web application is hosted on premises with a PostgreSQL database that contains all the data. The company wants the data to be uploaded securely to Amazon S3 each day for model retraining. How should a machine learning specialist meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an AWS Glue job to connect to the PostgreSQL DB instance. Ingest tables without sensitive data through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection directly into Amazon S3.
choices.B: Create an AWS Glue job to connect to the PostgreSQL DB instance. Ingest all data through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection into Amazon S3 while removing sensitive data using a PySpark job.
choices.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with table mapping to select PostgreSQL tables with no sensitive data through an SSL connection. Replicate data directly into Amazon S3.
choices.D: Use PostgreSQL logical replication to replicate all data to PostgreSQL in Amazon EC2 through AWS Direct Connect with a VPN connection. Use AWS Glue to move data from Amazon EC2 to Amazon S3.

explanation:
Key Concept: Data residency must be enforced before transfer, and the specified tunnel must provide IPsec.

A. Create an AWS Glue job to connect to the PostgreSQL DB instance. Ingest tables without sensitive data through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection directly into Amazon S3. — Read only nonsensitive tables at the on-premises source over Site-to-Site VPN, which supplies IPsec, then write the allowed data to S3.

B. Create an AWS Glue job to connect to the PostgreSQL DB instance. Ingest all data through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection into Amazon S3 while removing sensitive data using a PySpark job. — Removing sensitive fields in a cloud Glue job occurs after they have left the data center, violating the residency requirement.

C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with table mapping to select PostgreSQL tables with no sensitive data through an SSL connection. Replicate data directly into Amazon S3. — SSL/TLS encrypts the database connection but is not the explicitly required IPsec tunnel.

D. Use PostgreSQL logical replication to replicate all data to PostgreSQL in Amazon EC2 through AWS Direct Connect with a VPN connection. Use AWS Glue to move data from Amazon EC2 to Amazon S3. — Replicating all records to EC2 transfers sensitive data out of the data center before filtering, even if the connection is encrypted.

text: A logistics company needs a forecast model to predict next month's inventory requirements for a single item in 10 warehouses. A machine learning specialist uses Amazon Forecast to develop a forecast model from 3 years of monthly data. There is no missing data. The specialist selects the DeepAR+ algorithm to train a predictor. The predictor means absolute percentage error (MAPE) is much larger than the MAPE produced by the current human forecasters. Which changes to the CreatePredictor API call could improve the MAPE? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Set PerformAutoML to true.
choices.B: Set ForecastHorizon to 4.

explanation:
Key Concept: Algorithm selection and hyperparameter tuning are distinct ways to improve a forecast, but this legacy API forbids enabling both modes together.

A. Set PerformAutoML to true. — AutoML can compare supported forecasting algorithms. It is a plausible alternative experiment, but cannot be enabled together with PerformHPO in one CreatePredictor request.

B. Set ForecastHorizon to 4. — Increasing the horizon to four periods changes the forecasting objective; it does not directly improve the requested next-month accuracy.

C. Set ForecastFrequency to W for weekly. — Changing to weekly frequency does not create weekly information from monthly observations and changes the task resolution.

D. Set PerformHPO to true. — HPO can tune a selected algorithm, but the API restriction prevents combining it with PerformAutoML in the same call as the question suggests.

E. Set FeaturizationMethodName to filling. — Filling addresses missing values; the dataset is explicitly complete, so this does not target the described error.

text: A machine learning specialist is running an Amazon SageMaker endpoint using the built-in object detection algorithm on a P3 instance for real-time predictions in a company's production application. When evaluating the model's resource utilization, the specialist notices that the model is using only a fraction of the GPU. Which architecture changes would ensure that provisioned resources are being utilized effectively?

choices.A: Redeploy the model as a batch transform job on an M5 instance.
choices.B: Redeploy the model on an M5 instance. Attach Amazon Elastic Inference to the instance.
choices.C: Redeploy the model on a P3dn instance.
choices.D: Deploy the model onto an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster using a P3 instance.

explanation:
Key Concept: Inference accelerator capacity should match the model's actual demand rather than leaving a large GPU mostly idle.

A. Redeploy the model as a batch transform job on an M5 instance. — Batch Transform changes real-time serving to asynchronous batch inference, failing the production application's requirement.

B. Redeploy the model on an M5 instance. Attach Amazon Elastic Inference to the instance. — Historically, a CPU instance with a smaller Elastic Inference accelerator reduced unused GPU capacity. Elastic Inference is retired, so this is not a current architecture recommendation.

C. Redeploy the model on a P3dn instance. — A larger GPU instance increases provisioned capacity despite the observed low utilization.

explanation:

Create a Jupyter notebook file (.ipynb) with cells containing the package installation commands to execute and place the file under the /etc/init directory of each Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. — An .ipynb file is not an operating-system startup script simply because it is placed under /etc/init.

text: A Data Scientist is developing a machine learning model to classify whether a financial transaction is fraudulent. The labeled data available for training consists of 100,000 non-fraudulent observations and 1,000 fraudulent observations. The Data Scientist applies the XGBoost algorithm to the data, resulting in the following confusion matrix when the trained model is applied to a previously unseen validation dataset. The accuracy of the model is 99.1%, but the Data Scientist needs to reduce the number of false negatives. Which combination of steps should the Data Scientist take to reduce the number of false negative predictions by the model? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Change the XGBoost eval_metric parameter to optimize based on Root Mean Square Error (RMSE).
choices.B: Increase the XGBoost scale_pos_weight parameter to adjust the balance of positive and negative weights.
choices.C: Increase the XGBoost max_depth parameter because the model is currently underfitting the data.
choices.D: Change the XGBoost eval_metric parameter to optimize based on Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC).
choices.E: Decrease the XGBoost max_depth parameter because the model is currently overfitting the data.

explanation:
Key Concept: With rare fraud, overall accuracy can conceal many false negatives; weighting and suitable model selection focus attention on positive examples.

A. Change the XGBoost eval_metric parameter to optimize based on Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). — RMSE is not the most informative fraud classification evaluation metric and does not directly emphasize missed fraud.

B. Increase the XGBoost scale_pos_weight parameter to adjust the balance of positive and negative weights. — Increasing scale_pos_weight makes positive examples more influential in XGBoost's loss, helping the model detect the rare fraudulent class.

C. Increase the XGBoost max_depth parameter because the model is currently underfitting the data. — The confusion matrix does not establish underfitting or prove that deeper trees are needed; extra depth can overfit.

D. Change the XGBoost eval_metric parameter to optimize based on Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC). — Use AUC to evaluate/select models by discrimination rather than majority-class accuracy. Changing eval_metric alone does not alter the training loss or guarantee fewer false negatives.

E. Decrease the XGBoost max_depth parameter because the model is currently overfitting the data. — The stated evidence does not establish overfitting, so decreasing depth is not the direct class-imbalance remedy offered by B and D.

text: A data scientist has developed a machine learning translation model for English to Japanese by using Amazon SageMaker's built-in seq2seq algorithm with 500,000 aligned sentence pairs. While testing with sample sentences, the data scientist finds that the translation quality is reasonable for an example as short as five words. However, the quality becomes unacceptable if the sentence is 100 words long. Which action will resolve the problem?

choices.A: Change preprocessing to use n-grams.
choices.B: Add more nodes to the recurrent neural network (RNN) than the largest sentence's word count.
choices.C: Adjust hyperparameters related to the attention mechanism.
choices.D: Choose a different weight initialization type.

explanation:
Key Concept: Attention lets a sequence decoder access relevant encoder states instead of relying on a single compressed representation.

A. Change preprocessing to use n-grams. — Changing to n-grams does not directly resolve the encoder–decoder difficulty of retaining information over long sentences.

B. Add more nodes to the recurrent neural network (RNN) than the largest sentence's word count. — Hidden-unit count does not need to exceed sentence word count; this rule does not fix long-range alignment.

C. Adjust hyperparameters related to the attention mechanism. — Tuning the attention configuration improves how the decoder uses source positions, directly addressing degradation on longer sentences.

D. Choose a different weight initialization type. — Initialization can affect training, but it does not specifically address the long-input information bottleneck described.

text: A financial company is trying to detect credit card fraud. The company observed that, on average, 2% of credit card transactions were fraudulent. A data scientist trained a classifier on a year's worth of credit card transactions data. The model needs to identify the fraudulent transactions (positives) from the regular ones (negatives). The company's goal is to accurately capture as many positives as possible. Which metrics should the data scientist use to optimize the model? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Specificity
choices.B: False positive rate
choices.C: Accuracy
choices.D: Area under the precision-recall curve
choices.E: True positive rate

explanation:
Key Concept: For a rare positive class, evaluate how many positives are recovered and how reliable positive predictions remain.

A. Specificity — Specificity measures correctly rejected legitimate transactions, not the fraction of fraud cases captured.

B. False positive rate — False-positive rate measures false alarms among negatives, rather than positive-case coverage.

C. Accuracy — A model predicting every transaction as legitimate would already achieve about 98% accuracy while detecting no fraud.

D. Area under the precision-recall curve — PR-AUC summarizes the precision–recall trade-off and is informative when fraudulent examples are rare.

E. True positive rate — True-positive rate is recall: the fraction of actual fraudulent transactions detected by the classifier.

text: A machine learning specialist is developing a proof of concept for government users whose primary concern is security. The specialist is using Amazon SageMaker to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) model for a photo classifier application. The specialist wants to protect the data so that it cannot be accessed and transferred to a remote host by malicious code accidentally installed on the training container. Which action will provide the MOST secure protection?

choices.A: Remove Amazon S3 access permissions from the SageMaker execution role.
choices.B: Encrypt the weights of the CNN model.
choices.C: Encrypt the training and validation dataset.
choices.D: Enable network isolation for training jobs.

explanation:
Key Concept: Container network isolation prevents training code from making network calls that could exfiltrate accessible data.

A. Remove Amazon S3 access permissions from the SageMaker execution role. — Removing S3 permissions may prevent required input/output operations, but does not itself stop every outbound network path from malicious code.

B. Encrypt the weights of the CNN model. — Encrypting model weights does not block a training process from sending the plaintext data it can access to another host.

C. Encrypt the training and validation dataset. — At-rest encryption does not stop exfiltration by a process that legitimately receives decrypted training data.

D. Enable network isolation for training jobs. — Network isolation blocks container network access; SageMaker manages the permitted training input/output transfer outside that isolated container.

text: A company is using Amazon Textract to extract textual data from thousands of scanned text-heavy legal documents daily. The company uses this information to process loan applications automatically. Some of the documents fail business validation and are returned to human reviewers, who investigate the errors. This activity increases the time to process the loan applications. What should the company do to reduce the processing time of loan applications?

choices.A: Configure Amazon Textract to route low-confidence predictions to Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth. Perform a manual review on those words before performing a business validation.
choices.B: Use an Amazon Textract synchronous operation instead of an asynchronous operation.
choices.C: Configure Amazon Textract to route low-confidence predictions to Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I). Perform a manual review on those words before performing a business validation.
choices.D: Use Amazon Rekognition's feature to detect text in an image to extract the data from scanned images. Use this information to process the loan applications.

explanation:
Key Concept: Human review should target uncertain extraction results before those errors propagate into downstream validation.

A. Configure Amazon Textract to route low-confidence predictions to Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth. Perform a manual review on those words before performing a business validation. — Ground Truth creates labeled training datasets; A2I is the integration designed for human review of Textract inference results.

B. Use an Amazon Textract synchronous operation instead of an asynchronous operation. — Switching request mode changes how the operation is called, not the quality of low-confidence extracted fields.

C. Configure Amazon Textract to route low-confidence predictions to Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I). Perform a manual review on those words before performing a business validation. — A2I can route selected low-confidence Textract results to human reviewers before business validation. This is a historical service path with restricted new-customer availability.

D. Use Amazon Rekognition's feature to detect text in an image to extract the data from scanned images. Use this information to process the loan applications. — Rekognition text detection is not a replacement for the document extraction and targeted review workflow needed for these dense scanned documents.

text: A company ingests machine learning (ML) data from web advertising clicks into an Amazon S3 data lake. Click data is added to an Amazon Kinesis data stream by using the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL). The data is loaded into the S3 data lake from the data stream by using an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. As the data volume increases, an ML specialist notices that the rate of data ingested into Amazon S3 is relatively constant. There also is an increasing backlog of data for Kinesis Data Streams and Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest. Which next step is MOST likely to improve the data ingestion rate into Amazon S3?

choices.A: Increase the number of S3 prefixes for the delivery stream to write to.
choices.B: Decrease the retention period for the data stream.
choices.C: Increase the number of shards for the data stream.
choices.D: Add more consumers using the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).

explanation:
Key Concept: Provisioned Kinesis shard count limits aggregate stream throughput and can become the bottleneck before delivery.

A. Increase the number of S3 prefixes for the delivery stream to write to. — More S3 prefixes do not increase the upstream stream's shard throughput, which is the first capacity issue to investigate here.

B. Decrease the retention period for the data stream. — Shorter retention removes the opportunity to replay older data but does not increase write or consumer throughput.

C. Increase the number of shards for the data stream. — Additional shards increase aggregate stream capacity when traffic is distributed appropriately. Verify shard and Firehose metrics to confirm the actual bottleneck.

D. Add more consumers using the Kinesis Client Library (KCL). — Extra consumers do not increase producer write capacity and can compete for shared read throughput.

text: A data scientist must build a custom recommendation model in Amazon SageMaker for an online retail company. Due to the nature of the company's products, customers buy only 4-5 products every 5-10 years. So, the company relies on a steady stream of new customers. When a new customer signs up, the company collects data on the customer's preferences. Below is a sample of the data available to the data scientist. How should the data scientist split the dataset into a training and test set for this use case?

choices.A: Shuffle all interaction data. Split off the last 10% of the interaction data for the test set.
choices.B: Identify the most recent 10% of interactions for each user. Split off these interactions for the test set.
choices.C: Identify the 10% of users with the least interaction data. Split off all interaction data from these users for the test set.
choices.D: Randomly select 10% of the users. Split off all interaction data from these users for the test set.

explanation:
Key Concept: A test set for new-customer recommendations should contain users entirely absent from training.

A. Shuffle all interaction data. Split off the last 10% of the interaction data for the test set. — Random interaction splitting can place the same customer's history in both sets, making evaluation easier than the intended new-user scenario.

B. Identify the most recent 10% of interactions for each user. Split off these interactions for the test set. — Holding out recent interactions tests future behavior for already known users, not generalization to wholly new users.

C. Identify the 10% of users with the least interaction data. Split off all interaction data from these users for the test set. — Selecting only users with few interactions biases the test population rather than taking a representative sample of new users.

D. Randomly select 10% of the users. Split off all interaction data from these users for the test set. — Hold out every interaction for a random user subset, so evaluation measures generalization to unseen customers using their available preference features.

text: A financial services company wants to adopt Amazon SageMaker as its default data science environment. The company's data scientists run machine learning (ML) models on confidential financial data. The company is worried about data egress and wants an ML engineer to secure the environment. Which mechanisms can the ML engineer use to control data egress from SageMaker? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Connect to SageMaker by using a VPC interface endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink.
choices.B: Use SCPs to restrict access to SageMaker.
choices.C: Disable root access on the SageMaker notebook instances.
choices.D: Enable network isolation for training jobs and models.
choices.E: Restrict notebook presigned URLs to specific IPs used by the company.
choices.F: Protect data with encryption at rest and in transit. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage encryption keys.

explanation:
Key Concept: Controlling access paths and isolating container networking reduces opportunities to move confidential data outside the intended environment.

A. Connect to SageMaker by using a VPC interface endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink. — PrivateLink supplies a private API path that can be constrained with endpoint and IAM policies; it must be combined with restrictions on alternate egress paths.

B. Use SCPs to restrict access to SageMaker. — SCPs set permission boundaries but a general restriction on SageMaker access does not specifically implement the required notebook/container egress controls.

C. Disable root access on the SageMaker notebook instances. — Disabling root limits system administration but does not prevent ordinary user code from sending data through permitted network connections.

D. Enable network isolation for training jobs and models. — Network isolation prevents training and inference containers from making network calls, directly restricting their ability to exfiltrate data.

E. Restrict notebook presigned URLs to specific IPs used by the company. — Restricting notebook presigned-URL use to corporate source IPs reduces unauthorized remote access to the notebook and its data.

F. Protect data with encryption at rest and in transit. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage encryption keys. — Encryption protects confidentiality on storage and transport, but an authorized process can still transmit decrypted data unless access and egress are controlled.

text: A company is converting a large number of unstructured paper receipts into images. The company wants to create a model based on natural language processing (NLP) to find relevant entities such as date, location, and notes, as well as some custom entities such as receipt numbers. The company is using optical character recognition (OCR) to extract text for data labeling. However, documents are in different structures and formats, and the company is facing challenges with setting up the manual workflows for each document type. Additionally, the company trained a named entity recognition (NER) model for custom entity detection using a small sample size. This model has a very low confidence score and will require retraining with a large dataset. Which solution for text extraction and entity detection will require the LEAST amount of effort?

choices.A: Extract text from receipt images by using Amazon Textract. Use the Amazon SageMaker BlazingText algorithm to train on the text for entities and custom entities.
choices.B: Extract text from receipt images by using a deep learning OCR model from the AWS Marketplace. Use the NER deep learning model to extract entities.
choices.C: Extract text from receipt images by using Amazon Textract. Use Amazon Comprehend for entity detection, and use Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition for custom entity detection.
choices.D: Extract text from receipt images by using a deep learning OCR model from the AWS Marketplace. Use Amazon Comprehend for entity detection, and use Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition for custom entity detection.

explanation:
Key Concept: OCR extracts text; entity recognition identifies meaningful spans and domain-specific labels within that text.

A. Extract text from receipt images by using Amazon Textract. Use the Amazon SageMaker BlazingText algorithm to train on the text for entities and custom entities. — BlazingText supports word embeddings and text classification, not the proposed turnkey named-entity extraction workflow.

B. Extract text from receipt images by using a deep learning OCR model from the AWS Marketplace. Use the NER deep learning model to extract entities. — A marketplace OCR model and custom NER model require selection, hosting, and retraining work compared with managed document/NLP services.

C. Extract text from receipt images by using Amazon Textract. Use Amazon Comprehend for entity detection, and use Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition for custom entity detection. — Textract supplies managed OCR, while Comprehend's standard and custom entity recognition address general and receipt-specific entities with less custom infrastructure.

D. Extract text from receipt images by using a deep learning OCR model from the AWS Marketplace. Use Amazon Comprehend for entity detection, and use Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition for custom entity detection. — Replacing managed Textract with a separately selected OCR model adds integration and operation work without a stated need.

text: A company is building a predictive maintenance model based on machine learning (ML). The data is stored in a fully private Amazon S3 bucket that is encrypted at rest with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) CMKs. An ML specialist must run data preprocessing by using an Amazon SageMaker Processing job that is triggered from code in an Amazon SageMaker notebook. The job should read data from Amazon S3, process it, and upload it back to the same S3 bucket. The preprocessing code is stored in a container image in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The ML specialist needs to grant permissions to ensure a smooth data preprocessing workflow. Which set of actions should the ML specialist take to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs, S3 read and write access to the relevant S3 bucket, and appropriate KMS and ECR permissions. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Create an Amazon SageMaker Processing job from the notebook.
choices.B: Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Create an Amazon SageMaker Processing job with an IAM role that has read and write permissions to the relevant S3 bucket, and appropriate KMS and ECR permissions.
choices.C: Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs and to access Amazon ECR. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Set up both an S3 endpoint and a KMS endpoint in the default VPC. Create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs from the notebook.
choices.D: Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Set up an S3 endpoint in the default VPC. Create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs with the access key and secret key of the IAM user with appropriate KMS and ECR permissions.

explanation:
Key Concept: The caller's permission to create a job is separate from the execution role used by that job to access resources.

A. Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs, S3 read and write access to the relevant S3 bucket, and appropriate KMS and ECR permissions. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Create an Amazon SageMaker Processing job from the notebook. — Permissions attached only to the notebook role are not automatically inherited by a Processing job unless that role is explicitly supplied as its execution role.

B. Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Create an Amazon SageMaker Processing job with an IAM role that has read and write permissions to the relevant S3 bucket, and appropriate KMS and ECR permissions. — The notebook caller creates the job and passes an execution role; that role supplies S3, KMS, and ECR access. The caller also needs iam:PassRole.

C. Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs and to access Amazon ECR. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Set up both an S3 endpoint and a KMS endpoint in the default VPC. Create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs from the notebook. — VPC endpoints provide connectivity, not the missing execution-role authorizations to read, decrypt, and write data.

D. Create an IAM role that has permissions to create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs. Attach the role to the SageMaker notebook instance. Set up an S3 endpoint in the default VPC. Create Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs with the access key and secret key of the IAM user with appropriate KMS and ECR permissions. — Long-lived user keys are not the Processing execution-role mechanism and unnecessarily expose credentials; the proposed permissions also omit required S3 access.

text: A data scientist has been running an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance for a few weeks. During this time, a new version of Jupyter Notebook was released along with additional software updates. The security team mandates that all running SageMaker notebook instances use the latest security and software updates provided by SageMaker. How can the data scientist meet this requirements?

choices.A: Call the CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig API operation
choices.B: Create a new SageMaker notebook instance and mount the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the original instance
choices.C: Stop and then restart the SageMaker notebook instance
choices.D: Call the UpdateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig API operation

explanation:
Key Concept: Managed notebook updates are applied through the SageMaker notebook instance lifecycle.

A. Call the CreateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig API operation — Creating a lifecycle configuration creates a setup script resource; it does not itself update the running managed system software.

B. Create a new SageMaker notebook instance and mount the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the original instance — The service-owned notebook volume is not a customer-managed EBS volume that can simply be detached and mounted onto a new notebook.

C. Stop and then restart the SageMaker notebook instance — Stopping and starting the notebook allows SageMaker to apply the service-provided updated environment while retaining the persistent notebook storage.

D. Call the UpdateNotebookInstanceLifecycleConfig API operation — Editing lifecycle script configuration does not itself refresh the managed notebook's base software image.

text: A library is developing an automatic book-borrowing system that uses Amazon Rekognition. Images of library members' faces are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. When members borrow books, the Amazon Rekognition CompareFaces API operation compares real faces against the stored faces in Amazon S3. The library needs to improve security by making sure that images are encrypted at rest. Also, when the images are used with Amazon Rekognition. they need to be encrypted in transit. The library also must ensure that the images are not used to improve Amazon Rekognition as a service. How should a machine learning specialist architect the solution to satisfy these requirements?

choices.A: Enable server-side encryption on the S3 bucket. Submit an AWS Support ticket to opt out of allowing images to be used for improving the service, and follow the process provided by AWS Support.
choices.B: Switch to using an Amazon Rekognition collection to store the images. Use the IndexFaces and SearchFacesByImage API operations instead of the CompareFaces API operation.
choices.C: Switch to using the AWS GovCloud (US) Region for Amazon S3 to store images and for Amazon Rekognition to compare faces. Set up a VPN connection and only call the Amazon Rekognition API operations through the VPN.
choices.D: Enable client-side encryption on the S3 bucket. Set up a VPN connection and only call the Amazon Rekognition API operations through the VPN.

explanation:
Key Concept: Storage encryption, encrypted API transport, and AI-service data-use preferences are distinct controls.

A. Enable server-side encryption on the S3 bucket. Submit an AWS Support ticket to opt out of allowing images to be used for improving the service, and follow the process provided by AWS Support. — Historically, S3 server-side encryption, HTTPS API use, and the Support opt-out process addressed the requirements. Current opt-out management uses AWS Organizations AI services policies.

B. Switch to using an Amazon Rekognition collection to store the images. Use the IndexFaces and SearchFacesByImage API operations instead of the CompareFaces API operation. — A Rekognition collection stores face representations rather than the original image archive and does not replace storage encryption or data-use opt-out controls.

C. Switch to using the AWS GovCloud (US) Region for Amazon S3 to store images and for Amazon Rekognition to compare faces. Set up a VPN connection and only call the Amazon Rekognition API operations through the VPN. — Moving Regions and adding a VPN do not by themselves establish the required storage encryption and service-improvement opt-out settings.

D. Enable client-side encryption on the S3 bucket. Set up a VPN connection and only call the Amazon Rekognition API operations through the VPN. — Client-encrypted image objects are not directly usable as ordinary Rekognition S3 image input, and a VPN does not set the service-improvement opt-out policy.

text: A company is building a line-counting application for use in a quick-service restaurant. The company wants to use video cameras pointed at the line of customers at a given register to measure how many people are in line and deliver notifications to managers if the line grows too long. The restaurant locations have limited bandwidth for connections to external services and cannot accommodate multiple video streams without impacting other operations. Which solution should a machine learning specialist implement to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Install cameras compatible with Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to stream the data to AWS over the restaurant's existing internet connection. Write an AWS Lambda function to take an image and send it to Amazon Rekognition to count the number of faces in the image. Send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long.
choices.B: Deploy AWS DeepLens cameras in the restaurant to capture video. Enable Amazon Rekognition on the AWS DeepLens device, and use it to trigger a local AWS Lambda function when a person is recognized. Use the Lambda function to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long.
choices.C: Build a custom model in Amazon SageMaker to recognize the number of people in an image. Install cameras compatible with Amazon Kinesis Video Streams in the restaurant. Write an AWS Lambda function to take an image. Use the SageMaker endpoint to call the model to count people. Send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long.
choices.D: Build a custom model in Amazon SageMaker to recognize the number of people in an image. Deploy AWS DeepLens cameras in the restaurant. Deploy the model to the cameras. Deploy an AWS Lambda function to the cameras to use the model to count people and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long.

explanation:
Key Concept: Edge inference processes video locally and sends only compact events, reducing bandwidth use.

A. Install cameras compatible with Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to stream the data to AWS over the restaurant's existing internet connection. Write an AWS Lambda function to take an image and send it to Amazon Rekognition to count the number of faces in the image. Send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long. — Streaming every camera feed to AWS conflicts with the stated bandwidth constraint.

B. Deploy AWS DeepLens cameras in the restaurant to capture video. Enable Amazon Rekognition on the AWS DeepLens device, and use it to trigger a local AWS Lambda function when a person is recognized. Use the Lambda function to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long. — Rekognition is a managed cloud API, not a model that can simply be enabled locally on a DeepLens camera as described.

C. Build a custom model in Amazon SageMaker to recognize the number of people in an image. Install cameras compatible with Amazon Kinesis Video Streams in the restaurant. Write an AWS Lambda function to take an image. Use the SageMaker endpoint to call the model to count people. Send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long. — Calling a cloud SageMaker endpoint still requires image transfers from each location and does not provide the proposed local-video processing advantage.

D. Build a custom model in Amazon SageMaker to recognize the number of people in an image. Deploy AWS DeepLens cameras in the restaurant. Deploy the model to the cameras. Deploy an AWS Lambda function to the cameras to use the model to count people and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the line is too long. — In the historical solution, the deployed model and local Lambda count people on the cameras and send alerts. DeepLens is retired; the underlying edge-inference principle remains applicable.

options.B: Rekognition is a managed cloud API, not a model that can simply be enabled locally on a DeepLens camera as described.

text: A company has set up and deployed its machine learning (ML) model into production with an endpoint using Amazon SageMaker hosting services. The ML team has configured automatic scaling for its SageMaker instances to support workload changes. During testing, the team notices that additional instances are being launched before the new instances are ready. This behavior needs to change as soon as possible. How can the ML team solve this issue?

choices.A: Decrease the cooldown period for the scale-in activity. Increase the configured maximum capacity of instances.
choices.B: Replace the current endpoint with a multi-model endpoint using SageMaker.
choices.C: Set up Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to trigger the SageMaker inference endpoint.
choices.D: Increase the cooldown period for the scale-out activity.

explanation:
Key Concept: A scale-out cooldown allows newly added capacity time to become effective before further scaling decisions.

A. Decrease the cooldown period for the scale-in activity. Increase the configured maximum capacity of instances. — Scale-in timing controls removals, not the premature additions described, and raising maximum capacity does not fix the timing.

B. Replace the current endpoint with a multi-model endpoint using SageMaker. — A multi-model endpoint addresses model consolidation, not the cooldown behavior of additional instances.

C. Set up Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to trigger the SageMaker inference endpoint. — An API Gateway/Lambda invocation layer does not change the endpoint autoscaling policy's timing.

D. Increase the cooldown period for the scale-out activity. — Increase the scale-out cooldown to account for provisioning and model startup, reducing repeated additions before new capacity is ready.

text: A telecommunications company is developing a mobile app for its customers. The company is using an Amazon SageMaker hosted endpoint for machine learning model inferences. Developers want to introduce a new version of the model for a limited number of users who subscribed to a preview feature of the app. After the new version of the model is tested as a preview, developers will evaluate its accuracy. If a new version of the model has better accuracy, developers need to be able to gradually release the new version for all users over a fixed period of time. How can the company implement the testing model with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

choices.A: Update the ProductionVariant data type with the new version of the model by using the CreateEndpointConfig operation with the InitialVariantWeight parameter set to 0. Specify the TargetVariant parameter for InvokeEndpoint calls for users who subscribed to the preview feature. When the new version of the model is ready for release, gradually increase InitialVariantWeight until all users have the updated version.
choices.B: Configure two SageMaker hosted endpoints that serve the different versions of the model. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to route traffic to both endpoints based on the TargetVariant query string parameter. Reconfigure the app to send the TargetVariant query string parameter for users who subscribed to the preview feature. When the new version of the model is ready for release, change the ALB's routing algorithm to weighted until all users have the updated version.
choices.C: Update the DesiredWeightsAndCapacity data type with the new version of the model by using the UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities operation with the DesiredWeight parameter set to 0. Specify the TargetVariant parameter for InvokeEndpoint calls for users who subscribed to the preview feature. When the new version of the model is ready for release, gradually increase DesiredWeight until all users have the updated version.
choices.D: Configure two SageMaker hosted endpoints that serve the different versions of the model. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that is configured with a simple routing policy and that points to the current version of the model. Configure the mobile app to use the endpoint URL for users who subscribed to the preview feature and to use the Route 53 record for other users. When the new version of the model is ready for release, add a new model version endpoint to Route 53, and switch the policy to weighted until all users have the updated version.

explanation:
Key Concept: Add a model as an endpoint production variant before routing requests to it or adjusting its traffic weight.

A. Update the ProductionVariant data type with the new version of the model by using the CreateEndpointConfig operation with the InitialVariantWeight parameter set to 0. Specify the TargetVariant parameter for InvokeEndpoint calls for users who subscribed to the preview feature. When the new version of the model is ready for release, gradually increase InitialVariantWeight until all users have the updated version. — Create a configuration containing the new zero-weight variant and update the endpoint. Use TargetVariant for preview users, then gradually increase the variant's live traffic weight.

B. Configure two SageMaker hosted endpoints that serve the different versions of the model. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to route traffic to both endpoints based on the TargetVariant query string parameter. Reconfigure the app to send the TargetVariant query string parameter for users who subscribed to the preview feature. When the new version of the model is ready for release, change the ALB's routing algorithm to weighted until all users have the updated version. — SageMaker's native variant routing avoids a custom ALB architecture, and the asserted direct endpoint/TargetVariant ALB integration is not the intended mechanism.

C. Update the DesiredWeightsAndCapacity data type with the new version of the model by using the UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities operation with the DesiredWeight parameter set to 0. Specify the TargetVariant parameter for InvokeEndpoint calls for users who subscribed to the preview feature. When the new version of the model is ready for release, gradually increase DesiredWeight until all users have the updated version. — UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities changes existing variants; it cannot introduce a new model variant that is absent from the endpoint configuration.

D. Configure two SageMaker hosted endpoints that serve the different versions of the model. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that is configured with a simple routing policy and that points to the current version of the model. Configure the mobile app to use the endpoint URL for users who subscribed to the preview feature and to use the Route 53 record for other users. When the new version of the model is ready for release, add a new model version endpoint to Route 53, and switch the policy to weighted until all users have the updated version. — Separate endpoints and application/DNS routing add management and do not provide the direct per-request TargetVariant control available on one endpoint.

text: A company offers an online shopping service to its customers. The company wants to enhance the site's security by requesting additional information when customers access the site from locations that are different from their normal location. The company wants to update the process to call a machine learning (ML) model to determine when additional information should be requested. The company has several terabytes of data from its existing ecommerce web servers containing the source IP addresses for each request made to the web server. For authenticated requests, the records also contain the login name of the requesting user. Which approach should an ML specialist take to implement the new security feature in the web application?

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label each record as either a successful or failed access attempt. Use Amazon SageMaker to train a binary classification model using the factorization machines (FM) algorithm.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model using the IP Insights algorithm. Schedule updates and retraining of the model using new log data nightly.
choices.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label each record as either a successful or failed access attempt. Use Amazon SageMaker to train a binary classification model using the IP Insights algorithm.
choices.D: Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model using the Object2Vec algorithm. Schedule updates and retraining of the model using new log data nightly.

explanation:
Key Concept: IP Insights learns typical associations between entity identifiers and IP addresses from observed pairs.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label each record as either a successful or failed access attempt. Use Amazon SageMaker to train a binary classification model using the factorization machines (FM) algorithm. — Labeling login success does not directly identify whether a user–IP pairing is unusual, and adds an unnecessary supervised labeling step.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model using the IP Insights algorithm. Schedule updates and retraining of the model using new log data nightly. — IP Insights models user/IP associations without requiring fraud labels; periodic retraining incorporates evolving normal access patterns.

C. Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label each record as either a successful or failed access attempt. Use Amazon SageMaker to train a binary classification model using the IP Insights algorithm. — IP Insights is not configured as the described supervised binary classifier, and successful/failed access labels do not define the desired unusual-location target.

D. Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model using the Object2Vec algorithm. Schedule updates and retraining of the model using new log data nightly. — Object2Vec is a general embedding algorithm; IP Insights is specifically designed for the user–IP association anomaly use case.

options.B: IP Insights models user/IP associations without requiring fraud labels; periodic retraining incorporates evolving normal access patterns.

options.D: Object2Vec is a general embedding algorithm; IP Insights is specifically designed for the user–IP association anomaly use case.

text: A retail company wants to combine its customer orders with the product description data from its product catalog. The structure and format of the records in each dataset is different. A data analyst tried to use a spreadsheet to combine the datasets, but the effort resulted in duplicate records and records that were not properly combined. The company needs a solution that it can use to combine similar records from the two datasets and remove any duplicates. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to process the data. Use two arrays to compare equal strings in the fields from the two datasets and remove any duplicates.
choices.B: Create AWS Glue crawlers for reading and populating the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Call the AWS Glue SearchTables API operation to perform a fuzzy- matching search on the two datasets, and cleanse the data accordingly.
choices.C: Create AWS Glue crawlers for reading and populating the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use the FindMatches transform to cleanse the data.
choices.D: Create an AWS Lake Formation custom transform. Run a transformation for matching products from the Lake Formation console to cleanse the data automatically.

explanation:
Key Concept: Probabilistic record matching handles variations that exact string equality cannot reliably join.

A. Use an AWS Lambda function to process the data. Use two arrays to compare equal strings in the fields from the two datasets and remove any duplicates. — Exact string comparison misses equivalent records with formatting, spelling, or field differences and adds custom matching code.

B. Create AWS Glue crawlers for reading and populating the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Call the AWS Glue SearchTables API operation to perform a fuzzy- matching search on the two datasets, and cleanse the data accordingly. — SearchTables searches catalog metadata; it does not perform fuzzy entity matching on the rows in two datasets.

C. Create AWS Glue crawlers for reading and populating the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use the FindMatches transform to cleanse the data. — After cataloging the sources, a trained FindMatches transform can group corresponding records and remove duplicates despite imperfect field agreement.

D. Create an AWS Lake Formation custom transform. Run a transformation for matching products from the Lake Formation console to cleanse the data automatically. — FindMatches is configured and used through Glue's ML transform workflow; an unspecified console transform does not automatically learn the matching criteria.

options.B: SearchTables searches catalog metadata; it does not perform fuzzy entity matching on the rows in two datasets.
options.C: After cataloging the sources, a trained FindMatches transform can group corresponding records and remove duplicates despite imperfect field agreement.
options.D: FindMatches is configured and used through Glue's ML transform workflow; an unspecified console transform does not automatically learn the matching criteria.

text: A company provisions Amazon SageMaker notebook instances for its data science team and creates Amazon VPC interface endpoints to ensure communication between the VPC and the notebook instances. All connections to the Amazon SageMaker API are contained entirely and securely using the AWS network. However, the data science team realizes that individuals outside the VPC can still connect to the notebook instances across the internet. Which set of actions should the data science team take to fix the issue?

choices.A: Modify the notebook instances' security group to allow traffic only from the CIDR ranges of the VPC. Apply this security group to all of the notebook instances' VPC interfaces.
choices.B: Create an IAM policy that allows the sagemaker:CreatePresignedNotebooklnstanceUrl and sagemaker:DescribeNotebooklnstance actions from only the VPC endpoints. Apply this policy to all IAM users, groups, and roles used to access the notebook instances.
choices.C: Add a NAT gateway to the VPC. Convert all of the subnets where the Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are hosted to private subnets. Stop and start all of the notebook instances to reassign only private IP addresses.
choices.D: Change the network ACL of the subnet the notebook is hosted in to restrict access to anyone outside the VPC.

explanation:
Key Concept: Private API connectivity does not automatically restrict who can generate and use a notebook's browser-access URL.

A. Modify the notebook instances' security group to allow traffic only from the CIDR ranges of the VPC. Apply this security group to all of the notebook instances' VPC interfaces. — Notebook ENI security groups do not control every service-managed browser access path to the notebook.

B. Create an IAM policy that allows the sagemaker:CreatePresignedNotebooklnstanceUrl and sagemaker:DescribeNotebooklnstance actions from only the VPC endpoints. Apply this policy to all IAM users, groups, and roles used to access the notebook instances. — Use IAM conditions for the permitted VPC endpoint on presigned-URL access actions and apply them to all relevant identities, preventing the unrestricted public access path.

C. Add a NAT gateway to the VPC. Convert all of the subnets where the Amazon SageMaker notebook instances are hosted to private subnets. Stop and start all of the notebook instances to reassign only private IP addresses. — A NAT gateway and private subnet address outbound routing, not the authorization of presigned notebook access URLs.

D. Change the network ACL of the subnet the notebook is hosted in to restrict access to anyone outside the VPC. — Subnet NACLs do not replace IAM restrictions on the service-managed notebook URL access mechanism.

text: A company will use Amazon SageMaker to train and host a machine learning (ML) model for a marketing campaign. The majority of data is sensitive customer data. The data must be encrypted at rest. The company wants AWS to maintain the root of trust for the master keys and wants encryption key usage to be logged. Which implementation will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use encryption keys that are stored in AWS Cloud HSM to encrypt the ML data volumes, and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3.
choices.B: Use SageMaker built-in transient keys to encrypt the ML data volumes. Enable default encryption for new Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.
choices.C: Use customer managed keys in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the ML data volumes, and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3.
choices.D: Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to create temporary tokens to encrypt the ML storage volumes, and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3.

explanation:
Key Concept: KMS customer managed keys combine service-managed key protection with configurable policies and auditable key use.

A. Use encryption keys that are stored in AWS Cloud HSM to encrypt the ML data volumes, and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3. — CloudHSM gives the customer more responsibility for HSM and key administration, contrary to the requested AWS-managed root-of-trust approach.

B. Use SageMaker built-in transient keys to encrypt the ML data volumes. Enable default encryption for new Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. — Transient storage encryption and default EBS settings do not supply the requested consistent customer-controlled key-use audit across volumes and S3 artifacts.

C. Use customer managed keys in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the ML data volumes, and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3. — Configure supported SageMaker storage and S3 encryption with customer managed KMS keys, and audit relevant KMS API activity through CloudTrail.

D. Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to create temporary tokens to encrypt the ML storage volumes, and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3. — STS issues temporary authorization credentials; its tokens are not encryption keys for the described storage resources.

text: A machine learning specialist stores IoT soil sensor data in Amazon DynamoDB table and stores weather event data as JSON files in Amazon S3. The dataset in DynamoDB is 10 GB in size and the dataset in Amazon S3 is 5 GB in size. The specialist wants to train a model on this data to help predict soil moisture levels as a function of weather events using Amazon SageMaker. Which solution will accomplish the necessary transformation to train the Amazon SageMaker model with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?

choices.A: Launch an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Hive external table for the DynamoDB table and S3 data. Join the Hive tables and write the results out to Amazon S3.
choices.B: Crawl the data using AWS Glue crawlers. Write an AWS Glue ETL job that merges the two tables and writes the output to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
choices.C: Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the sensor table. Write an AWS Lambda function that consumes the stream and appends the results to the existing weather files in Amazon S3.
choices.D: Crawl the data using AWS Glue crawlers. Write an AWS Glue ETL job that merges the two tables and writes the output in CSV format to Amazon S3.

explanation:
Key Concept: A managed ETL job can join DynamoDB and S3 data and write a training-ready dataset back to S3.

A. Launch an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Hive external table for the DynamoDB table and S3 data. Join the Hive tables and write the results out to Amazon S3. — An EMR Hive solution works but requires more cluster and application administration for this modest-sized join.

B. Crawl the data using AWS Glue crawlers. Write an AWS Glue ETL job that merges the two tables and writes the output to an Amazon Redshift cluster. — Writing the joined dataset to Redshift adds a warehouse and another transfer step instead of producing the intended S3 training input.

C. Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the sensor table. Write an AWS Lambda function that consumes the stream and appends the results to the existing weather files in Amazon S3. — DynamoDB Streams captures changes rather than simply joining the full existing dataset, and S3 objects are not generally appendable files.

D. Crawl the data using AWS Glue crawlers. Write an AWS Glue ETL job that merges the two tables and writes the output in CSV format to Amazon S3. — Glue can discover the sources, perform the join, and write CSV to S3 without maintaining a separate cluster or warehouse.

text: A company sells thousands of products on a public website and wants to automatically identify products with potential durability problems. The company has 1.000 reviews with date, star rating, review text, review summary, and customer email fields, but many reviews are incomplete and have empty fields. Each review has already been labeled with the correct durability result. A machine learning specialist must train a model to identify reviews expressing concerns over product durability. The first model needs to be trained and ready to review in 2 days. What is the MOST direct approach to solve this problem within 2 days?

choices.A: Train a custom classifier by using Amazon Comprehend.
choices.B: Build a recurrent neural network (RNN) in Amazon SageMaker by using Gluon and Apache MXNet.
choices.C: Train a built-in BlazingText model using Word2Vec mode in Amazon SageMaker.
choices.D: Use a built-in seq2seq model in Amazon SageMaker.

explanation:
Key Concept: A managed custom text classifier can learn the supplied durability labels without designing a new neural architecture.

A. Train a custom classifier by using Amazon Comprehend. — Comprehend custom classification uses labeled review text directly and minimizes model-building work for the two-day deadline.

B. Build a recurrent neural network (RNN) in Amazon SageMaker by using Gluon and Apache MXNet. — Developing and tuning a custom RNN adds code and experimentation that the managed classifier avoids.

C. Train a built-in BlazingText model using Word2Vec mode in Amazon SageMaker. — Word2Vec mode learns embeddings, not the supervised durability category classifier required here.

D. Use a built-in seq2seq model in Amazon SageMaker. — seq2seq models map input sequences to output sequences and are not the direct tool for this labeled text classification task.

text: A company that runs an online library is implementing a chatbot using Amazon Lex to provide book recommendations based on category. This intent is fulfilled by an AWS Lambda function that queries an Amazon DynamoDB table for a list of book titles, given a particular category. For testing, there are only three categories implemented as the custom slot types: "comedy," "adventure,` and "documentary.` A machine learning (ML) specialist notices that sometimes the request cannot be fulfilled because Amazon Lex cannot understand the category spoken by users with utterances such as "funny," "fun," and "humor." The ML specialist needs to fix the problem without changing the Lambda code or data in DynamoDB. How should the ML specialist fix the problem?

choices.A: Add the unrecognized words in the enumeration values list as new values in the slot type.
choices.B: Create a new custom slot type, add the unrecognized words to this slot type as enumeration values, and use this slot type for the slot.
choices.C: Use the AMAZON.SearchQuery built-in slot types for custom searches in the database.
choices.D: Add the unrecognized words as synonyms in the custom slot type.

explanation:
Key Concept: Slot synonyms normalize multiple user expressions to the canonical value expected by the fulfillment function.

A. Add the unrecognized words in the enumeration values list as new values in the slot type. — Adding funny and humor as independent values can pass values the existing DynamoDB lookup does not recognize.

B. Create a new custom slot type, add the unrecognized words to this slot type as enumeration values, and use this slot type for the slot. — A replacement slot with independent values still fails to map those expressions to the existing comedy category.

C. Use the AMAZON.SearchQuery built-in slot types for custom searches in the database. — A free-form search slot changes the input contract instead of preserving the existing category lookup without code changes.

D. Add the unrecognized words as synonyms in the custom slot type. — Map funny, fun, and humor as synonyms of comedy so Lex resolves them to the canonical category already handled by Lambda.

text: A manufacturing company uses machine learning (ML) models to detect quality issues. The models use images that are taken of the company's product at the end of each production step. The company has thousands of machines at the production site that generate one image per second on average. The company ran a successful pilot with a single manufacturing machine. For the pilot, ML specialists used an industrial PC that ran AWS IoT Greengrass with a long-running AWS Lambda function that uploaded the images to Amazon S3. The uploaded images invoked a Lambda function that was written in Python to perform inference by using an Amazon SageMaker endpoint that ran a custom model. The inference results were forwarded back to a web service that was hosted at the production site to prevent faulty products from being shipped. The company scaled the solution out to all manufacturing machines by installing similarly configured industrial PCs on each production machine. However, latency for predictions increased beyond acceptable limits. Analysis shows that the internet connection is at its capacity limit. How can the company resolve this issue MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Set up a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the production site and the nearest AWS Region. Use the Direct Connect connection to upload the images. Increase the size of the instances and the number of instances that are used by the SageMaker endpoint.
choices.B: Extend the long-running Lambda function that runs on AWS IoT Greengrass to compress the images and upload the compressed files to Amazon S3. Decompress the files by using a separate Lambda function that invokes the existing Lambda function to run the inference pipeline.
choices.C: Use auto scaling for SageMaker. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the production site and the nearest AWS Region. Use the Direct Connect connection to upload the images.
choices.D: Deploy the Lambda function and the ML models onto the AWS IoT Greengrass core that is running on the industrial PCs that are installed on each machine. Extend the long-running Lambda function that runs on AWS IoT Greengrass to invoke the Lambda function with the captured images and run the inference on the edge component that forwards the results directly to the web service.

explanation:
Key Concept: Moving inference to existing local compute avoids sending every full image over a saturated internet connection.

A. Set up a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the production site and the nearest AWS Region. Use the Direct Connect connection to upload the images. Increase the size of the instances and the number of instances that are used by the SageMaker endpoint. — A large dedicated connection and more cloud GPU capacity add cost while retaining the unnecessary per-image remote processing path.

B. Extend the long-running Lambda function that runs on AWS IoT Greengrass to compress the images and upload the compressed files to Amazon S3. Decompress the files by using a separate Lambda function that invokes the existing Lambda function to run the inference pipeline. — Compression adds processing steps and may affect image quality; it does not remove reliance on the saturated connection for every prediction.

C. Use auto scaling for SageMaker. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the production site and the nearest AWS Region. Use the Direct Connect connection to upload the images. — Autoscaling the endpoint does not fix the network bottleneck, and Direct Connect adds connectivity cost.

D. Deploy the Lambda function and the ML models onto the AWS IoT Greengrass core that is running on the industrial PCs that are installed on each machine. Extend the long-running Lambda function that runs on AWS IoT Greengrass to invoke the Lambda function with the captured images and run the inference on the edge component that forwards the results directly to the web service. — Run the compatible model on the existing Greengrass industrial PCs and send results directly to the local service, eliminating the per-image cloud round trip.

options.B: Compression adds processing steps and may affect image quality; it does not remove reliance on the saturated connection for every prediction.

text: A data scientist is using an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance and needs to securely access data stored in a specific Amazon S3 bucket. How should the data scientist accomplish this?

choices.A: Add an S3 bucket policy allowing GetObject, PutObject, and ListBucket permissions to the Amazon SageMaker notebook ARN as principal.
choices.B: Encrypt the objects in the S3 bucket with a custom AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that only the notebook owner has access to.
choices.C: Attach the policy to the IAM role associated with the notebook that allows GetObject, PutObject, and ListBucket operations to the specific S3 bucket.
choices.D: Use a script in a lifecycle configuration to configure the AWS CLI on the instance with an access key ID and secret.

explanation:
Key Concept: A notebook uses its execution role to obtain temporary AWS permissions for data access.

A. Add an S3 bucket policy allowing GetObject, PutObject, and ListBucket permissions to the Amazon SageMaker notebook ARN as principal. — A notebook resource ARN is not the IAM principal that signs its S3 requests; the associated role is the relevant principal.

B. Encrypt the objects in the S3 bucket with a custom AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that only the notebook owner has access to. — KMS encryption does not grant S3 access, and restricting the key only to an owner may exclude the notebook execution role.

C. Attach the policy to the IAM role associated with the notebook that allows GetObject, PutObject, and ListBucket operations to the specific S3 bucket. — Grant the notebook execution role the required bucket and object permissions, scoped to that bucket and its objects; use only the operations actually needed.

D. Use a script in a lifecycle configuration to configure the AWS CLI on the instance with an access key ID and secret. — Embedding long-lived access keys in a lifecycle script is unnecessary when the notebook already supports an execution role.

text: A company is launching a new product and needs to build a mechanism to monitor comments about the company and its new product on social media. The company needs to be able to evaluate the sentiment expressed in social media posts, and visualize trends and configure alarms based on various thresholds. The company needs to implement this solution quickly, and wants to minimize the infrastructure and data science resources needed to evaluate the messages. The company already has a solution in place to collect posts and store them within an Amazon S3 bucket. What services should the data science team use to deliver this solution?

choices.A: Train a model in Amazon SageMaker by using the BlazingText algorithm to detect sentiment in the corpus of social media posts. Expose an endpoint that can be called by AWS Lambda. Trigger a Lambda function when posts are added to the S3 bucket to invoke the endpoint and record the sentiment in an Amazon DynamoDB table and in a custom Amazon CloudWatch metric. Use CloudWatch alarms to notify analysts of trends.
choices.B: Train a model in Amazon SageMaker by using the semantic segmentation algorithm to model the semantic content in the corpus of social media posts. Expose an endpoint that can be called by AWS Lambda. Trigger a Lambda function when objects are added to the S3 bucket to invoke the endpoint and record the sentiment in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Schedule a second Lambda function to query recently added records and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to notify analysts of trends.
choices.C: Trigger an AWS Lambda function when social media posts are added to the S3 bucket. Call Amazon Comprehend for each post to capture the sentiment in the message and record the sentiment in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Schedule a second Lambda function to query recently added records and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to notify analysts of trends.
choices.D: Trigger an AWS Lambda function when social media posts are added to the S3 bucket. Call Amazon Comprehend for each post to capture the sentiment in the message and record the sentiment in a custom Amazon CloudWatch metric and in S3. Use CloudWatch alarms to notify analysts of trends.

explanation:
Key Concept: Managed sentiment analysis plus metrics and alarms satisfies both inference and threshold-based monitoring needs.

A. Train a model in Amazon SageMaker by using the BlazingText algorithm to detect sentiment in the corpus of social media posts. Expose an endpoint that can be called by AWS Lambda. Trigger a Lambda function when posts are added to the S3 bucket to invoke the endpoint and record the sentiment in an Amazon DynamoDB table and in a custom Amazon CloudWatch metric. Use CloudWatch alarms to notify analysts of trends. — A custom BlazingText classifier requires labeled data, training, and endpoint operation when Comprehend already offers sentiment detection.

B. Train a model in Amazon SageMaker by using the semantic segmentation algorithm to model the semantic content in the corpus of social media posts. Expose an endpoint that can be called by AWS Lambda. Trigger a Lambda function when objects are added to the S3 bucket to invoke the endpoint and record the sentiment in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Schedule a second Lambda function to query recently added records and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to notify analysts of trends. — Semantic segmentation labels image pixels, not sentiment in social-media text.

C. Trigger an AWS Lambda function when social media posts are added to the S3 bucket. Call Amazon Comprehend for each post to capture the sentiment in the message and record the sentiment in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Schedule a second Lambda function to query recently added records and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to notify analysts of trends. — This uses managed sentiment but adds custom scheduled trend detection and does not directly provide the requested metric dashboard/alarm workflow.

D. Trigger an AWS Lambda function when social media posts are added to the S3 bucket. Call Amazon Comprehend for each post to capture the sentiment in the message and record the sentiment in a custom Amazon CloudWatch metric and in S3. Use CloudWatch alarms to notify analysts of trends. — Lambda invokes Comprehend, persists results, and publishes CloudWatch metrics; dashboards and alarms supply trends and threshold notifications with little custom ML work.
