text: A bank wants to launch a low-rate credit promotion. The bank is located in a town that recently experienced economic hardship. Only some of the bank's customers were affected by the crisis, so the bank's credit team must identify which customers to target with the promotion. However, the credit team wants to make sure that loyal customers' full credit history is considered when the decision is made. The bank's data science team developed a model that classifies account transactions and understands credit eligibility. The data science team used the XGBoost algorithm to train the model. The team used 7 years of bank transaction historical data for training and hyperparameter tuning over the course of several days. The accuracy of the model is sufficient, but the credit team is struggling to explain accurately why the model denies credit to some customers. The credit team has almost no skill in data science. What should the data science team do to address this issue in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Studio to rebuild the model. Create a notebook that uses the XGBoost training container to perform model training. Deploy the model at an endpoint. Enable Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to store inferences. Use the inferences to create Shapley values that help explain model behavior. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to explain to the credit team how the features affect the model outcomes.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Studio to rebuild the model. Create a notebook that uses the XGBoost training container to perform model training. Activate Amazon SageMaker Debugger, and configure it to calculate and collect Shapley values. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to explain to the credit team how the features affect the model outcomes.
choices.C: Create an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. Use the notebook instance and the XGBoost library to locally retrain the model. Use the plot_importance() method in the Python XGBoost interface to create a feature importance chart. Use that chart to explain to the credit team how the features affect the model outcomes.
choices.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Studio to rebuild the model. Create a notebook that uses the XGBoost training container to perform model training. Deploy the model at an endpoint. Use Amazon SageMaker Processing to post-analyze the model and create a feature importance explainability chart automatically for the credit team.

explanation:
Key Concept: SHAP values attribute an individual model prediction to its input features.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio to rebuild the model. Create a notebook that uses the XGBoost training container to perform model training. Deploy the model at an endpoint. Enable Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to store inferences. Use the inferences to create Shapley values that help explain model behavior. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to explain to the credit team how the features affect the model outcomes. — Model Monitor captures and evaluates production behavior but does not itself produce the proposed SHAP values without additional computation.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio to rebuild the model. Create a notebook that uses the XGBoost training container to perform model training. Activate Amazon SageMaker Debugger, and configure it to calculate and collect Shapley values. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to explain to the credit team how the features affect the model outcomes. — The supported XGBoost/Debugger integration can collect SHAP contributions, which can be charted to explain how features influence predictions.

C. Create an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. Use the notebook instance and the XGBoost library to locally retrain the model. Use the plot_importance() method in the Python XGBoost interface to create a feature importance chart. Use that chart to explain to the credit team how the features affect the model outcomes. — plot_importance supplies aggregate split-based importance, not the signed per-customer feature contributions needed to explain a particular denial.

D. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio to rebuild the model. Create a notebook that uses the XGBoost training container to perform model training. Deploy the model at an endpoint. text: A data science team is planning to build a natural language processing (NLP) application. The application's text preprocessing stage will include part-of-speech tagging and key phase extraction. text: A machine learning (ML) specialist must develop a classification model for a financial services company. A domain expert provides the dataset, which is tabular with 10,000 rows and 1,020 features. During exploratory data analysis, the specialist finds no missing values and a small percentage of duplicate rows. There are correlation scores of > 0.9 for 200 feature pairs. The mean value of each feature is similar to its 50th percentile. Which feature engineering strategy should the ML specialist use with Amazon SageMaker?

choices.A: Apply dimensionality reduction by using the principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm.
choices.B: Drop the features with low correlation scores by using a Jupyter notebook.
choices.C: Apply anomaly detection by using the Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm.
choices.D: Concatenate the features with high correlation scores by using a Jupyter notebook.

explanation:
Key Concept: Strongly correlated feature pairs suggest redundancy that can be compressed into fewer dimensions.

A. Apply dimensionality reduction by using the principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm. — PCA transforms correlated numeric features into orthogonal components and can reduce the 1,020-column representation before classification.

B. Drop the features with low correlation scores by using a Jupyter notebook. — Low correlation with other features can indicate useful independent information; it does not establish irrelevance to the target.

C. Apply anomaly detection by using the Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm. — RCF detects unusual observations rather than removing redundant feature dimensions.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist is administering a production Amazon SageMaker endpoint with model monitoring configured. Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor detects violations on the SageMaker endpoint, so the ML specialist retrains the model with the latest dataset. This dataset is statistically representative of the current production traffic. The ML specialist notices that even after deploying the new SageMaker model and running the first monitoring job, the SageMaker endpoint still has violations. What should the ML specialist do to resolve the violations?

choices.A: Manually trigger the monitoring job to re-evaluate the SageMaker endpoint traffic sample.
choices.B: Run the Model Monitor baseline job again on the new training set. Configure Model Monitor to use the new baseline.
choices.C: Delete the endpoint and recreate it with the original configuration.
choices.D: Retrain the model again by using a combination of the original training set and the new training set.

explanation:
Key Concept: Data-quality monitoring compares captured production data against a configured baseline, independently of model retraining.

A. Manually trigger the monitoring job to re-evaluate the SageMaker endpoint traffic sample. — Repeating the check against the same stale baseline is likely to report the same distribution differences.

B. Run the Model Monitor baseline job again on the new training set. Configure Model Monitor to use the new baseline. — After validating the new representative training data, generate its baseline statistics/constraints and update the monitoring configuration to use them.

C. Delete the endpoint and recreate it with the original configuration. — Recreating an endpoint with the original monitoring settings preserves the obsolete baseline.

D. Retrain the model again by using a combination of the original training set and the new training set. — Retraining again does not change the monitor's comparison baseline and may unnecessarily reintroduce stale data.

text: A company supplies wholesale clothing to thousands of retail stores. A data scientist must create a model that predicts the daily sales volume for each item for each store. The data scientist discovers that more than half of the stores have been in business for less than 6 months. Sales data is highly consistent from week to week. Daily data from the database has been aggregated weekly, and weeks with no sales are omitted from the current dataset. Five years (100 MB) of sales data is available in Amazon S3. Which factors will adversely impact the performance of the forecast model to be developed, and which actions should the data scientist take to mitigate them? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Detecting seasonality for the majority of stores will be an issue. Request categorical data to relate new stores with similar stores that have more historical data.
choices.B: The sales data does not have enough variance. Request external sales data from other industries to improve the model's ability to generalize.
choices.C: Sales data is aggregated by week. Request daily sales data from the source database to enable building a daily model.
choices.D: The sales data is missing zero entries for item sales. Request that item sales data from the source database include zero entries to enable building the model.
choices.E: Only 100 MB of sales data is available in Amazon S3. Request 10 years of sales data, which would provide 200 MB of training data for the model.

explanation:
Key Concept: Forecast training data must preserve the requested time resolution, genuine zero demand, and relevant history for seasonal patterns.

A. Detecting seasonality for the majority of stores will be an issue. Request categorical data to relate new stores with similar stores that have more historical data. — Store metadata can help share information with young stores, particularly for longer seasonality. This is plausible in addition to the two direct data corrections, making the fixed answer count ambiguous.

B. The sales data does not have enough variance. Request external sales data from other industries to improve the model's ability to generalize. — Consistent sales are not inherently defective data; unrelated industries can introduce distribution mismatch rather than improve generalization.

C. Sales data is aggregated by week. Request daily sales data from the source database to enable building a daily model. — Daily forecasts should be trained from suitable daily observations; weekly aggregation removes within-week information needed for the requested resolution.

D. The sales data is missing zero entries for item sales. Request that item sales data from the source database include zero entries to enable building the model. — Omitting true zero-sales periods biases observed demand upward and obscures the time axis. Restore genuine zeros while distinguishing them from missing observations.

E. Only 100 MB of sales data is available in Amazon S3. Request 10 years of sales data, which would provide 200 MB of training data for the model. — File size alone does not determine forecast quality; doubling megabytes or years is not a justified remedy without considering relevance and seasonality.

choices.B: Use the Amazon Rekognition DetectLabels API to classify the products in the dataset.
choices.C: Augment the images in the dataset. Use open source libraries to crop, resize, flip, rotate, and adjust the brightness and contrast of the images.
choices.D: Use a SageMaker notebook to implement the normalization of pixels and scaling of the images. Store the new dataset in Amazon S3.
choices.E: Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a new model.

explanation:

F. Check whether there are class imbalances in the product categories, and apply oversampling or undersampling as required. Store the new dataset in Amazon S3. — Check class frequencies and rebalance training where needed so underrepresented product categories contribute adequately to learning.

The company needs to ensure that everyone can update their customizations multiple times each hour. Which approach will maximize transcription accuracy during the development phase?

choices.A: Use a voice-driven Amazon Lex bot to perform the ASR customization. Create customer slots within the bot that specifically identify each of the required product names. Use the Amazon Lex synonym mechanism to provide additional variations of each product name as mis-transcriptions are identified in development.
choices.B: Use Amazon Transcribe to perform the ASR customization. Analyze the word confidence scores in the transcript, and automatically create or update a custom vocabulary file with any word that has a confidence score below an acceptable threshold value. Use this updated custom vocabulary file in all future transcription tasks.
choices.C: Create a custom vocabulary file containing each product name with phonetic pronunciations, and use it with Amazon Transcribe to perform the ASR customization. Analyze the transcripts and manually update the custom vocabulary file to include updated or additional entries for those names that are not being correctly identified.
choices.D: Use the audio transcripts to create a training dataset and build an Amazon Transcribe custom language model. Analyze the transcripts and update the training dataset with a manually corrected version of transcripts where product names are not being transcribed correctly. Create an updated custom language model.

explanation:
Key Concept: A curated custom vocabulary targets product names; its supported fields must be distinguished from historical pronunciation features.

A. Use a voice-driven Amazon Lex bot to perform the ASR customization. Create customer slots within the bot that specifically identify each of the required product names. B. Use Amazon Transcribe to perform the ASR customization. Analyze the word confidence scores in the transcript, and automatically create or update a custom vocabulary file with any word that has a confidence score below an acceptable threshold value. Analyze the transcripts and manually update the custom vocabulary file to include updated or additional entries for those names that are not being correctly identified. — Curating the known product names and correcting observed errors is the intended approach. D. Use the audio transcripts to create a training dataset and build an Amazon Transcribe custom language model. Analyze the transcripts and update the training dataset with a manually corrected version of transcripts where product names are not being transcribed correctly. Create an updated custom language model. — A custom language model requires substantially more training text and retraining effort; 4,000 words and several updates per hour favor vocabulary customization.

text: A data scientist is working on a public sector project for an urban traffic system. While studying the traffic patterns, it is clear to the data scientist that the traffic behavior at each light is correlated, subject to a small stochastic error term. The data scientist must model the traffic behavior to analyze the traffic patterns and reduce congestion. How will the data scientist MOST effectively model the problem?

choices.A: The data scientist should obtain a correlated equilibrium policy by formulating this problem as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem.
choices.B: The data scientist should obtain the optimal equilibrium policy by formulating this problem as a single-agent reinforcement learning problem.
choices.C: Rather than finding an equilibrium policy, the data scientist should obtain accurate predictors of traffic flow by using historical data through a supervised learning approach.
choices.D: Rather than finding an equilibrium policy, the data scientist should obtain accurate predictors of traffic flow by using unlabeled simulated data representing the new traffic patterns in the city and applying an unsupervised learning approach.

explanation:
Key Concept: Interacting traffic-control decisions can be modeled as agents whose actions affect one another's outcomes.

A. The data scientist should obtain a correlated equilibrium policy by formulating this problem as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. — A multi-agent formulation represents the interacting traffic lights and can learn coordinated policies aimed at reducing system-wide congestion.

B. The data scientist should obtain the optimal equilibrium policy by formulating this problem as a single-agent reinforcement learning problem. — A single controller is possible in principle, but this option does not directly represent the multiple interacting decision makers emphasized in the question.

C. Rather than finding an equilibrium policy, the data scientist should obtain accurate predictors of traffic flow by using historical data through a supervised learning approach. — Predicting traffic alone does not learn the control policy for coordinating signals to reduce congestion.

D. Rather than finding an equilibrium policy, the data scientist should obtain accurate predictors of traffic flow by using unlabeled simulated data representing the new traffic patterns in the city and applying an unsupervised learning approach. — Unsupervised pattern discovery does not directly optimize sequential signal-control actions or a congestion reward.

text: A data scientist is using the Amazon SageMaker Neural Topic Model (NTM) algorithm to build a model that recommends tags from blog posts. The raw blog post data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in JSON format. During model evaluation, the data scientist discovered that the model recommends certain stopwords such as "a," "an," and "the" as tags to certain blog posts, along with a few rare words that are present only in certain blog entries. After a few iterations of tag review with the content team, the data scientist notices that the rare words are unusual but feasible. The data scientist also must ensure that the tag recommendations of the generated model do not include the stopwords. What should the data scientist do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use the Amazon Comprehend entity recognition API operations. Remove the detected words from the blog post data. Replace the blog post data source in the S3 bucket.
choices.B: Run the SageMaker built-in principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm with the blog post data from the S3 bucket as the data source. Replace the blog post data in the S3 bucket with the results of the training job.
choices.C: Use the SageMaker built-in Object Detection algorithm instead of the NTM algorithm for the training job to process the blog post data.
choices.D: Remove the stopwords from the blog post data by using the CountVectorizer function in the scikit-learn library. Replace the blog post data in the S3 bucket with the results of the vectorizer.

explanation:
Key Concept: Remove explicitly unwanted vocabulary terms before constructing the document-term representation for topic modeling.

A. Use the Amazon Comprehend entity recognition API operations. Remove the detected words from the blog post data. Replace the blog post data source in the S3 bucket. — Entity recognition finds names and other entities, not the exact stopword set that must be excluded from topic tags.

B. Run the SageMaker built-in principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm with the blog post data from the S3 bucket as the data source. Replace the blog post data in the S3 bucket with the results of the training job. — PCA compresses numeric features but does not specifically remove stopwords from a vocabulary.

C. Use the SageMaker built-in Object Detection algorithm instead of the NTM algorithm for the training job to process the blog post data. — Object detection analyzes images rather than extracting topics from blog text.

D. Remove the stopwords from the blog post data by using the CountVectorizer function in the scikit-learn library. Replace the blog post data in the S3 bucket with the results of the vectorizer. — Configure CountVectorizer with the stopword list and a threshold that retains valid rare words, then supply the resulting counts in NTM's supported input format.

text: A company wants to create a data repository in the AWS Cloud for machine learning (ML) projects. The company wants to use AWS to perform complete ML lifecycles and wants to use Amazon S3 for the data storage. All of the company's data currently resides on premises and is 40 [unit unreadable in source] in size. The company wants a solution that can transfer and automatically update data between the on-premises object storage and Amazon S3. The solution must support encryption, scheduling, monitoring, and data integrity validation. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Use the S3 sync command to compare the source S3 bucket and the destination S3 bucket. Determine which source files do not exist in the destination S3 bucket and which source files were modified.
choices.B: Use AWS Transfer for FTPS to transfer the files from the on-premises storage to Amazon S3.
choices.C: Use AWS DataSync to make an initial copy of the entire dataset. Schedule subsequent incremental transfers of changing data until the final cutover from on premises to AWS.
choices.D: Use S3 Batch Operations to pull data periodically from the on-premises storage. Enable S3 Versioning on the S3 bucket to protect against accidental overwrites.

explanation:
Key Concept: A managed data-transfer service can coordinate scheduled incremental copies and verify transfer integrity.

A. Use the S3 sync command to compare the source S3 bucket and the destination S3 bucket. Determine which source files do not exist in the destination S3 bucket and which source files were modified. — An S3-to-S3 sync comparison does not describe the full on-premises object-store transfer, scheduling, monitoring, and verification workflow requested.

B. Use AWS Transfer for FTPS to transfer the files from the on-premises storage to Amazon S3. — An FTPS endpoint enables file transfer but does not itself provide the complete managed incremental synchronization workflow described.

C. Use AWS DataSync to make an initial copy of the entire dataset. Schedule subsequent incremental transfers of changing data until the final cutover from on premises to AWS. — DataSync supports an initial copy followed by scheduled incremental transfers, with encryption, monitoring, and integrity checks for supported storage locations.

D. Use S3 Batch Operations to pull data periodically from the on-premises storage. Enable S3 Versioning on the S3 bucket to protect against accidental overwrites. — S3 Batch Operations acts on S3 objects; it is not a general connector that periodically pulls arbitrary on-premises object storage.

text: A company has video feeds and images of a subway train station. The company wants to create a deep learning model that will alert the station manager if any passenger crosses the yellow safety line when there is no train in the station. The alert will be based on the video feeds. The company wants the model to detect the yellow line, the passengers who cross the yellow line, and the trains in the video feeds. This task requires labeling. The video data must remain confidential. A data scientist creates a bounding box to label the sample data and uses an object detection model. However, the object detection model cannot clearly demarcate the yellow line, the passengers who cross the yellow line, and the trains. Which labeling approach will help the company improve this model?

choices.A: Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to label the dataset and create a custom Amazon Rekognition object detection model. Create a private workforce. Use Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) to review the low-confidence predictions and retrain the custom Amazon Rekognition model.
choices.B: Use an Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth object detection labeling task. Use Amazon Mechanical Turk as the labeling workforce.
choices.C: Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to label the dataset and create a custom Amazon Rekognition object detection model. Create a workforce with a third-party AWS Marketplace vendor. Use Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) to review the low-confidence predictions and retrain the custom Amazon Rekognition model.
choices.D: Use an Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth semantic segmentation labeling task. Use a private workforce as the labeling workforce.

explanation:
Key Concept: Pixel-level segmentation labels describe precise boundaries that bounding boxes cannot.

A. Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to label the dataset and create a custom Amazon Rekognition object detection model. Create a private workforce. Use Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) to review the low-confidence predictions and retrain the custom Amazon Rekognition model. — An object-detection model and human review still rely on bounding boxes, which do not give the required precise line and object boundaries.

B. Use an Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth object detection labeling task. Use Amazon Mechanical Turk as the labeling workforce. — This retains the insufficient bounding-box labeling approach and introduces a public workforce despite the confidentiality requirement.

C. Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to label the dataset and create a custom Amazon Rekognition object detection model. Create a workforce with a third-party AWS Marketplace vendor. Use Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) to review the low-confidence predictions and retrain the custom Amazon Rekognition model. — This adds an external workforce and still proposes object detection instead of the finer segmentation labels needed.

D. Use an Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth semantic segmentation labeling task. Use a private workforce as the labeling workforce. — Ground Truth semantic segmentation supplies pixel masks, while a private workforce limits access to authorized labelers.

text: A data engineer at a bank is evaluating a new tabular dataset that includes customer data. The data engineer will use the customer data to create a new model to predict customer behavior. After creating a correlation matrix for the variables, the data engineer notices that many of the 100 features are highly correlated with each other. Which steps should the data engineer take to address this issue? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use a linear-based algorithm to train the model.
choices.B: Apply principal component analysis (PCA).
choices.C: Remove a portion of highly correlated features from the dataset.
choices.D: Apply min-max feature scaling to the dataset.
choices.E: Apply one-hot encoding category-based variables.

explanation:
Key Concept: Redundant correlated columns can be removed or transformed into a lower-dimensional representation.

A. Use a linear-based algorithm to train the model. — Simply switching to a linear algorithm does not remove collinearity and may expose it more strongly in unstable coefficients.

B. Apply principal component analysis (PCA). — PCA produces orthogonal components that can compress the correlated feature information.

C. Remove a portion of highly correlated features from the dataset. — Removing selected redundant columns reduces dimensionality while retaining representative information from each correlated group.

D. Apply min-max feature scaling to the dataset. — Min-max scaling changes scale but preserves pairwise linear correlations.

E. Apply one-hot encoding category-based variables. — One-hot encoding represents categorical variables and does not solve the stated redundancy among existing correlated features.

text: A company is building a new version of a recommendation engine. Machine learning (ML) specialists need to keep adding new data from users to improve personalized recommendations. The ML specialists gather data from the users' interactions on the platform and from sources such as external websites and social media. The pipeline cleans, transforms, enriches, and compresses terabytes of data daily, and this data is stored in Amazon S3. A set of Python scripts was coded to do the job and is stored in a large Amazon EC2 instance. The whole process takes more than 20 hours to finish, with each script taking at least an hour. The company wants to move the scripts out of Amazon EC2 into a more managed solution that will eliminate the need to maintain servers. Which approach will address all of these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

choices.A: Load the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster. Execute the pipeline by using SQL. Store the results in Amazon S3.
choices.B: Load the data into Amazon DynamoDB. Convert the scripts to an AWS Lambda function. Execute the pipeline by triggering Lambda executions. Store the results in Amazon S3.
choices.C: Create an AWS Glue job. Convert the scripts to PySpark. Execute the pipeline. Store the results in Amazon S3.
choices.D: Create a set of individual AWS Lambda functions to execute each of the scripts. Build a step function by using the AWS Step Functions Data Science SDK. Store the results in Amazon S3.

explanation:
Key Concept: Long-running terabyte-scale data preparation needs distributed processing rather than short-lived function invocations.

A. Load the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster. Execute the pipeline by using SQL. Store the results in Amazon S3. — Rewriting the entire Python pipeline as SQL and loading a warehouse introduces substantial changes and warehouse management.

B. Load the data into Amazon DynamoDB. Convert the scripts to an AWS Lambda function. Execute the pipeline by triggering Lambda executions. Store the results in Amazon S3. — DynamoDB is not a necessary staging store, and the hour-long scripts exceed Lambda's invocation duration limit.

C. Create an AWS Glue job. Convert the scripts to PySpark. Execute the pipeline. Store the results in Amazon S3. — Converting the transformations to Glue PySpark enables managed distributed ETL over S3 without maintaining the current EC2 server.

D. Create a set of individual AWS Lambda functions to execute each of the scripts. Build a step function by using the AWS Step Functions Data Science SDK. Store the results in Amazon S3. — Step Functions coordinates jobs but does not extend an individual Lambda invocation beyond its execution limit; the existing hour-long scripts cannot run unchanged there.

text: A retail company is selling products through a global online marketplace. The company wants to use machine learning (ML) to analyze customer feedback and identify specific areas for improvement. A developer has built a tool that collects customer reviews from the online marketplace and stores them in an Amazon S3 bucket. This process yields a dataset of 40 reviews. A data scientist building the ML models must identify additional sources of data to increase the size of the dataset. Which data sources should the data scientist use to augment the dataset of reviews? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Emails exchanged by customers and the company's customer service agents
choices.B: Social media posts containing the name of the company or its products
choices.C: A publicly available collection of news articles
choices.D: A publicly available collection of customer reviews
choices.E: Product sales revenue figures for the company
choices.F: Instruction manuals for the company's products

explanation:
Key Concept: Useful sentiment training data contains actual customer opinions in a relevant domain.

A. Emails exchanged by customers and the company's customer service agents — Customer-service exchanges contain complaints, praise, and descriptions of product issues, subject to appropriate access and data preparation.

B. Social media posts containing the name of the company or its products — Company/product mentions can contain current opinions and concerns expressed outside the marketplace reviews.

C. A publicly available collection of news articles — A generic news corpus is less directly related to customers' opinions and may introduce a substantial domain mismatch.

D. A publicly available collection of customer reviews — Relevant public review datasets provide additional examples of opinionated product text, after checking label compatibility and domain relevance.

E. Product sales revenue figures for the company — Revenue is a numeric business outcome rather than text expressing what customers liked or disliked.

F. Instruction manuals for the company's products — Instruction manuals describe intended usage, not customers' opinions or satisfaction with the product.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist wants to create a data preparation job that uses a PySpark script with complex window aggregation operations to create data for training and testing. The ML specialist needs to evaluate the impact of the number of features and the sample count on model performance. Which approach should the ML specialist use to determine the ideal data transformations for the model?

choices.A: Add an Amazon SageMaker Debugger hook to the script to capture key metrics. Run the script as an AWS Glue job.
choices.B: Add an Amazon SageMaker Experiments tracker to the script to capture key metrics. Run the script as an AWS Glue job.
choices.C: Add an Amazon SageMaker Debugger hook to the script to capture key parameters. Run the script as a SageMaker processing job.
choices.D: Add an Amazon SageMaker Experiments tracker to the script to capture key parameters. Run the script as a SageMaker processing job.

explanation:
Key Concept: Track data-preparation parameters and resulting model metrics so transformation experiments can be compared reproducibly.

A. Add an Amazon SageMaker Debugger hook to the script to capture key metrics. Run the script as an AWS Glue job. — Debugger targets training tensors and performance diagnostics; it is not the primary experiment registry for feature-count and sample-count comparisons.

B. Add an Amazon SageMaker Experiments tracker to the script to capture key metrics. Run the script as an AWS Glue job. — Glue can execute PySpark, but this option emphasizes metrics rather than explicitly tracking the preparation parameters and SageMaker processing lineage required by the selected workflow.

C. Add an Amazon SageMaker Debugger hook to the script to capture key parameters. Run the script as a SageMaker processing job. — A Processing job fits the execution need, but Debugger is not the tool intended to organize the experiment parameters and outcomes.

D. Add an Amazon SageMaker Experiments tracker to the script to capture key parameters. Run the script as a SageMaker processing job. — Run distributed PySpark preparation in Processing and log feature/sample counts and downstream evaluation metrics with Experiments for comparison.

text: A data scientist has a dataset of machine part images stored in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). The data scientist needs to use Amazon SageMaker to create and train an image classification machine learning model based on this dataset. Because of budget and time constraints, management wants the data scientist to create and train a model with the least number of steps and integration work required. How should the data scientist meet these requirements?

choices.A: Mount the EFS file system to a SageMaker notebook and run a script that copies the data to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Run the SageMaker training job with the FSx for Lustre file system as the data source.
choices.B: Launch a transient Amazon EMR cluster. Configure steps to mount the EFS file system and copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using S3DistCp. Run the SageMaker training job with Amazon S3 as the data source.
choices.C: Mount the EFS file system to an Amazon EC2 instance and use the AWS CLI to copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the SageMaker training job with Amazon S3 as the data source.
choices.D: Run a SageMaker training job with an EFS file system as the data source.

explanation:
Key Concept: SageMaker training can directly access a supported EFS file system through the required VPC configuration.

A. Mount the EFS file system to a SageMaker notebook and run a script that copies the data to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Run the SageMaker training job with the FSx for Lustre file system as the data source. — Copying the data to FSx adds another file system and migration step when EFS is already supported.

B. Launch a transient Amazon EMR cluster. Configure steps to mount the EFS file system and copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using S3DistCp. Run the SageMaker training job with Amazon S3 as the data source. — Creating an EMR cluster just to move the dataset introduces unnecessary infrastructure and copying.

C. Mount the EFS file system to an Amazon EC2 instance and use the AWS CLI to copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the SageMaker training job with Amazon S3 as the data source. — An EC2-mediated S3 copy is unnecessary when the existing EFS source can be mounted for training.

D. Run a SageMaker training job with an EFS file system as the data source. — Use EFS as the training data source, with the appropriate subnet, security groups, and access permissions, avoiding an intermediate migration.

text: A retail company uses a machine learning (ML) model for daily sales forecasting. The company's brand manager reports that the model has provided inaccurate results for the past 3 weeks. At the end of each day, an AWS Glue job consolidates the input data that is used for the forecasting with the actual daily sales data and the predictions of the model. The AWS Glue job stores the data in Amazon S3. The company's ML team is using an Amazon SageMaker Studio notebook to gain an understanding about the source of the model's inaccuracies. What should the ML team do on the SageMaker Studio notebook to visualize the model's degradation MOST accurately?

choices.A: Create a histogram of the daily sales over the last 3 weeks. In addition, create a histogram of the daily sales from before that period.
choices.B: Create a histogram of the model errors over the last 3 weeks. In addition, create a histogram of the model errors from before that period.
choices.C: Create a line chart with the weekly mean absolute error (MAE) of the model.
choices.D: Create a scatter plot of daily sales versus model error for the last 3 weeks. In addition, create a scatter plot of daily sales versus model error from before that period.

explanation:
Key Concept: A time-indexed error metric shows when forecast quality changes and how large the change is.

A. Create a histogram of the daily sales over the last 3 weeks. In addition, create a histogram of the daily sales from before that period. — Sales distributions can change without proving model error; this does not compare predictions with their actual outcomes.

B. Create a histogram of the model errors over the last 3 weeks. In addition, create a histogram of the model errors from before that period. — Error histograms show distribution changes but obscure the ordering and timing of degradation across weeks.

C. Create a line chart with the weekly mean absolute error (MAE) of the model. — A weekly MAE line chart summarizes the magnitude of prediction error over time, making the reported recent deterioration visible.

D. Create a scatter plot of daily sales versus model error for the last 3 weeks. In addition, create a scatter plot of daily sales versus model error from before that period. — Sales-versus-error scatter plots may diagnose error patterns, but they are less direct for showing the week-by-week degradation trajectory.

text: An ecommerce company sends a weekly email newsletter to all of its customers. Management has hired a team of writers to create additional targeted content. A data scientist needs to identify five customer segments based on age, income, and location. The customers' current segmentation is unknown. The data scientist previously built an XGBoost model to predict the likelihood of a customer responding to an email based on age, income, and location. Why does the XGBoost model NOT meet the current requirements, and how can this be fixed?

choices.A: The XGBoost model provides a true/false binary output. Apply principal component analysis (PCA) with five feature dimensions to predict a segment.
choices.B: The XGBoost model provides a true/false binary output. Increase the number of classes the XGBoost model predicts to five classes to predict a segment.
choices.C: The XGBoost model is a supervised machine learning algorithm. Train a k-Nearest-Neighbors (kNN) model with K = 5 on the same dataset to predict a segment.
choices.D: The XGBoost model is a supervised machine learning algorithm. Train a k-means model with K = 5 on the same dataset to predict a segment.

explanation:
Key Concept: Unlabeled customer segmentation is clustering, whereas the existing response model is supervised classification.

A. The XGBoost model provides a true/false binary output. Apply principal component analysis (PCA) with five feature dimensions to predict a segment. — PCA's five dimensions are transformed features, not five customer-segment labels.

B. The XGBoost model provides a true/false binary output. Increase the number of classes the XGBoost model predicts to five classes to predict a segment. — Increasing the class count still requires labeled examples of the five segments, which are unavailable.

C. The XGBoost model is a supervised machine learning algorithm. Train a k-Nearest-Neighbors (kNN) model with K = 5 on the same dataset to predict a segment. — kNN is supervised in this usage; k = 5 denotes neighbors, not five discovered customer groups.

D. The XGBoost model is a supervised machine learning algorithm. Train a k-means model with K = 5 on the same dataset to predict a segment. — k-means with five clusters discovers groups from customer similarity without needing segment labels, after suitable encoding and scaling.

text: A global financial company is using machine learning to automate its loan approval process. The company has a dataset of customer information. The dataset contains some categorical fields, such as customer location by city and housing status. The dataset also includes financial fields in different units, such as account balances in US dollars and monthly interest in US cents. The company's data scientists are using a gradient boosting regression model to infer the credit score for each customer. The model has a training accuracy of 99% and a testing accuracy of 75%. The data scientists want to improve the model's testing accuracy. Which process will improve the testing accuracy the MOST?

choices.A: Use a one-hot encoder for the categorical fields in the dataset. Perform standardization on the financial fields in the dataset. Apply L1 regularization to the data.
choices.B: Use tokenization of the categorical fields in the dataset. Perform binning on the financial fields in the dataset. Remove the outliers in the data by using the z- score.
choices.C: Use a label encoder for the categorical fields in the dataset. Perform L1 regularization on the financial fields in the dataset. Apply L2 regularization to the data.
choices.D: Use a logarithm transformation on the categorical fields in the dataset. Perform binning on the financial fields in the dataset. Use imputation to populate missing values in the dataset.

explanation:
Key Concept: Represent categories sensibly and regularize the fitted model when training performance greatly exceeds test performance.

A. Use a one-hot encoder for the categorical fields in the dataset. Perform standardization on the financial fields in the dataset. Apply L1 regularization to the data. — One-hot encoding avoids arbitrary category order, and an L1 penalty on the model can reduce overfitting. Standardization is not generally necessary for trees, but does not invalidate the option.

explanation:

text: A data scientist is evaluating a GluonTS on Amazon SageMaker DeepAR model. The evaluation metrics on the test set indicate that the coverage score is 0.489 and 0.889 at the 0.5 and 0.9 quantiles, respectively. What can the data scientist reasonably conclude about the distributional forecast related to the test set?

choices.A: The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is poorly calibrated. These scores should be approximately equal to each other at all quantiles.
choices.B: The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is poorly calibrated. These scores should peak at the median and be lower at the tails.
choices.C: The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is correctly calibrated. These scores should always fall below the quantile itself.
choices.D: The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is correctly calibrated. These scores should be approximately equal to the quantile itself.

explanation:
Key Concept: A calibrated quantile forecast has approximately q of the observed outcomes at or below its predicted q-quantile.

A. The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is poorly calibrated. These scores should be approximately equal to each other at all quantiles. — Coverage should increase with the quantile level. Equal coverage at the median and the 90th percentile would indicate a calibration problem.

B. The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is poorly calibrated. These scores should peak at the median and be lower at the tails. — Coverage is a cumulative proportion, not a density. It should not peak at the median and then decline toward the upper tail.

C. The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is correctly calibrated. These scores should always fall below the quantile itself. — The observed values are close to their nominal levels, but good calibration does not require every empirical coverage estimate to fall below its quantile.

D. The coverage scores indicate that the distributional forecast is correctly calibrated. These scores should be approximately equal to the quantile itself. — The coverages 0.489 and 0.889 are close to 0.5 and 0.9. They support approximate calibration at these two quantiles, though they do not prove calibration everywhere.

text: An energy company has wind turbines, weather stations, and solar panels that generate telemetry data. The company wants to perform predictive maintenance on these devices. The devices are in various locations and have unstable internet connectivity. A team of data scientists is using the telemetry data to perform machine learning (ML) to conduct anomaly detection and predict maintenance before the devices start to deteriorate. The team needs a scalable, secure, high-velocity data ingestion mechanism. The team has decided to use Amazon S3 as the data storage location. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.A: Ingest the data by using an HTTP API call to a web server that is hosted on Amazon EC2. Set up EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling configuration behind an Elastic Load Balancer to load the data into Amazon S3.
choices.B: Ingest the data over Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to AWS IoT Core. Set up a rule in AWS IoT Core to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream that is configured to write to an S3 bucket.
choices.C: Ingest the data over Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to AWS IoT Core. Set up a rule in AWS IoT Core to direct all MQTT data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that is configured to write to an S3 bucket.
choices.D: Ingest the data over Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to Amazon Kinesis data stream that is configured to write to an S3 bucket.

explanation:
Key Concept: AWS IoT Core accepts authenticated MQTT device messages and can route them through an IoT rule to Amazon Data Firehose for S3 delivery.

A. Ingest the data by using an HTTP API call to a web server that is hosted on Amazon EC2. Set up EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling configuration behind an Elastic Load Balancer to load the data into Amazon S3. — An EC2 HTTP ingestion tier requires custom device handling, scaling, and S3 delivery logic. It has more operational overhead than managed IoT ingestion.

B. Ingest the data over Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to AWS IoT Core. Set up a rule in AWS IoT Core to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream that is configured to write to an S3 bucket. — This reverses the delivery relationship: Firehose is not used to send records into a Kinesis data stream. A direct IoT rule to Firehose is sufficient.

C. Ingest the data over Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to AWS IoT Core. Set up a rule in AWS IoT Core to direct all MQTT data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that is configured to write to an S3 bucket. — IoT Core supplies MQTT connectivity and device security, while the Firehose rule action delivers buffered records to S3. Devices still need suitable retry or local buffering for outages.

D. Ingest the data over Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to Amazon Kinesis data stream that is configured to write to an S3 bucket. — Kinesis Data Streams does not expose an MQTT broker endpoint. Devices need IoT Core or an adapter before their MQTT messages can enter the ingestion pipeline.

text: A retail company collects customer comments about its products from social media, the company website, and customer call logs. A team of data scientists and engineers wants to find common topics and determine which products the customers are referring to in their comments. The team is using natural language processing (NLP) to build a model to help with this classification. Each product can be classified into multiple categories that the company defines. These categories are related but are not mutually exclusive. For example, if there is mention of "Sample Yogurt" in the document of customer comments, then "Sample Yogurt" should be classified as "yogurt," "snack," and "dairy product." The team is using Amazon Comprehend to train the model and must complete the project as soon as possible. Which functionality of Amazon Comprehend should the team use to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Custom classification with multi-class mode
choices.B: Custom classification with multi-label mode
choices.C: Custom entity recognition
choices.D: Built-in models

explanation:
Key Concept: Multi-label classification allows several nonexclusive category labels on the same document; multi-class classification selects one mutually exclusive class.

A. Custom classification with multi-class mode — Multi-class mode would choose a single class, so it cannot represent yogurt, snack, and dairy product together for the same text.

B. Custom classification with multi-label mode — Multi-label custom classification learns the company's overlapping categories and can assign all applicable labels to a comment.

C. Custom entity recognition — Custom entity recognition locates named spans such as product mentions. It does not replace document classification into several business categories.

D. Built-in models — Built-in models provide predefined capabilities and labels. They do not learn the company's custom overlapping product taxonomy without custom classification.

text: A data engineer is using AWS Glue to create optimized, secure datasets in Amazon S3. The data science team wants the ability to access the ETL scripts directly from Amazon SageMaker notebooks within a VPC. After this setup is complete, the data science team wants the ability to run the AWS Glue job and invoke the SageMaker training job. Which combination of steps should the data engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Create a SageMaker development endpoint in the data science team's VPC.
choices.B: Create an AWS Glue development endpoint in the data science team's VPC.
choices.C: Create SageMaker notebooks by using the AWS Glue development endpoint.
choices.D: Create SageMaker notebooks by using the SageMaker console.
choices.E: Attach a decryption policy to the SageMaker notebooks.
choices.F: Create an IAM policy and an IAM role for the SageMaker notebooks.

explanation:
Key Concept: The historical Glue development-endpoint workflow connected a SageMaker notebook to an interactive Glue environment and used IAM roles for authorized service access.

A. Create a SageMaker development endpoint in the data science team's VPC. — A SageMaker development endpoint is not the Glue development resource used by this workflow. SageMaker hosting endpoints serve models instead.

B. Create an AWS Glue development endpoint in the data science team's VPC. — A Glue development endpoint in the team's VPC supplies the interactive Glue environment described by the historical setup.

C. Create SageMaker notebooks by using the AWS Glue development endpoint. — Creating the notebook through the Glue development-endpoint integration connects it to that Glue environment for ETL development.

D. Create SageMaker notebooks by using the SageMaker console. — A standalone notebook created in the SageMaker console does not by itself configure the specific Glue development-endpoint integration requested here.

E. Attach a decryption policy to the SageMaker notebooks. — A notebook cannot use a free-standing decryption policy as its execution identity. Any required KMS permissions belong in an appropriate IAM policy attached to its role.

F. Create an IAM policy and an IAM role for the SageMaker notebooks. — The notebook needs an IAM role with policies permitting the relevant Glue, SageMaker, S3, and any required KMS operations. Modern implementations should review Glue interactive sessions instead of assuming this legacy setup is current.

text: A data engineer needs to provide a team of data scientists with the appropriate dataset to run machine learning training jobs. The data will be stored in Amazon S3. The data engineer is obtaining the data from an Amazon Redshift database and is using join queries to extract a single tabular dataset. A portion of the schema is as follows: TransactionTimestamp (Timestamp) CardName (Varchar) CardNo (Varchar) The data engineer must provide the data so that any row with a CardNo value of NULL is removed. Also, the TransactionTimestamp column must be separated into a TransactionDate column and a TransactionTime column. Finally, the CardName column must be renamed to NameOnCard. The data will be extracted on a monthly basis and will be loaded into an S3 bucket. The solution must minimize the effort that is needed to set up infrastructure for the ingestion and transformation. The solution also must be automated and must minimize the load on the Amazon Redshift cluster. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Set up an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Spark job to read the data from the Amazon Redshift cluster and transform the data. Load the data into the S3 bucket. Schedule the job to run monthly.
choices.B: Set up an Amazon EC2 instance with a SQL client tool, such as SQL Workbench/J, to query the data from the Amazon Redshift cluster directly Export the resulting dataset into a file. Upload the file into the S3 bucket. Perform these tasks monthly.
choices.C: Set up an AWS Glue job that has the Amazon Redshift cluster as the source and the S3 bucket as the destination. Use the built-in transforms Filter, Map, and RenameField to perform the required transformations. Schedule the job to run monthly.
choices.D: Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to run a query that writes the data directly to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to run the query monthly.

explanation:
Key Concept: A scheduled Glue ETL job provides managed extraction and transformations without maintaining a separate compute cluster.

A. Set up an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Spark job to read the data from the Amazon Redshift cluster and transform the data. Load the data into the S3 bucket. Schedule the job to run monthly. — Spark on EMR can perform the transformations, but creating and operating an EMR cluster adds infrastructure work for a monthly extraction.

B. Set up an Amazon EC2 instance with a SQL client tool, such as SQL Workbench/J, to query the data from the Amazon Redshift cluster directly Export the resulting dataset into a file. Upload the file into the S3 bucket. Perform these tasks monthly. — An EC2 SQL client introduces a host to maintain and a manual export-and-upload workflow. It does not provide the requested managed automation.

C. Set up an AWS Glue job that has the Amazon Redshift cluster as the source and the S3 bucket as the destination. Use the built-in transforms Filter, Map, and RenameField to perform the required transformations. Schedule the job to run monthly. — Glue can extract the Redshift data, filter null card numbers, map the timestamp to date and time, and rename the cardholder field. Processing transformations outside Redshift avoids additional transformation workload there.

D. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to run a query that writes the data directly to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to run the query monthly. — Redshift Spectrum primarily queries external data. Redshift UNLOAD, not a Spectrum query as described, is the normal mechanism for exporting Redshift query results to S3.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist wants to bring a custom training algorithm to Amazon SageMaker. The ML specialist implements the algorithm in a Docker container that is supported by SageMaker. How should the ML specialist package the Docker container so that SageMaker can launch the training correctly?

choices.A: Specify the server argument in the ENTRYPOINT instruction in the Dockerfile.
choices.B: Specify the training program in the ENTRYPOINT instruction in the Dockerfile.
choices.C: Include the path to the training data in the docker build command when packaging the container.
choices.D: Use a COPY instruction in the Dockerfile to copy the training program to the /opt/ml/train directory.

explanation:
Key Concept: SageMaker starts a custom training container using its configured entry point and the training invocation contract.

A. Specify the server argument in the ENTRYPOINT instruction in the Dockerfile. — A serving command launches an inference server, not the training program. It would not implement the training invocation expected by SageMaker.

B. Specify the training program in the ENTRYPOINT instruction in the Dockerfile. — Setting ENTRYPOINT to the training executable makes the container start the intended program when SageMaker launches the training job; the program must also handle SageMaker's invocation arguments.

C. Include the path to the training data in the docker build command when packaging the container. — Training channels are supplied at job runtime. Adding a data path to docker build neither selects the container entry point nor configures those runtime channels.

D. Use a COPY instruction in the Dockerfile to copy the training program to the /opt/ml/train directory. — COPY places a file in the image but does not make it executable at container startup. The container still needs an entry point that launches training.

text: An ecommerce company wants to use machine learning (ML) to monitor fraudulent transactions on its website. The company is using Amazon SageMaker to research, train, deploy, and monitor the ML models. The historical transactions data is in a .csv file that is stored in Amazon S3. The data contains features such as the user's IP address, navigation time, average time on each page, and the number of clicks for each session. There is no label in the data to indicate if a transaction is anomalous. Which models should the company use in combination to detect anomalous transactions? (Choose two.)

choices.A: IP Insights
choices.B: K-nearest neighbors (k-NN)
choices.C: Linear learner with a logistic function
choices.D: Random Cut Forest (RCF)
choices.E: XGBoost

explanation:
Key Concept: Unlabeled fraud signals require unsupervised anomaly detection; anomalous behavior is a review signal rather than proof of fraud.

A. IP Insights — IP Insights learns normal associations between identifiers and IP addresses and flags unusual pairs. The input must include an appropriate entity identifier in addition to the IP address.

B. K-nearest neighbors (k-NN) — The SageMaker built-in k-NN classifier or regressor requires target labels for its supervised prediction task, which this dataset lacks.

C. Linear learner with a logistic function — A logistic linear learner requires labeled normal and fraudulent examples. It cannot directly train that classifier from the unlabeled transactions described.

D. Random Cut Forest (RCF) — RCF assigns anomaly scores to multivariate numeric behavior, such as session duration and click counts, without requiring fraud labels.

E. XGBoost — The proposed XGBoost classifier needs supervised target labels. It does not directly solve the stated unlabeled anomaly-detection task.

text: A healthcare company is using an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance to develop machine learning (ML) models. The company's data scientists will need to be able to access datasets stored in Amazon S3 to train the models. Due to regulatory requirements, access to the data from instances and services used for training must not be transmitted over the internet. Which combination of steps should an ML specialist take to provide this access? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Configure the SageMaker notebook instance to be launched with a VPC attached and internet access disabled.
choices.B: Create and configure a VPN tunnel between SageMaker and Amazon S3.
choices.C: Create and configure an S3 VPC endpoint Attach it to the VPC.
choices.D: Create an S3 bucket policy that allows traffic from the VPC and denies traffic from the internet.
choices.E: Deploy AWS Transit Gateway Attach the S3 bucket and the SageMaker instance to the gateway.

explanation:
Key Concept: A VPC-attached notebook with direct internet access disabled can reach S3 privately through an S3 VPC endpoint.

A. Configure the SageMaker notebook instance to be launched with a VPC attached and internet access disabled. — Attaching the notebook to the VPC and disabling its direct internet path makes its network access follow the configured VPC routes and endpoints.

B. Create and configure a VPN tunnel between SageMaker and Amazon S3. — S3 is not a customer VPN endpoint. A VPN tunnel between a notebook service and an S3 bucket is not the supported private-access mechanism.

C. Create and configure an S3 VPC endpoint Attach it to the VPC. — An S3 VPC endpoint provides the private route needed to access training data without sending that traffic through an internet gateway.

D. Create an S3 bucket policy that allows traffic from the VPC and denies traffic from the internet. — A bucket policy can restrict access using endpoint-related conditions, but it does not create a private network route. The endpoint and notebook networking must be configured first.

E. Deploy AWS Transit Gateway Attach the S3 bucket and the SageMaker instance to the gateway. — An S3 bucket cannot be attached directly to Transit Gateway as described. Transit Gateway does not replace the S3 VPC endpoint.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist at a retail company is forecasting sales for one of the company's stores. The ML specialist is using data from the past 10 years. The company has provided a dataset that includes the total amount of money in sales each day for the store. Approximately 5% of the days are missing sales data. The ML specialist builds a simple forecasting model with the dataset and discovers that the model performs poorly. The performance is poor around the time of seasonal events, when the model consistently predicts sales figures that are too low or too high. Which actions should the ML specialist take to try to improve the model's performance? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Add information about the store's sales periods to the dataset.
choices.B: Aggregate sales figures from stores in the same proximity.
choices.C: Apply smoothing to correct for seasonal variation.
choices.D: Change the forecast frequency from daily to weekly.
choices.E: Replace missing values in the dataset by using linear interpolation.

explanation:
Key Concept: Forecasts can improve when they include known sales-event covariates and use an explicit, validated strategy for missing observations.

A. Add information about the store's sales periods to the dataset. — Sales-period indicators identify promotions or seasonal events that ordinary date patterns may not capture, helping the model account for systematic event-related errors.

B. Aggregate sales figures from stores in the same proximity. — Nearby stores may have different demand patterns. Aggregating their sales changes the target population and does not directly address missing days or this store's event effects.

C. Apply smoothing to correct for seasonal variation. — Smoothing away seasonal variation can remove the very demand signal the forecast must learn. It does not explain event-specific increases or decreases.

D. Change the forecast frequency from daily to weekly. — Weekly aggregation loses the daily detail required by the existing task and can conceal event effects rather than model them.

E. Replace missing values in the dataset by using linear interpolation. — Linear interpolation supplies a plausible baseline for short gaps in the training series. It must be checked against event-driven demand, since interpolated values are estimates rather than observed sales.

text: A company will use Amazon SageMaker to train and host a machine learning model for a marketing campaign. The data must be encrypted at rest. Most of the data is sensitive customer data. The company wants AWS to maintain the root of trust for the encryption keys and wants key usage to be logged. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to create temporary tokens to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3.
choices.B: Use customer managed keys in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3.
choices.C: Use encryption keys stored in AWS CloudHSM to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3.
choices.D: Use SageMaker built-in transient keys to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances. Enable default encryption ffnew Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.

explanation:
Key Concept: AWS KMS integrates managed key protection, service-side encryption, and CloudTrail logging of key API use.

A. Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to create temporary tokens to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3. — STS issues temporary credentials for authorization. Those credentials are not encryption keys for EBS volumes or S3 objects.

B. Use customer managed keys in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3. — Customer managed KMS keys provide policy-controlled encryption for supported SageMaker storage and S3 data, with AWS-managed key infrastructure and auditable key operations.

C. Use encryption keys stored in AWS CloudHSM to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances and to encrypt the model artifacts and data in Amazon S3. — CloudHSM requires managing an HSM cluster and its integration. It adds operational responsibility compared with native SageMaker and S3 integration with KMS.

D. Use SageMaker built-in transient keys to encrypt the storage volumes for all SageMaker instances. Enable default encryption ffnew Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. — Instance-local transient encryption and EBS defaults do not establish a single auditable KMS-based encryption policy for both the relevant SageMaker storage and S3 artifacts.

text: A data scientist is working on a model to predict a company's required inventory stock levels. All historical data is stored in .csv files in the company's data lake on Amazon S3. The dataset consists of approximately 500 GB of data The data scientist wants to use SQL to explore the data before training the model. The company wants to minimize costs. choices.A: Create an Amazon EMR cluster. Create external tables in the Apache Hive metastore, referencing the data that is stored in the S3 bucket. Explore the data from the Hive console.
choices.B: Use AWS Glue to crawl the S3 bucket and create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use Amazon Athena to explore the data.
choices.C: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Use the COPY command to ingest the data from Amazon S3. Explore the data from the Amazon Redshift query editor GUI.
choices.D: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Create external tables in an external schema, referencing the S3 bucket that contains the data. Explore the data from the Amazon Redshift query editor GUI.

explanation:

A. Create an Amazon EMR cluster. Create external tables in the Apache Hive metastore, referencing the data that is stored in the S3 bucket. Explore the data from the Hive console. — Hive on EMR can query the files, but a provisioned cluster adds administration and running costs for exploratory SQL.

B. Use AWS Glue to crawl the S3 bucket and create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use Amazon Athena to explore the data. — A Glue crawler registers the CSV schema, and Athena runs SQL directly against S3. Partitioning and columnar conversion can further reduce the amount scanned.

C. Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Use the COPY command to ingest the data from Amazon S3. Explore the data from the Amazon Redshift query editor GUI. — Loading all data into a new Redshift cluster adds storage, ingestion, and cluster management that are unnecessary for this S3 exploration task.

D. Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Create external tables in an external schema, referencing the S3 bucket that contains the data. Explore the data from the Amazon Redshift query editor GUI. — Redshift external tables avoid copying the data, but this option still provisions a Redshift cluster. text: A geospatial analysis company processes thousands of new satellite images each day to produce vessel detection data for commercial shipping. The company stores the training data in Amazon S3. The training data incrementally increases in size with new images each day. The company has configured an Amazon SageMaker training job to use a single ml.p2.xlarge instance with File input mode to train the built-in Object Detection algorithm. The training process was successful last month but is now failing because of a lack of storage. Aside from the addition of training data, nothing has changed in the model training process. A machine learning (ML) specialist needs to change the training configuration to fix the problem. The solution must optimize performance and must minimize the cost of training. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Modify the training configuration to use two ml.p2.xlarge instances.
choices.B: Modify the training configuration to use Pipe input mode.
choices.C: Modify the training configuration to use a single ml.p3.2xlarge instance.
choices.D: Modify the training configuration to use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) instead of Amazon S3 to store the input training data.

explanation:
Key Concept: Pipe mode streams training input instead of downloading the entire dataset onto the training instance before training begins.

A. Modify the training configuration to use two ml.p2.xlarge instances. — Adding another GPU instance raises cost and does not inherently fix local disk exhaustion, especially if each instance still receives the full input.

B. Modify the training configuration to use Pipe input mode. — Streaming supported Object Detection input through Pipe mode avoids storing the growing dataset in full on the instance and reduces the initial download delay.

C. Modify the training configuration to use a single ml.p3.2xlarge instance. — A more powerful GPU addresses computation, not the demonstrated shortage of input storage. It also increases instance cost without fixing the input strategy.

D. Modify the training configuration to use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) instead of Amazon S3 to store the input training data. — Moving the dataset to EFS introduces another storage system and configuration work. Pipe mode can solve the local-storage problem directly with the existing S3 data.

Audio files from customer calls are located in an on-premises VoIP system that has petabytes of recorded calls. The on-premises infrastructure has high-velocity networking and connects to the company's AWS infrastructure through a VPN connection over a 100 Mbps connection. The company has an algorithm for transcribing customer calls that requires GPUs for inference. The company wants to store these transcriptions in an Amazon S3 bucket in the AWS Cloud for model development. Which solution should an ML specialist use to deliver the transcriptions to the S3 bucket as quickly as possible?

choices.A: Order and use an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized device with an NVIDIA Tesla module to run the transcription algorithm. Use AWS DataSync to send the resulting transcriptions to the transcription S3 bucket.
choices.B: Order and use an AWS Snowcone device with Amazon EC2 Inf1 instances to run the transcription algorithm. Use AWS DataSync to send the resulting transcriptions to the transcription S3 bucket.
choices.C: Order and use AWS Outposts to run the transcription algorithm on GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances. Store the resulting transcriptions in the transcription S3 bucket.
choices.D: Use AWS DataSync to ingest the audio files to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Lambda function to run the transcription algorithm on the audio files when they are uploaded to Amazon S3. Configure the function to write the resulting transcriptions to the transcription S3 bucket.

explanation:
Key Concept: When raw data is much larger than derived results, running GPU inference near the data can avoid a slow bulk transfer. This question describes historical Snow hardware.

A. Order and use an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized device with an NVIDIA Tesla module to run the transcription algorithm. Use AWS DataSync to send the resulting transcriptions to the transcription S3 bucket. — The GPU-equipped Snowball Edge configuration could transcribe the local audio first, allowing only the much smaller text results to cross the 100 Mbps connection.

B. Order and use an AWS Snowcone device with Amazon EC2 Inf1 instances to run the transcription algorithm. Use AWS DataSync to send the resulting transcriptions to the transcription S3 bucket. — Snowcone did not provide the proposed EC2 Inf1 configuration, and Inferentia is not a drop-in GPU for an algorithm that requires GPU execution.

C. Order and use AWS Outposts to run the transcription algorithm on GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances. Store the resulting transcriptions in the transcription S3 bucket. — Outposts introduces substantial installation and infrastructure lead time. Ordering a rack deployment is not the quickest approach to this one-time transcription bottleneck.

D. Use AWS DataSync to ingest the audio files to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Lambda function to run the transcription algorithm on the audio files when they are uploaded to Amazon S3. Configure the function to write the resulting transcriptions to the transcription S3 bucket. — Uploading petabytes over the constrained link is the bottleneck, and Lambda does not provide the GPU runtime required by the transcription algorithm.

text: A company has a podcast platform that has thousands of users. The company has implemented an anomaly detection algorithm to detect low podcast engagement based on a 10-minute running window of user events such as listening, pausing, and exiting the podcast. A machine learning (ML) specialist is designing the data ingestion of these events with the knowledge that the event payload needs some small transformations before inference. How should the ML specialist design the data ingestion to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Ingest event data by using a GraphQLAPI in AWS AppSync. Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use DynamoDB Streams to call an AWS Lambda function to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.
choices.B: Ingest event data by using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Store the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use AWS Glue to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.
choices.C: Ingest event data by using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for Apache Flink application to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.
choices.D: Ingest event data by using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Use an AWS Lambda function to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.

explanation:
Key Concept: Managed Apache Flink applications support stateful stream transformations and time-window aggregations over Kinesis events.

A. Ingest event data by using a GraphQLAPI in AWS AppSync. Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use DynamoDB Streams to call an AWS Lambda function to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — DynamoDB Streams invokes processing for changes, but reconstructing and maintaining each ten-minute window requires additional custom state and query logic.

B. Ingest event data by using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Store the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use AWS Glue to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — Firehose delivery to S3 and Glue batch processing introduce buffering and batch orchestration. They are less direct for continuously maintained ten-minute windows.

C. Ingest event data by using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for Apache Flink application to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — Kinesis ingestion plus a managed Flink application provides built-in windowing and state management for the transformations before anomaly inference. The service is now named Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink.

D. Ingest event data by using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Use an AWS Lambda function to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — MSK with Lambda can process events, but managing the required rolling window and state adds application logic; the proposed solution does not supply Flink's native window semantics.
