text: A company wants to predict the classification of documents that are created from an application. New documents are saved to an Amazon S3 bucket every 3 seconds. The company has developed three versions of a machine learning (ML) model within Amazon SageMaker to classify document text. The company wants to deploy these three versions to predict the classification of each document. Which approach will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are created. Configure the Lambda function to create three SageMaker batch transform jobs, one batch transform job for each model for each document.
choices.B: Deploy all the models to a single SageMaker endpoint. Treat each model as a production variant. Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are created. Configure the Lambda function to call each production variant and return the results of each model.
choices.C: Deploy each model to its own SageMaker endpoint Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are created. Configure the Lambda function to call each endpoint and return the results of each model.
choices.D: Deploy each model to its own SageMaker endpoint. Create three AWS Lambda functions. Configure each Lambda function to call a different endpoint and return the results. Configure three S3 event notifications to invoke the Lambda functions when new documents are created.

explanation:
Key Concept: Production variants place multiple model versions behind one endpoint; TargetVariant selects a particular variant for an invocation.

A. Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are created. Configure the Lambda function to create three SageMaker batch transform jobs, one batch transform job for each model for each document. — Starting three batch jobs for every document incurs repeated provisioning and orchestration overhead, which is unsuitable for arrivals every three seconds.

B. Deploy all the models to a single SageMaker endpoint. Treat each model as a production variant. Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are created. Configure the Lambda function to call each production variant and return the results of each model. — One endpoint can hold all three variants, and the Lambda function can invoke each with TargetVariant. Default weighted routing alone would not return all three predictions.

C. Deploy each model to its own SageMaker endpoint Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are created. Configure the Lambda function to call each endpoint and return the results of each model. — Three separate endpoints can produce the results, but require more endpoint configurations and management than variants on one endpoint.

D. Deploy each model to its own SageMaker endpoint. Create three AWS Lambda functions. Configure each Lambda function to call a different endpoint and return the results. Configure three S3 event notifications to invoke the Lambda functions when new documents are created. — Separate endpoints, functions, and notifications multiply the resources and failure paths. They provide no required benefit over one function invoking three variants.

text: A manufacturing company needs to identify returned smartphones that have been damaged by moisture. The company has an automated process that produces 2,000 diagnostic values for each phone. The database contains more than five million phone evaluations. The evaluation process is consistent, and there are no missing values in the data. A machine learning (ML) specialist has trained an Amazon SageMaker linear learner ML model to classify phones as moisture damaged or not moisture damaged by using all available features. The model's F1 score is 0.6. Which changes in model training would MOST likely improve the model's F1 score? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Continue to use the SageMaker linear learner algorithm. Reduce the number of features with the SageMaker principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm.
choices.B: Continue to use the SageMaker linear learner algorithm. Reduce the number of features with the scikit-learn multi-dimensional scaling (MDS) algorithm.
choices.C: Continue to use the SageMaker linear learner algorithm. Set the predictor type to regressor.
choices.D: Use the SageMaker k-means algorithm with k of less than 1,000 to train the model.
choices.E: Use the SageMaker k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) algorithm. Set a dimension reduction target of less than 1,000 to train the model.

explanation:
Key Concept: Reducing redundant high-dimensional features can improve generalization and neighbor search, but the effect on F1 must be confirmed on held-out labeled data.

A. Continue to use the SageMaker linear learner algorithm. Reduce the number of features with the SageMaker principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm. — PCA can compress correlated diagnostic measurements before linear classification, reducing redundancy and noise. The retained components and resulting F1 need validation.

B. Continue to use the SageMaker linear learner algorithm. Reduce the number of features with the scikit-learn multi-dimensional scaling (MDS) algorithm. — MDS generally relies on pairwise distances and is poorly suited to millions of records compared with the proposed scalable dimension-reduction approaches.

C. Continue to use the SageMaker linear learner algorithm. Set the predictor type to regressor. — Changing to a regressor changes the prediction task to a continuous target. It does not address the binary moisture-damage classification problem.

D. Use the SageMaker k-means algorithm with k of less than 1,000 to train the model. — K-means forms unlabeled clusters. Choosing fewer than 1,000 clusters does not train the required supervised classifier or directly optimize its F1 score.

E. Use the SageMaker k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) algorithm. Set a dimension reduction target of less than 1,000 to train the model. — SageMaker k-NN supports dimensionality reduction, which can make neighbor comparisons more effective in a large feature space. Its nonlinear decision rule is also worth testing against the linear baseline.

text: A company is building a machine learning (ML) model to classify images of plants. An ML specialist has trained the model using the Amazon SageMaker built-in Image Classification algorithm. The model is hosted using a SageMaker endpoint on an ml.m5.xlarge instance for real-time inference. When used by researchers in the field, the inference has greater latency than is acceptable. The latency gets worse when multiple researchers perform inference at the same time on their devices. Using Amazon CloudWatch metrics, the ML specialist notices that the ModelLatency metric shows a high value and is responsible for most of the response latency. The ML specialist needs to fix the performance issue so that researchers can experience less latency when performing inference from their devices. Which action should the ML specialist take to meet this requirement?

choices.A: Change the endpoint instance to an ml.t3 burstable instance with the same vCPU number as the ml.m5.xlarge instance has.
choices.B: Attach an Amazon Elastic Inference ml.eia2.medium accelerator to the endpoint instance.
choices.C: Enable Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to automatically tune performance of the model.
choices.D: Change the endpoint instance to use a memory optimized ML instance.

explanation:
Key Concept: High ModelLatency indicates that model execution, rather than network transit, dominates response time. Elastic Inference was a historical GPU-acceleration option.

A. Change the endpoint instance to an ml.t3 burstable instance with the same vCPU number as the ml.m5.xlarge instance has. — A burstable CPU instance with the same vCPU count does not provide the missing neural-network acceleration and may introduce CPU-credit limits under load.

B. Attach an Amazon Elastic Inference ml.eia2.medium accelerator to the endpoint instance. — Historically, an Elastic Inference accelerator could offload supported image-model operations from the CPU, reducing model execution latency. It is no longer a current deployment choice.

C. Enable Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to automatically tune performance of the model. — Autopilot builds and compares models for supported AutoML tasks. It is not a switch that tunes the runtime of this existing image-classification endpoint.

D. Change the endpoint instance to use a memory optimized ML instance. — More memory only addresses a memory bottleneck. The scenario gives no evidence of memory pressure, while the supported historical accelerator targets neural-network computation.

The models are trained with PyTorch through the use of the Amazon SageMaker SDK. The company wants to reduce the time that is required for performing inferences, given the low latency that is required for self-driving. Which solution should the company use to evaluate and improve the performance of the models?

choices.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch algorithm metrics for visibility into the SageMaker training weights, gradients, biases, and activation outputs. Compute the filter ranks based on this information. Apply pruning to remove the low-ranking filters. Set the new weights. Run a new training job with the pruned model.
choices.B: Use SageMaker Debugger for visibility into the training weights, gradients, biases, and activation outputs. Adjust the model hyperparameters, and look for lower inference times. Run a new training job.
choices.C: Use SageMaker Debugger for visibility into the training weights, gradients, biases, and activation outputs. Compute the filter ranks based on this information. Apply pruning to remove the low-ranking filters. Set the new weights. Run a new training job with the pruned model.
choices.D: Use SageMaker Model Monitor for visibility into the ModelLatency metric and OverheadLatency metric of the model after the model is deployed. Adjust the model hyperparameters, and look for lower inference times. Run a new training job.

explanation:
Key Concept: Structured pruning removes less useful CNN filters, reducing inference computation; captured training tensors can inform which filters to prune.

A. Use Amazon CloudWatch algorithm metrics for visibility into the SageMaker training weights, gradients, biases, and activation outputs. Compute the filter ranks based on this information. Apply pruning to remove the low-ranking filters. Set the new weights. Run a new training job with the pruned model. — Ordinary CloudWatch algorithm metrics do not expose the detailed weight, gradient, and activation tensors needed for the proposed filter analysis.

B. Use SageMaker Debugger for visibility into the training weights, gradients, biases, and activation outputs. Adjust the model hyperparameters, and look for lower inference times. Run a new training job. — Debugger supplies useful tensors, but generic hyperparameter adjustment does not explicitly reduce the convolutional computation that drives inference latency.

C. Use SageMaker Debugger for visibility into the training weights, gradients, biases, and activation outputs. Compute the filter ranks based on this information. Apply pruning to remove the low-ranking filters. Set the new weights. Run a new training job with the pruned model. — Debugger can provide tensors for ranking filters. Removing low-value filters and retraining the smaller network can reduce inference work while recovering accuracy; latency must be benchmarked on the target hardware.

D. Use SageMaker Model Monitor for visibility into the ModelLatency metric and OverheadLatency metric of the model after the model is deployed. Adjust the model hyperparameters, and look for lower inference times. Run a new training job. — ModelLatency and OverheadLatency are endpoint performance metrics in CloudWatch. Model Monitor focuses on data and prediction-quality issues, and the option omits a concrete compression method.

text: A company's machine learning (ML) specialist is designing a scalable data storage solution for Amazon SageMaker. The company has an existing TensorFlow-based model that uses a train.py script. The model relies on static training data that is currently stored in TFRecord format. What should the ML specialist do to provide the training data to SageMaker with the LEAST development overhead?

choices.A: Put the TFRecord data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Glue or AWS Lambda to reformat the data to protobuf format and store the data in a second S3 bucket. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the second S3 bucket.
choices.B: Rewrite the train.py script to add a section that converts TFRecord data to protobuf format. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the local path of the data. Ingest the protobuf data instead of the TFRecord data.
choices.C: Use SageMaker script mode, and use train.py unchanged. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the local path of the data without reformatting the training data.
choices.D: Use SageMaker script mode, and use train.py unchanged. Put the TFRecord data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the S3 bucket without reformatting the training data.

explanation:
Key Concept: TensorFlow script mode runs a user training script with managed training infrastructure and supports training channels backed by S3 without converting TFRecord files.

A. Put the TFRecord data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Glue or AWS Lambda to reformat the data to protobuf format and store the data in a second S3 bucket. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the second S3 bucket. — TensorFlow can consume TFRecord data directly. An extra format-conversion pipeline and second bucket add work without addressing a requirement.

B. Rewrite the train.py script to add a section that converts TFRecord data to protobuf format. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the local path of the data. Ingest the protobuf data instead of the TFRecord data. — Rewriting the script for an unnecessary conversion increases development effort. A local path alone also does not provide a scalable remote training data source.

C. Use SageMaker script mode, and use train.py unchanged. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the local path of the data without reformatting the training data. — Keeping TFRecord is appropriate, but pointing a remote training job at a notebook-local path does not make that local data available to its training instances.

D. Use SageMaker script mode, and use train.py unchanged. Put the TFRecord data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Point the SageMaker training invocation to the S3 bucket without reformatting the training data. — S3-backed input channels supply the existing TFRecord dataset to the managed TensorFlow job. The script must already read the configured training-channel path for it to run unchanged.

text: An ecommerce company wants to train a large image classification model with 10,000 classes. The company runs multiple model training iterations and needs to minimize operational overhead and cost. The company also needs to avoid loss of work and model retraining. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create the training jobs as AWS Batch jobs that use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances in a managed compute environment.
choices.B: Use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the training jobs. Use a Spot Instance interruption notice to save a snapshot of the model to Amazon S3 before an instance is terminated.
choices.C: Use AWS Lambda to run the training jobs. Save model weights to Amazon S3.
choices.D: Use managed spot training in Amazon SageMaker. Launch the training jobs with checkpointing enabled.

explanation:
Key Concept: Managed Spot Training reduces compute cost, while periodically saved checkpoints let interrupted training resume from saved state.

A. Create the training jobs as AWS Batch jobs that use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances in a managed compute environment. — Batch can run Spot jobs, but the described job lacks checkpoint and resume handling. Retrying an interrupted job can repeat work from the beginning.

B. Use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the training jobs. Use a Spot Instance interruption notice to save a snapshot of the model to Amazon S3 before an instance is terminated. — Self-managed Spot instances require custom orchestration and interruption handling. Relying only on the short interruption notice is less robust than regularly saving checkpoints.

C. Use AWS Lambda to run the training jobs. Save model weights to Amazon S3. — Lambda has limited execution duration and no GPU instances. It is not suited to long-running training of this large image classifier.

D. Use managed spot training in Amazon SageMaker. Launch the training jobs with checkpointing enabled. — SageMaker manages Spot capacity and checkpoint synchronization. A checkpoint-aware training script can resume after interruption, preserving saved progress while reducing instance cost.

text: A retail company uses a machine learning (ML) model for daily sales forecasting. The model has provided inaccurate results for the past 3 weeks. At the end of each day, an AWS Glue job consolidates the input data that is used for the forecasting with the actual daily sales data and the predictions of the model. The AWS Glue job stores the data in Amazon S3. The company's ML team determines that the inaccuracies are occurring because of a change in the value distributions of the model features. The ML team must implement a solution that will detect when this type of change occurs in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to create a data quality baseline. Confirm that the emit_metrics option is set to Enabled in the baseline constraints file. Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the metric.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to create a model quality baseline. Confirm that the emit_metrics option is set to Enabled in the baseline constraints file. Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the metric.
choices.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to create rules to capture feature values Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the rules.
choices.D: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor Amazon SageMaker endpoints. Analyze logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to check for data drift.

explanation:
Key Concept: Data quality monitoring compares input feature statistics and distributions with a baseline; model quality monitoring evaluates prediction performance against ground truth.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to create a data quality baseline. Confirm that the emit_metrics option is set to Enabled in the baseline constraints file. Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the metric. — A data quality baseline captures expected feature behavior. A monitoring schedule can compare new data with that baseline, emit violation metrics, and trigger a CloudWatch alarm.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to create a model quality baseline. Confirm that the emit_metrics option is set to Enabled in the baseline constraints file. Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the metric. — Model quality monitoring can detect degraded forecast accuracy, but the specified change is in input feature distributions, which data quality monitoring targets directly.

C. Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to create rules to capture feature values Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the rules. — Debugger inspects training behavior and tensors. It is not the managed production-data drift comparison needed for these daily forecast inputs.

D. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor Amazon SageMaker endpoints. Analyze logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to check for data drift. — Standard endpoint metrics describe operational behavior. Detecting feature-distribution drift from logs requires custom calculations that Model Monitor already provides.

text: A company wants to deliver digital car management services to its customers. The company plans to analyze data to predict the likelihood of users changing cars. choices.A: Launch multiple medium-sized instances in a distributed SageMaker Processing job. Use the prebuilt Docker images for Apache Spark to query and plot the relevant data and to export the relevant data from Amazon Redshift to Amazon S3.
choices.B: Launch multiple medium-sized notebook instances with a PySpark kernel in distributed mode. Download the data from Amazon Redshift to the notebook cluster. Query and plot the relevant data. Export the relevant data from the notebook cluster to Amazon S3.
choices.C: Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the Amazon Redshift credentials. From a SageMaker Studio notebook, use the stored credentials to connect to Amazon Redshift with a Python adapter. Use the Python client to query the relevant data and to export the relevant data from Amazon Redshift to Amazon S3.
choices.D: Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the Amazon Redshift credentials. Launch a SageMaker extra-large notebook instance with block storage that is slightly larger than 10 TB. Use the stored credentials to connect to Amazon Redshift with a Python adapter. Download, query, and plot the relevant data. Export the relevant data from the local notebook drive to Amazon S3.
choices.E: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to query and plot the relevant data and to export the relevant data from Amazon Redshift to Amazon S3.

explanation:

A. Launch multiple medium-sized instances in a distributed SageMaker Processing job. Use the Python client to query the relevant data and to export the relevant data from Amazon Redshift to Amazon S3. — Secrets Manager avoids embedding credentials in the notebook. Use the stored credentials to connect to Amazon Redshift with a Python adapter. Download, query, and plot the relevant data. text: A company is building an application that can predict spam email messages based on email text. The company can generate a few thousand human-labeled datasets that contain a list of email messages and a label of "spam" or "not spam" for each email message. A machine learning (ML) specialist wants to use transfer learning with a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model that is trained on English Wikipedia text data. What should the ML specialist do to initialize the model to fine-tune the model with the custom data?

choices.A: Initialize the model with pretrained weights in all layers except the last fully connected layer.
choices.B: Initialize the model with pretrained weights in all layers. Stack a classifier on top of the first output position. Train the classifier with the labeled data.
choices.C: Initialize the model with random weights in all layers. Replace the last fully connected layer with a classifier. Train the classifier with the labeled data.
choices.D: Initialize the model with pretrained weights in all layers. Replace the last fully connected layer with a classifier. Train the classifier with the labeled data.

explanation:
Key Concept: BERT sequence classification usually initializes the encoder from pretrained weights and adds a task-specific classifier over the first token representation. The option wording leaves the treatment of the existing head ambiguous.

A. Initialize the model with pretrained weights in all layers except the last fully connected layer. — Preserving pretrained layers except a task head can be appropriate, but this wording does not specify which final layer is meant or how the BERT sequence representation reaches the classifier.

B. Initialize the model with pretrained weights in all layers. Stack a classifier on top of the first output position. Train the classifier with the labeled data. — A classifier over the first output position describes the usual CLS-token approach. Full fine-tuning normally updates encoder weights as well, so training only the classifier is not a complete description of that process.

C. Initialize the model with random weights in all layers. Replace the last fully connected layer with a classifier. Train the classifier with the labeled data. — Randomly initializing every layer discards the knowledge learned from Wikipedia and defeats the stated transfer-learning goal.

D. Initialize the model with pretrained weights in all layers. Replace the last fully connected layer with a classifier. Train the classifier with the labeled data. — Replacing a pretrained task-specific head while retaining the encoder is also a legitimate interpretation. The missing distinction between encoder and head prevents an unambiguous single answer.

text: A finance company needs to forecast the price of a commodity. The company has compiled a dataset of historical daily prices. A data scientist must train various forecasting models on 80% of the dataset and must validate the efficacy of those models on the remaining 20% of the dataset. How should the data scientist split the dataset into a training dataset and a validation dataset to compare model performance?

choices.A: Pick a date so that 80% of the data points precede the date. Assign that group of data points as the training dataset. Assign all the remaining data points to the validation dataset.
choices.B: Pick a date so that 80% of the data points occur after the date. Assign that group of data points as the training dataset. Assign all the remaining data points to the validation dataset.
choices.C: Starting from the earliest date in the dataset, pick eight data points for the training dataset and two data points for the validation dataset. Repeat this stratified sampling until no data points remain.
choices.D: Sample data points randomly without replacement so that 80% of the data points are in the training dataset. Assign all the remaining data points to the validation dataset.

explanation:
Key Concept: Forecast validation must mimic predicting future observations from past data, preserving chronological order across the split.

A. Pick a date so that 80% of the data points precede the date. Assign that group of data points as the training dataset. Assign all the remaining data points to the validation dataset. — Training on the earliest 80% and validating on the latest 20% evaluates performance on unseen future periods without training on later prices.

B. Pick a date so that 80% of the data points occur after the date. Assign that group of data points as the training dataset. Assign all the remaining data points to the validation dataset. — Training on later observations and validating on earlier ones reverses the real forecasting direction and can leak information from the future.

C. Starting from the earliest date in the dataset, pick eight data points for the training dataset and two data points for the validation dataset. Repeat this stratified sampling until no data points remain. — Interleaving training and validation points across the series allows later training observations to inform predictions for earlier validation dates.

D. Sample data points randomly without replacement so that 80% of the data points are in the training dataset. Assign all the remaining data points to the validation dataset. — A random split mixes past and future observations. It can produce overly optimistic results when prices and market conditions are temporally dependent.

Exclude the items that the user previously purchased from the results before sending the results back to the web application.

text: A bank wants to use a machine learning (ML) model to predict if users will default on credit card payments. The training data consists of 30,000 labeled records and is evenly balanced between two categories. For the model, an ML specialist selects the Amazon SageMaker built-in XGBoost algorithm and configures a SageMaker automatic hyperparameter optimization job with the Bayesian method. The ML specialist uses the validation accuracy as the objective metric. When the bank implements the solution with this model, the prediction accuracy is 75%. The bank has given the ML specialist 1 day to improve the model in production. Which approach is the FASTEST way to improve the model's accuracy?

choices.A: Run a SageMaker incremental training based on the best candidate from the current model's tuning job. Monitor the same metric that was used as the objective metric in the previous tuning, and look for improvements.
choices.B: Set the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) as the objective metric for a new SageMaker automatic hyperparameter tuning job. Use the same maximum training jobs parameter that was used in the previous tuning job.
choices.C: Run a SageMaker warm start hyperparameter tuning job based on the current model’s tuning job. Use the same objective metric that was used in the previous tuning.
choices.D: Set the F1 score as the objective metric for a new SageMaker automatic hyperparameter tuning job. Double the maximum training jobs parameter that was used in the previous tuning job.

explanation:
Key Concept: Warm-start hyperparameter tuning uses completed tuning results to inform a subsequent search instead of starting without prior observations.

A. Run a SageMaker incremental training based on the best candidate from the current model's tuning job. Monitor the same metric that was used as the objective metric in the previous tuning, and look for improvements. — Continuing model training is different from reusing the hyperparameter search. More training iterations alone may not improve the validation accuracy or find a better configuration.

B. Set the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) as the objective metric for a new SageMaker automatic hyperparameter tuning job. Use the same maximum training jobs parameter that was used in the previous tuning job. — Changing the objective to AUC optimizes ranking across thresholds rather than the requested accuracy. Starting a fresh search also discards the direct warm-start opportunity.

C. Run a SageMaker warm start hyperparameter tuning job based on the current model’s tuning job. Use the same objective metric that was used in the previous tuning. — A warm-start tuning job can exploit the existing search history while retaining the comparable validation-accuracy objective. It is the fastest reuse strategy offered, though improvement is not guaranteed.

D. Set the F1 score as the objective metric for a new SageMaker automatic hyperparameter tuning job. Double the maximum training jobs parameter that was used in the previous tuning job. — A new F1 objective and twice as many trials increase the search work and change the optimization target. Neither directly meets the one-day accuracy-improvement constraint.

text: A company is building a pipeline that periodically retrains its machine learning (ML) models by using new streaming data from devices. The company's data engineering team wants to build a data ingestion system that has high throughput, durable storage, and scalability. The company can tolerate up to 5 minutes of latency for data ingestion. The company needs a solution that can apply basic data transformation during the ingestion process. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.A: Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to automatically consume the Kinesis data stream, transform the data with an AWS Lambda function, and save the output into an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.B: Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by S3 event notifications to transform the data and load the data into an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to automatically consume the Kinesis data stream and load the output back into the S3 bucket.
choices.C: Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Glue job that is invoked by S3 event notifications to read the data, transform the data, and load the output into a new S3 bucket.
choices.D: Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure an AWS Glue job that connects to the delivery stream to transform the data and load the output into an Amazon S3 bucket.

explanation:
Key Concept: Kinesis Data Streams provides durable stream ingestion, while Firehose buffers, optionally transforms, and delivers records to destinations such as S3.

A. Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to automatically consume the Kinesis data stream, transform the data with an AWS Lambda function, and save the output into an Amazon S3 bucket. — The stream supports scalable ingestion and retention. Firehose can consume it, invoke a Lambda transformation, and deliver to S3 within a suitably configured buffering interval.

B. Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by S3 event notifications to transform the data and load the data into an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to automatically consume the Kinesis data stream and load the output back into the S3 bucket. — Writing to S3, moving through a stream, and then returning to S3 adds an unnecessary round trip and event-processing stages.

C. Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Glue job that is invoked by S3 event notifications to read the data, transform the data, and load the output into a new S3 bucket. — Starting Glue processing from individual S3 arrivals adds batch orchestration and startup overhead. It is less direct for simple continuous ingestion transformations.

D. Configure the devices to send streaming data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure an AWS Glue job that connects to the delivery stream to transform the data and load the output into an Amazon S3 bucket. — A Firehose delivery stream is not a Glue streaming source in the manner described. Firehose's supported Lambda transformation supplies the required basic processing.

text: A retail company is ingesting purchasing records from its network of 20,000 stores to Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. The company uses a small, server-based application in each store to send the data to AWS over the internet. The company uses this data to train a machine learning model that is retrained each day. The company's data science team has identified existing attributes on these records that could be combined to create an improved model. Key Concept: Firehose can invoke a Lambda function on incoming batches to transform records before delivering them to S3.

A. Create an AWS Lambda function that can transform the incoming records. Enable data transformation on the ingestion Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use the Lambda function as the invocation target. — Adding the transformation to the existing delivery stream creates the derived attributes during ingestion without changing software in 20,000 stores or adding a cluster.

B. Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster that runs Apache Spark and includes the transformation logic. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to schedule an AWS Lambda function to launch the cluster each day and transform the records that accumulate in Amazon S3. Deliver the transformed records to Amazon S3. — A daily EMR cluster adds scheduling, cluster lifecycle management, and a second pass over S3 data for a transformation that fits in the ingestion path.

C. Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway in the stores. Update the in-store software to deliver data to the S3 File Gateway. Use a scheduled daily AWS Glue job to transform the data that the S3 File Gateway delivers to Amazon S3. — Installing gateways and changing every store's upload process adds substantial deployment work and does not simplify the existing Firehose pipeline.

D. Launch a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that include the transformation logic. Configure the EC2 instances with a daily cron job to transform the records that accumulate in Amazon S3. Deliver the transformed records to Amazon S3. — An EC2 fleet requires patching, capacity management, scheduling, and failure handling. Managed Firehose transformation avoids those responsibilities.

text: A sports broadcasting company is planning to introduce subtitles in multiple languages for a live broadcast. The commentary is in English. The company needs the transcriptions to appear on screen in French or Spanish, depending on the broadcasting country. The transcriptions must be able to capture domain-specific terminology, names, and locations based on the commentary context. The company needs a solution that can support options to provide tuning data. Which combination of AWS services and features will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Amazon Transcribe with custom vocabularies
choices.B: Amazon Transcribe with custom language models
choices.C: Amazon SageMaker Seq2Seq
choices.D: Amazon SageMaker with Hugging Face Speech2Text
choices.E: Amazon Translate

explanation:
Key Concept: Custom language models use domain text to improve contextual speech recognition; translation converts the resulting English text to the broadcast language.

A. Amazon Transcribe with custom vocabularies — Custom vocabularies help recognize particular words and names, but do not learn domain usage and context from training and tuning text as custom language models do.

B. Amazon Transcribe with custom language models — A custom language model can learn sports terminology in context from supplied text. The selected English locale and streaming feature combination must support that model.

C. Amazon SageMaker Seq2Seq — Training and hosting a Seq2Seq model introduces model-development work for capabilities available through managed transcription and translation services.

D. Amazon SageMaker with Hugging Face Speech2Text — A custom Speech2Text deployment requires selecting, tuning, and operating the model. It has more overhead than the supported Transcribe language-model workflow.

E. Amazon Translate — Translate converts the English transcript into French or Spanish. It complements speech recognition; it does not itself transcribe the live audio.

text: A data scientist at a retail company is forecasting sales for a product over the next 3 months. After preliminary analysis, the data scientist identifies that sales are seasonal and that holidays affect sales. The data scientist also determines that sales of the product are correlated with sales of other products in the same category. The data scientist needs to train a sales forecasting model that incorporates this information. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

choices.A: Use Amazon Forecast with Holidays featurization and the built-in autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) algorithm to train the model.
choices.B: Use Amazon Forecast with Holidays featurization and the built-in DeepAR+ algorithm to train the model.
choices.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Processing to enrich the data with holiday information. Train the model by using the SageMaker DeepAR built-in algorithm.
choices.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Processing to enrich the data with holiday information. Train the model by using the Gluon Time Series (GluonTS) toolkit.

explanation:
Key Concept: Forecast DeepAR+ learned patterns across related time series and could incorporate holiday features. Amazon Forecast is unavailable to new customers, so this is a historical service-selection question.

A. Use Amazon Forecast with Holidays featurization and the built-in autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) algorithm to train the model. — ARIMA models individual series and does not exploit the collection of related product series in the same global-learning manner as DeepAR+.

B. Use Amazon Forecast with Holidays featurization and the built-in DeepAR+ algorithm to train the model. — DeepAR+ combines learning across related products with managed holiday featurization, meeting the stated requirements with less custom preparation in the historical Forecast workflow.

C. Use Amazon SageMaker Processing to enrich the data with holiday information. Train the model by using the SageMaker DeepAR built-in algorithm. — SageMaker DeepAR can model related series, but the team must build and operate the holiday-enrichment and training pipeline itself.

D. Use Amazon SageMaker Processing to enrich the data with holiday information. Train the model by using the Gluon Time Series (GluonTS) toolkit. — GluonTS provides forecasting tools, but requires choosing and configuring a model and implementing feature preparation instead of using Forecast's managed feature workflow.

text: A company is building a predictive maintenance model for its warehouse equipment. The model must predict the probability of failure of all machines in the warehouse. The company has collected 10,000 event samples within 3 months. The event samples include 100 failure cases that are evenly distributed across 50 different machine types. How should the company prepare the data for the model to improve the model's accuracy?

choices.A: Adjust the class weight to account for each machine type.
choices.B: Oversample the failure cases by using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE).
choices.C: Undersample the non-failure events. Stratify the non-failure events by machine type.
choices.D: Undersample the non-failure events by using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE).

explanation:
Key Concept: With only 1% failure events, class imbalance can hide poor failure detection. Resampling must affect training data only and respect meaningful feature and machine-type boundaries.

A. Adjust the class weight to account for each machine type. — The imbalance is between failure and non-failure outcomes, not necessarily among machine types. Weighting machine types does not directly correct that target-class imbalance.

B. Oversample the failure cases by using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). — SMOTE creates synthetic minority-class training examples rather than discarding normal observations. With very few failures per machine type, neighbor selection needs care, and improvement must be judged with failure-sensitive metrics.

C. Undersample the non-failure events. Stratify the non-failure events by machine type. — Undersampling can address imbalance, but discards many normal examples from an already modest dataset. The intended approach preserves those examples while augmenting failures.

D. Undersample the non-failure events by using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). — SMOTE is an oversampling technique for the minority class. It does not perform the proposed undersampling of non-failure records.

text: A company stores its documents in Amazon S3 with no predefined product categories. A data scientist needs to build a machine learning model to categorize the documents for all the company's products. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.A: Build a custom clustering model. Create a Dockerfile and build a Docker image. Register the Docker image in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use the custom image in Amazon SageMaker to generate a trained model.
choices.B: Tokenize the data and transform the data into tabular data. Train an Amazon SageMaker k-means model to generate the product categories.
choices.C: Train an Amazon SageMaker Neural Topic Model (NTM) model to generate the product categories.
choices.D: Train an Amazon SageMaker Blazing Text model to generate the product categories.

explanation:
Key Concept: Topic modeling discovers latent themes in unlabeled documents; business category names can then be assigned by interpreting those themes.

A. Build a custom clustering model. Create a Dockerfile and build a Docker image. Register the Docker image in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use the custom image in Amazon SageMaker to generate a trained model. — A custom containerized clustering model requires implementation and maintenance that the built-in topic-modeling algorithm avoids.

B. Tokenize the data and transform the data into tabular data. Train an Amazon SageMaker k-means model to generate the product categories. — K-means can cluster vectorized text, but requires more explicit representation and clustering choices. NTM directly models document topics from suitable text features.

C. Train an Amazon SageMaker Neural Topic Model (NTM) model to generate the product categories. — NTM learns topics without predefined category labels, making it appropriate for discovering product-related groups. The topics still need interpretation rather than being guaranteed business categories.

D. Train an Amazon SageMaker Blazing Text model to generate the product categories. — BlazingText supports word embeddings and supervised text classification. Its classification mode requires labels, which the company does not yet have.

choices.D: Use Amazon Lookout for Vision.

explanation:

text: A manufacturing company wants to monitor its devices for anomalous behavior. A data scientist has trained an Amazon SageMaker scikit-learn model that classifies a device as normal or anomalous based on its 4-day telemetry. The 4-day telemetry of each device is collected in a separate file and is placed in an Amazon S3 bucket once every hour. The total time to run the model across the telemetry for all devices is 5 minutes. What is the MOST cost-effective solution for the company to use to run the model across the telemetry for all the devices?

choices.A: SageMaker Batch Transform
choices.B: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
choices.C: SageMaker Processing
choices.D: A SageMaker multi-container endpoint

explanation:
Key Concept: Batch Transform runs offline inference over S3 datasets and releases its job resources when the batch completes.

A. SageMaker Batch Transform — The hourly files can be scored in a short batch job without maintaining an endpoint during the long idle interval, matching this periodic offline workload.

B. SageMaker Asynchronous Inference — Asynchronous Inference supports queued requests and can scale down, but adds endpoint and queue configuration for a task that naturally processes a complete hourly batch.

C. SageMaker Processing — Processing can run custom inference code, but requires implementing the scoring workflow that Batch Transform provides for the trained model.

D. A SageMaker multi-container endpoint — A multi-container endpoint is designed for hosted inference and multiple containers. Keeping endpoint capacity for this five-minute hourly batch adds unnecessary cost.

text: A company wants to segment a large group of customers into subgroups based on shared characteristics. The company’s data scientist is planning to use the Amazon SageMaker built-in k-means clustering algorithm for this task. The data scientist needs to determine the optimal number of subgroups (k) to use. Which data visualization approach will MOST accurately determine the optimal value of k?

choices.A: Calculate the principal component analysis (PCA) components. Run the k-means clustering algorithm for a range of k by using only the first two PCA components. For each value of k, create a scatter plot with a different color for each cluster. The optimal value of k is the value where the clusters start to look reasonably separated.
choices.B: Calculate the principal component analysis (PCA) components. Create a line plot of the number of components against the explained variance. The optimal value of k is the number of PCA components after which the curve starts decreasing in a linear fashion.
choices.C: Create a t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) plot for a range of perplexity values. The optimal value of k is the value of perplexity, where the clusters start to look reasonably separated.
choices.D: Run the k-means clustering algorithm for a range of k. For each value of k, calculate the sum of squared errors (SSE). Plot a line chart of the SSE for each value of k. The optimal value of k is the point after which the curve starts decreasing in a linear fashion.

explanation:
Key Concept: The elbow method compares within-cluster squared error across candidate values of k and looks for diminishing improvement from adding clusters.

A. Calculate the principal component analysis (PCA) components. Run the k-means clustering algorithm for a range of k by using only the first two PCA components. For each value of k, create a scatter plot with a different color for each cluster. The optimal value of k is the value where the clusters start to look reasonably separated. — A two-component projection can hide structure present in other dimensions. Visual separation in that projection is subjective and need not identify the best k for the full feature space.

B. Calculate the principal component analysis (PCA) components. Create a line plot of the number of components against the explained variance. The optimal value of k is the number of PCA components after which the curve starts decreasing in a linear fashion. — PCA explained variance helps choose the number of retained dimensions, not the number of k-means clusters.

C. Create a t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) plot for a range of perplexity values. The optimal value of k is the value of perplexity, where the clusters start to look reasonably separated. — t-SNE perplexity controls the neighborhood scale used in visualization. It is not a cluster count and cannot be substituted for k.

D. Run the k-means clustering algorithm for a range of k. For each value of k, calculate the sum of squared errors (SSE). Plot a line chart of the SSE for each value of k. The optimal value of k is the point after which the curve starts decreasing in a linear fashion. — An elbow in the SSE curve identifies a useful tradeoff between compact clusters and extra complexity. It is a heuristic, and some datasets have no clear elbow.

text: A data scientist at a financial services company used Amazon SageMaker to train and deploy a model that predicts loan defaults. The model analyzes new loan applications and predicts the risk of loan default. To train the model, the data scientist manually extracted loan data from a database. The data scientist performed the model training and deployment steps in a Jupyter notebook that is hosted on SageMaker Studio notebooks. The model's prediction accuracy is decreasing over time. Which combination of steps is the MOST operationally efficient way for the data scientist to maintain the model's accuracy? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use SageMaker Pipelines to create an automated workflow that extracts fresh data, trains the model, and deploys a new version of the model.
choices.B: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor with an accuracy threshold to check for model drift. Initiate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm when the threshold is exceeded. Connect the workflow in SageMaker Pipelines with the CloudWatch alarm to automatically initiate retraining.
choices.C: Store the model predictions in Amazon S3. Create a daily SageMaker Processing job that reads the predictions from Amazon S3, checks for changes in model prediction accuracy, and sends an email notification if a significant change is detected.
choices.D: Rerun the steps in the Jupyter notebook that is hosted on SageMaker Studio notebooks to retrain the model and redeploy a new version of the model.
choices.E: Export the training and deployment code from the SageMaker Studio notebooks into a Python script. Package the script into an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task that an AWS Lambda function can initiate.

explanation:
Key Concept: Maintaining predictive quality requires both a ground-truth-based monitor and an automated, validated retraining workflow.

A. Use SageMaker Pipelines to create an automated workflow that extracts fresh data, trains the model, and deploys a new version of the model. — Pipelines can orchestrate fresh data extraction, training, evaluation, and deployment, replacing repeated manual notebook execution.

B. Configure SageMaker Model Monitor with an accuracy threshold to check for model drift. Initiate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm when the threshold is exceeded. Connect the workflow in SageMaker Pipelines with the CloudWatch alarm to automatically initiate retraining. — Model quality monitoring can compare predictions with observed loan outcomes and publish metrics for an alarm. An integration such as EventBridge and Lambda can start the pipeline when accuracy falls below its threshold.

C. Store the model predictions in Amazon S3. Create a daily SageMaker Processing job that reads the predictions from Amazon S3, checks for changes in model prediction accuracy, and sends an email notification if a significant change is detected. — Predictions alone cannot reveal accuracy without actual outcomes. A custom daily checker and email also leave retraining manual and duplicate managed monitoring functionality.

D. Rerun the steps in the Jupyter notebook that is hosted on SageMaker Studio notebooks to retrain the model and redeploy a new version of the model. — Manually rerunning the notebook depends on human intervention and does not provide systematic detection or timely retraining.

E. Export the training and deployment code from the SageMaker Studio notebooks into a Python script. Package the script into an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task that an AWS Lambda function can initiate. — An ECS task can automate a script, but requires custom workflow, monitoring, and deployment handling instead of using ML-specific orchestration.

text: A retail company wants to create a system that can predict sales based on the price of an item. A machine learning (ML) engineer built an initial linear model that resulted in the following residual plot: Which actions should the ML engineer take to improve the accuracy of the predictions in the next phase of model building? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Downsample the data uniformly to reduce the amount of data.
choices.B: Create two different models for different sections of the data.
choices.C: Downsample the data in sections where Price < 50.
choices.D: Offset the input data by a constant value where Price > 50.
choices.E: Examine the input data, and apply non-linear data transformations where appropriate.
choices.F: Use a non-linear model instead of a linear model.

explanation:
Key Concept: A systematic residual trend above a price threshold indicates a relationship the current linear model does not capture; changing the functional form can address it.

A. Downsample the data uniformly to reduce the amount of data. — Uniformly removing observations does not fix the residual pattern and leaves less information for learning the relationship.

B. Create two different models for different sections of the data. — Separate models on either side of the apparent price breakpoint can capture different regimes that a single straight-line model misses.

C. Downsample the data in sections where Price < 50. — The lower-price region already has residuals near zero. Discarding its data does not correct the systematic high-price errors.

D. Offset the input data by a constant value where Price > 50. — A fixed offset shifts predictions but does not correct the changing residual slope above 50. The error grows with price rather than remaining constant.

E. Examine the input data, and apply non-linear data transformations where appropriate. — Inspecting the data and applying suitable nonlinear features or transformations can let the model represent the threshold-dependent relationship; the isolated outlier also merits inspection.

F. Use a non-linear model instead of a linear model. — A nonlinear model can learn the changing response above the breakpoint. Its improvement should be assessed on held-out data rather than assumed from training fit.

text: A data scientist at a food production company wants to use an Amazon SageMaker built-in model to classify different vegetables. The current dataset has many features. The company wants to save on memory costs when the data scientist trains and deploys the model. The company also wants to be able to find similar data points for each test data point. Which algorithm will meet these requirements?

choices.A: K-nearest neighbors (k-NN) with dimension reduction
choices.B: Linear learner with early stopping
choices.C: K-means
choices.D: Principal component analysis (PCA) with the algorithm mode set to random

explanation:
Key Concept: k-NN classifies using nearby training examples, and dimensionality reduction reduces the representation stored and searched for those examples.

A. K-nearest neighbors (k-NN) with dimension reduction — k-NN directly supports neighbor-based classification and identifying similar points. Reducing the feature dimension lowers the memory needed for the neighbor representation.

B. Linear learner with early stopping — Early stopping limits training iterations but does not provide a neighbor index or directly reduce the dimensionality of stored examples.

C. K-means — K-means assigns points to cluster centers. It does not directly provide the requested supervised vegetable classification and nearest-example retrieval.

D. Principal component analysis (PCA) with the algorithm mode set to random — PCA reduces dimensions, but it is not itself a classifier or a nearest-neighbor search algorithm. Another model would still be required.

text: A data scientist is training a large PyTorch model by using Amazon SageMaker. It takes 10 hours on average to train the model on GPU instances. The data scientist suspects that training is not converging and that resource utilization is not optimal. What should the data scientist do to identify and address training issues with the LEAST development effort?

choices.A: Use CPU utilization metrics that are captured in Amazon CloudWatch. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to stop the training job early if low CPU utilization occurs.
choices.B: Use high-resolution custom metrics that are captured in Amazon CloudWatch. Configure an AWS Lambda function to analyze the metrics and to stop the training job early if issues are detected.
choices.C: Use the SageMaker Debugger vanishing_gradient and LowGPUUtilization built-in rules to detect issues and to launch the StopTrainingJob action if issues are detected.
choices.D: Use the SageMaker Debugger confusion and feature_importance_overweight built-in rules to detect issues and to launch the StopTrainingJob action if issues are detected.

explanation:
Key Concept: Debugger rules can detect training pathologies and resource underuse, with configured actions to stop an unproductive training job.

A. Use CPU utilization metrics that are captured in Amazon CloudWatch. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to stop the training job early if low CPU utilization occurs. — Low CPU use can be normal for GPU-bound training. It does not diagnose vanishing gradients or establish that the GPU is underused.

B. Use high-resolution custom metrics that are captured in Amazon CloudWatch. Configure an AWS Lambda function to analyze the metrics and to stop the training job early if issues are detected. — Custom high-resolution metrics and a Lambda analyzer require instrumentation and rule code that the named built-in Debugger rules already provide.

C. Use the SageMaker Debugger vanishing_gradient and LowGPUUtilization built-in rules to detect issues and to launch the StopTrainingJob action if issues are detected. — The vanishing-gradient rule targets a possible convergence problem, while LowGPUUtilization targets wasted GPU capacity. text: A bank wants to launch a low-rate credit promotion campaign. The bank must identify which customers to target with the promotion and wants to make sure that each customer's full credit history is considered when an approval or denial decision is made. The bank's data science team used the XGBoost algorithm to train a classification model based on account transaction features. The data science team deployed the model by using the Amazon SageMaker model hosting service. The accuracy of the model is sufficient, but the data science team wants to be able to explain why the model denies the promotion to some customers. What should the data science team do to meet this requirement in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

choices.A: Create a SageMaker notebook instance. Upload the model artifact to the notebook. Use the plot_importance() method in the Python XGBoost interface to create a feature importance chart for the individual predictions.
choices.B: Retrain the model by using SageMaker Debugger. Configure Debugger to calculate and collect Shapley values. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley. Additive explanations (SHAP) values to explain how the features affect the model outcomes.
choices.C: Set up and run an explainability job powered by SageMaker Clarify to analyze the individual customer data, using the training data as a baseline. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive explanations (SHAP) values to explain how the features affect the model outcomes.
choices.D: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to create Shapley values that help explain model behavior. Store the Shapley values in Amazon S3. Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive explanations (SHAP) values to explain how the features affect the model outcomes.

explanation:
Key Concept: Local SHAP explanations attribute an individual prediction to input features relative to a reference baseline.

A. Create a SageMaker notebook instance. Upload the model artifact to the notebook. Use the plot_importance() method in the Python XGBoost interface to create a feature importance chart for the individual predictions. — XGBoost plot_importance summarizes global split-based importance. It does not explain why one particular customer received a denial.

Additive explanations (SHAP) values to explain how the features affect the model outcomes. — Debugger can support tensor-based analysis in appropriate training workflows, but retraining only to obtain explanations adds work when the deployed model can be explained directly.

Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive explanations (SHAP) values to explain how the features affect the model outcomes. — A Clarify explainability job can evaluate the trained model and compute per-customer SHAP contributions against a suitable baseline without retraining it. Clarify availability must be checked for new AWS customers.

Create a chart that shows features and SHapley Additive explanations (SHAP) values to explain how the features affect the model outcomes. — Model Monitor's explainability monitoring tracks changes in feature attribution. text: A company has hired a data scientist to create a loan risk model. The dataset contains loan amounts and variables such as loan type, region, and other demographic variables. The data scientist wants to use Amazon SageMaker to test bias regarding the loan amount distribution with respect to some of these categorical variables. Which pretraining bias metrics should the data scientist use to check the bias distribution? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Class imbalance
choices.B: Conditional demographic disparity
choices.C: Difference in proportions of labels
choices.D: Jensen-Shannon divergence
choices.E: Kullback-Leibler divergence
choices.F: Total variation distance

explanation:
Key Concept: Distribution distances compare the full distribution of loan amounts across demographic facets, rather than only group sizes or an aggregate positive-outcome rate.

A. Class imbalance — Class imbalance measures how many samples belong to each facet. It does not measure how loan amounts are distributed within those facets.

B. Conditional demographic disparity — Conditional demographic disparity compares outcome proportions while accounting for subgroups. It is not a direct distance between the full loan-amount distributions.

C. Difference in proportions of labels — Difference in proportions of labels summarizes an outcome-rate or continuous-label difference. It does not capture all changes in distribution shape as the selected distance metrics do.

D. Jensen-Shannon divergence — Jensen-Shannon divergence compares each facet's outcome distribution with their mixture, providing a symmetric measure of distributional difference.

E. Kullback-Leibler divergence — Kullback-Leibler divergence measures how one facet's loan-amount distribution differs from another. It is directional and requires care where probabilities are zero.

F. Total variation distance — Total variation distance aggregates probability differences across the outcome distributions, making it useful for comparing loan-amount distributions between facets.

text: A retail company wants to use Amazon Forecast to predict daily stock levels of inventory. The cost of running out of items in stock is much higher for the company than the cost of having excess inventory. The company has millions of data samples for multiple years for thousands of items. The company’s purchasing department needs to predict demand for 30-day cycles for each item to ensure that restocking occurs. A machine learning (ML) specialist wants to use item-related features such as "category," "brand," and "safety stock count." The ML specialist also wants to use a binary time series feature that has "promotion applied?" as its name. Future promotion information is available only for the next 5 days. The ML specialist must choose an algorithm and an evaluation metric for a solution to produce prediction results that will maximize company profit. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Train a model by using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Quantile Loss (wQL) metric at 0.75 (P75).
choices.B: Train a model by using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Absolute Percentage Error (WAPE) metric.
choices.C: Train a model by using the Convolutional Neural Network - Quantile Regression (CNN-QR) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Quantile Loss (wQL) metric at 0.75 (P75).
choices.D: Train a model by using the Convolutional Neural Network - Quantile Regression (CNN-QR) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Absolute Percentage Error (WAPE) metric.

explanation:
Key Concept: CNN-QR supported item metadata and historical covariates without requiring those covariates across the entire future horizon. An upper quantile reflects a greater penalty for underforecasting.

A. Train a model by using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Quantile Loss (wQL) metric at 0.75 (P75). — P75 is directionally appropriate for costly stockouts, but ARIMA does not exploit item metadata and cross-item learning as the proposed CNN-QR model does.

B. Train a model by using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Absolute Percentage Error (WAPE) metric. — ARIMA does not meet the metadata-related modeling needs as well, and WAPE does not express the asymmetric cost of stockouts versus excess inventory.

C. Train a model by using the Convolutional Neural Network - Quantile Regression (CNN-QR) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Quantile Loss (wQL) metric at 0.75 (P75). — CNN-QR can use the item features and past promotion information even though the full 30-day promotion schedule is unavailable. P75 weighted quantile loss favors avoiding underforecasts; the ideal quantile still depends on the actual cost ratio.

D. Train a model by using the Convolutional Neural Network - Quantile Regression (CNN-QR) algorithm. Evaluate the model by using the Weighted Absolute Percentage Error (WAPE) metric. — CNN-QR is suitable for the available features, but WAPE penalizes absolute errors without expressing the higher cost of underpredicting demand. Forecast is a historical choice for customers without existing access.

text: An online retail company wants to develop a natural language processing (NLP) model to improve customer service. A machine learning (ML) specialist is setting up distributed training of a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model on Amazon SageMaker. SageMaker will use eight compute instances for the distributed training. The ML specialist wants to ensure the security of the data during the distributed training. The data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which combination of steps should the ML specialist take to protect the data during the distributed training? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Run distributed training jobs in a private VPC. Enable inter-container traffic encryption.
choices.B: Run distributed training jobs across multiple VPCs. Enable VPC peering.
choices.C: Create an S3 VPC endpoint. Then configure network routes, endpoint policies, and S3 bucket policies.
choices.D: Grant read-only access to SageMaker resources by using an IAM role.
choices.E: Create a NAT gateway. Assign an Elastic IP address for the NAT gateway.
choices.F: Configure an inbound rule to allow traffic from a security group that is associated with the training instances.

explanation:
Key Concept: Secure distributed training combines private data access, authorized inter-instance communication, and encryption of traffic exchanged among training containers.

A. Run distributed training jobs in a private VPC. Enable inter-container traffic encryption. — Private VPC networking controls connectivity, while inter-container traffic encryption protects data exchanged between the eight training instances.

B. Run distributed training jobs across multiple VPCs. Enable VPC peering. — Splitting a training job across multiple VPCs and adding peering does not itself encrypt its traffic and is not the normal single-job VPC configuration.

C. Create an S3 VPC endpoint. Then configure network routes, endpoint policies, and S3 bucket policies. — An S3 VPC endpoint with appropriate routes and policies provides controlled private access to the training data without an internet route.

D. Grant read-only access to SageMaker resources by using an IAM role. — Read-only access to SageMaker resources does not grant the training execution role the specific S3 access it needs or configure secure instance-to-instance communication.

E. Create a NAT gateway. Assign an Elastic IP address for the NAT gateway. — A NAT gateway enables outbound internet access. It is unnecessary for private S3 access through a VPC endpoint and does not secure distributed training traffic.

F. Configure an inbound rule to allow traffic from a security group that is associated with the training instances. — A security-group rule allowing the training instances to communicate with peers in the same group supports distributed coordination while avoiding broad inbound access.

text: An analytics company has an Amazon SageMaker hosted endpoint for an image classification model. The model is a custom-built convolutional neural network (CNN) and uses the PyTorch deep learning framework. The company wants to increase throughput and decrease latency for customers that use the model. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Use Amazon Elastic Inference on the SageMaker hosted endpoint.
choices.B: Retrain the CNN with more layers and a larger dataset.
choices.C: Retrain the CNN with more layers and a smaller dataset.
choices.D: Choose a SageMaker instance type that has multiple GPUs.

explanation:
Key Concept: Inference acceleration can improve neural-network throughput without paying for a large full-GPU host. Elastic Inference was an older implementation of this approach.

A. Use Amazon Elastic Inference on the SageMaker hosted endpoint. — For supported PyTorch models, Elastic Inference historically added fractional GPU acceleration to a SageMaker endpoint. It is no longer an available option for new deployments.

B. Retrain the CNN with more layers and a larger dataset. — More layers generally add inference computation. A larger training dataset may improve accuracy, but does not directly reduce the deployed model's latency.

C. Retrain the CNN with more layers and a smaller dataset. — Adding layers still increases model complexity, and reducing training data does not make the resulting architecture cheaper to execute.

D. Choose a SageMaker instance type that has multiple GPUs. — A multi-GPU instance can be costly and requires a workload that uses its parallel capacity. It is not automatically the most economical way to accelerate this single model.

text: An ecommerce company is collecting structured data and unstructured data from its website, mobile apps, and IoT devices. The data is stored in several databases and Amazon S3 buckets. The company is implementing a scalable repository to store structured data and unstructured data. The company must implement a solution that provides a central data catalog, self-service access to the data, and granular data access policies and encryption to protect the data. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of setup? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Identify the existing data in the databases and S3 buckets. Link the data to AWS Lake Formation.
choices.B: Identify the existing data in the databases and S3 buckets. Link the data to AWS Glue.
choices.C: Run AWS Glue crawlers on the linked data sources to create a central data catalog.
choices.D: Apply granular access policies by using AWS Identity and Access Management (1AM). Configure server-side encryption on each data source.
choices.E: Apply granular access policies and encryption by using AWS Lake Formation.
choices.F: Apply granular access policies and encryption by using AWS Glue.

explanation:
Key Concept: Lake Formation governs an S3 data lake using the Glue Data Catalog, with crawlers for discovery and integration with IAM and KMS for protected access.

A. Identify the existing data in the databases and S3 buckets. Link the data to AWS Lake Formation. — Identifying and registering relevant lake locations places them under Lake Formation governance. Database data may first need an ingestion workflow into the lake.

B. Identify the existing data in the databases and S3 buckets. Link the data to AWS Glue. — Glue connects and catalogs data sources, but linking sources to Glue alone does not provide the requested central fine-grained Lake Formation permissions.

C. Run AWS Glue crawlers on the linked data sources to create a central data catalog. — Glue crawlers discover schemas and populate the shared Data Catalog, making the datasets discoverable through supported analytics tools.

D. Apply granular access policies by using AWS Identity and Access Management (1AM). Configure server-side encryption on each data source. — IAM and storage encryption are necessary foundations, but manually managing each source's permissions does not provide Lake Formation's catalog-level fine-grained governance with the same setup effort.

E. Apply granular access policies and encryption by using AWS Lake Formation. — Lake Formation supplies fine-grained permissions and works with KMS-encrypted lake data and catalog metadata. Encryption must be configured in the underlying supported services; registration alone does not encrypt existing objects.

F. Apply granular access policies and encryption by using AWS Glue. — Glue handles discovery and ETL, but is not the central fine-grained data-lake authorization service specified by the question.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist is developing a deep learning sentiment analysis model that is based on data from movie reviews. After the ML specialist trains the model and reviews the model results on the validation set, the ML specialist discovers that the model is overfitting. Which solutions will MOST improve the model generalization and reduce overfitting? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Shuffle the dataset with a different seed.
choices.B: Decrease the learning rate.
choices.C: Increase the number of layers in the network.
choices.D: Add L1 regularization and L2 regularization.
choices.E: Add dropout.
choices.F: Decrease the number of layers in the network.

explanation:
Key Concept: Overfitting occurs when a model learns training-specific patterns that do not generalize. Regularization and reduced model capacity can limit this behavior.

A. Shuffle the dataset with a different seed. — Changing the shuffle seed changes sample order or the split, but does not directly constrain the model's tendency to memorize training data.

B. Decrease the learning rate. — A smaller learning rate changes optimization speed and stability. It does not reliably reduce model capacity or prevent eventual overfitting.

C. Increase the number of layers in the network. — Adding layers increases capacity and can worsen overfitting when the current network already fits training-specific noise.

D. Add L1 regularization and L2 regularization. — L1 and L2 penalties discourage unnecessarily large weights, reducing the freedom to fit noise in the training reviews.

E. Add dropout. — Dropout randomly suppresses units during training, reducing dependence on particular internal features and encouraging more robust representations.

F. Decrease the number of layers in the network. — Reducing the number of layers lowers model capacity and can improve generalization when the original architecture is too complex for the available data.
