text: An online advertising company is developing a linear model to predict the bid price of advertisements in real time with low-latency predictions. A data scientist has trained the linear model by using many features, but the model is overfitting the training dataset. The data scientist needs to prevent overfitting and must reduce the number of features. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Retrain the model with L1 regularization applied.
choices.B: Retrain the model with L2 regularization applied.
choices.C: Retrain the model with dropout regularization applied.
choices.D: Retrain the model by using more data.

explanation:
Key Concept: L1 regularization encourages sparse linear-model coefficients, combining regularization with implicit feature selection.

A. Retrain the model with L1 regularization applied. — An L1 penalty can drive some coefficients exactly to zero, reducing the active feature set while limiting overfitting.

B. Retrain the model with L2 regularization applied. — L2 shrinks coefficients but generally does not make them exactly zero. It addresses overfitting without directly meeting the feature-removal requirement.

C. Retrain the model with dropout regularization applied. — Dropout is primarily a neural-network regularizer and does not directly select a smaller set of coefficients for this linear model.

D. Retrain the model by using more data. — More representative data may improve generalization, but it does not by itself reduce the number of input features.

text: A credit card company wants to identify fraudulent transactions in real time. A data scientist builds a machine learning model for this purpose. The transactional data is captured and stored in Amazon S3. The historic data is already labeled with two classes: fraud (positive) and fair transactions (negative). The data scientist removes all the missing data and builds a classifier by using the XGBoost algorithm in Amazon SageMaker. The model produces the following results: • True positive rate (TPR): 0.700 • False negative rate (FNR): 0.300 • True negative rate (TNR): 0.977 • False positive rate (FPR): 0.023 • Overall accuracy: 0.949 Which solution should the data scientist use to improve the performance of the model?

choices.A: Apply the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the minority class in the training dataset. Retrain the model with the updated training data.
choices.B: Apply the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the majority class in the training dataset. Retrain the model with the updated training data.
choices.C: Undersample the minority class.
choices.D: Oversample the majority class.

explanation:
Key Concept: High overall accuracy can conceal weak minority-class recall. Training-only minority oversampling is one way to improve attention to rare fraud examples.

A. Apply the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the minority class in the training dataset. Retrain the model with the updated training data. — SMOTE increases the representation of minority fraud cases through synthetic training examples. Recall, precision, and false-positive costs must then be evaluated on an untouched validation set.

B. Apply the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the majority class in the training dataset. Retrain the model with the updated training data. — Oversampling the majority fair-transaction class increases the imbalance and does not address the 30% of fraud cases being missed.

C. Undersample the minority class. — Removing minority fraud cases leaves even less information about fraudulent patterns and makes the imbalance worse.

D. Oversample the majority class. — Adding more majority examples increases the dominance of fair transactions rather than improving representation of the fraud class.

text: A company is training machine learning (ML) models on Amazon SageMaker by using 200 TB of data that is stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The training data consists of individual files that are each larger than 200 MB in size. The company needs a data access solution that offers the shortest processing time and the least amount of setup. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use File mode in SageMaker to copy the dataset from the S3 buckets to the ML instance storage.
choices.B: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Link the file system to the S3 buckets.
choices.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the file system to the training instances.
choices.D: Use FastFile mode in SageMaker to stream the files on demand from the S3 buckets.

explanation:
Key Concept: FastFile exposes S3 training data through a file interface and retrieves content on demand, avoiding a complete local download before training starts.

A. Use File mode in SageMaker to copy the dataset from the S3 buckets to the ML instance storage. — File mode downloads the full input before training. For 200 TB, that creates substantial startup delay and local-storage requirements.

B. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Link the file system to the S3 buckets. — FSx for Lustre can deliver high throughput, especially for repeated workloads, but requires a file system and networking setup beyond selecting FastFile mode.

C. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the file system to the training instances. — EFS requires provisioning, mounting, and making the S3 dataset available in the file system. It adds setup without the direct on-demand S3 integration requested.

D. Use FastFile mode in SageMaker to stream the files on demand from the S3 buckets. — FastFile starts reading the existing large S3 files as training needs them, minimizing setup and avoiding a full 200 TB staging step. Actual throughput still depends on the access pattern.

text: An online store is predicting future book sales by using a linear regression model that is based on past sales data. The data includes duration, a numerical feature that represents the number of days that a book has been listed in the online store. A data scientist performs an exploratory data analysis and discovers that the relationship between book sales and duration is skewed and non-linear. Which data transformation step should the data scientist take to improve the predictions of the model?

choices.A: One-hot encoding
choices.B: Cartesian product transformation
choices.C: Quantile binning
choices.D: Normalization

explanation:
Key Concept: Quantile bins divide a skewed numeric feature into intervals with roughly comparable sample counts, allowing different effects in different value ranges.

A. One-hot encoding — One-hot encoding raw continuous durations can create many sparse categories. Binning first provides a more useful representation of a skewed numeric relationship.

B. Cartesian product transformation — A Cartesian-product transformation models interactions among categorical values. It does not directly address the skewed nonlinear effect of this single numeric feature.

C. Quantile binning — Quantile binning can represent a piecewise relationship between duration and sales instead of forcing one slope across the entire range. The binned features need suitable encoding for the linear model.

D. Normalization — Normalization changes scale but preserves the basic shape of the relationship. A nonlinear association remains nonlinear after ordinary rescaling.

text: A company's data engineer wants to use Amazon S3 to share datasets with data scientists. The data scientists work in three departments: Finance. Marketing, and Human Resources. Each department has its own IAM user group. Some datasets contain sensitive information and should be accessed only by the data scientists from the Finance department. How can the data engineer set up access to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create an S3 bucket for each dataset. Create an ACL for each S3 bucket. For each S3 bucket that contains a sensitive dataset, set the ACL to allow access only from the Finance department user group. Allow all three department user groups to access each S3 bucket that contains a non-sensitive dataset.
choices.B: Create an S3 bucket for each dataset. For each S3 bucket that contains a sensitive dataset, set the bucket policy to allow access only from the Finance department user group. Allow all three department user groups to access each S3 bucket that contains a non-sensitive dataset.
choices.C: Create a single S3 bucket that includes two folders to separate the sensitive datasets from the non-sensitive datasets. For the Finance department user group, attach an IAM policy that provides access to both folders. For the Marketing and Human Resources department user groups, attach an IAM policy that provides access to only the folder that contains the non-sensitive datasets.
choices.D: Create a single S3 bucket that includes two folders to separate the sensitive datasets from the non-sensitive datasets. Set the policy for the S3 bucket to allow only the Finance department user group to access the folder that contains the sensitive datasets. Allow all three department user groups to access the folder that contains the non-sensitive datasets.

explanation:
Key Concept: IAM groups receive identity-based policies; they are not valid principals in S3 bucket policies or S3 ACL grants.

A. Create an S3 bucket for each dataset. Create an ACL for each S3 bucket. For each S3 bucket that contains a sensitive dataset, set the ACL to allow access only from the Finance department user group. Allow all three department user groups to access each S3 bucket that contains a non-sensitive dataset. — S3 ACLs cannot grant permissions to an IAM user group. Separate buckets do not fix the unsupported grant target.

B. Create an S3 bucket for each dataset. For each S3 bucket that contains a sensitive dataset, set the bucket policy to allow access only from the Finance department user group. Allow all three department user groups to access each S3 bucket that contains a non-sensitive dataset. — An IAM group cannot be named as the Principal in a bucket policy. Access for its members should be granted through an identity policy attached to the group.

C. Create a single S3 bucket that includes two folders to separate the sensitive datasets from the non-sensitive datasets. For the Finance department user group, attach an IAM policy that provides access to both folders. For the Marketing and Human Resources department user groups, attach an IAM policy that provides access to only the folder that contains the non-sensitive datasets. — Group-attached policies can grant Finance access to both object prefixes and the other groups access only to the nonsensitive prefix. Relevant bucket-list permissions and any other policies must also respect those boundaries.

D. Create a single S3 bucket that includes two folders to separate the sensitive datasets from the non-sensitive datasets. Set the policy for the S3 bucket to allow only the Finance department user group to access the folder that contains the sensitive datasets. Allow all three department user groups to access the folder that contains the non-sensitive datasets. — A bucket policy cannot directly designate the Finance IAM group as its principal, even when the data is separated into prefixes.

text: A company operates an amusement park. The company wants to collect, monitor, and store real-time traffic data at several park entrances by using strategically placed cameras. The company’s security team must be able to immediately access the data for viewing. Stored data must be indexed and must be accessible to the company’s data science team. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest, index, and store the data. Use the built-in integration with Amazon Rekognition for viewing by the security team.
choices.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest, index, and store the data. Use the built-in HTTP live streaming (HLS) capability for viewing by the security team.
choices.C: Use Amazon Rekognition Video and the GStreamer plugin to ingest the data for viewing by the security team. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to index and store the data.
choices.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest, index, and store the data. Use the built-in HTTP live streaming (HLS) capability for viewing by the security team.

explanation:
Key Concept: Kinesis Video Streams ingests and retains timestamp-indexed video, and HLS playback lets viewers consume the stream through compatible players.

A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest, index, and store the data. Use the built-in integration with Amazon Rekognition for viewing by the security team. — Rekognition performs video analysis such as detection. It is not the playback interface the security team needs to watch the camera feed.

B. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest, index, and store the data. Use the built-in HTTP live streaming (HLS) capability for viewing by the security team. — Kinesis Video Streams provides the ingestion, retention, and indexed retrieval, while its HLS capability supports viewing without building a separate video-delivery system.

C. Use Amazon Rekognition Video and the GStreamer plugin to ingest the data for viewing by the security team. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to index and store the data. — Rekognition is an analysis service, and Kinesis Data Streams is not a video fragment store with the requested indexing and playback capabilities.

D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest, index, and store the data. Use the built-in HTTP live streaming (HLS) capability for viewing by the security team. — Firehose delivers buffered records to data destinations. It does not supply Kinesis Video Streams' video indexing and HLS playback.

text: An engraving company wants to automate its quality control process for plaques. The company performs the process before mailing each customized plaque to a customer. The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket that contains images of defects that should cause a plaque to be rejected. Low-confidence predictions must be sent to an internal team of reviewers who are using Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I). Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use Amazon Textract for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with Amazon Mechanical Turk for manual review.
choices.B: Use Amazon Rekognition for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with a private workforce option for manual review.
choices.C: Use Amazon Transcribe for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with a private workforce option for manual review.
choices.D: Use AWS Panorama for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with Amazon Mechanical Turk for manual review.

explanation:
Key Concept: Visual defect detection needs an image model, and review by internal employees requires a private human-review workforce. The A2I portion is a historical availability consideration.

A. Use Amazon Textract for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with Amazon Mechanical Turk for manual review. — Textract extracts document text and structure, rather than learning arbitrary plaque defects. Mechanical Turk also uses an external workforce instead of the required internal team.

B. Use Amazon Rekognition for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with a private workforce option for manual review. — A suitable Rekognition model, such as Custom Labels trained for the defect classes, can flag images. A custom A2I review workflow with a private workforce can route uncertain cases to employees.

C. Use Amazon Transcribe for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with a private workforce option for manual review. — Transcribe converts speech to text and cannot classify visual plaque defects, even though the private-workforce choice is appropriate.

D. Use AWS Panorama for automatic processing. Use Amazon A2I with Amazon Mechanical Turk for manual review. — Panorama targeted edge computer vision rather than this S3 image workflow, and Mechanical Turk does not restrict review to the internal team.

text: A machine learning (ML) engineer at a bank is building a data ingestion solution to provide transaction features to financial ML models. Raw transactional data is available in an Amazon Kinesis data stream. The solution must compute rolling averages of the ingested data from the data stream and must store the results in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. The solution also must serve the results to the models in near real time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use a SageMaker Processing job to aggregate the data and to load the results into SageMaker Feature Store as an online feature group.
choices.B: Write the data directly from the data stream into SageMaker Feature Store as an online feature group. Calculate the rolling averages in place within SageMaker Feature Store by using the SageMaker GetRecord API operation.
choices.C: Consume the data stream by using an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics SQL application that calculates the rolling averages. Generate a result stream. Consume the result stream by using a custom AWS Lambda function that publishes the results to SageMaker Feature Store as an online feature group.
choices.D: Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use a SageMaker Processing job to load the data into SageMaker Feature Store as an offline feature group. Compute the rolling averages at query time.

explanation:
Key Concept: Windowed stream processing computes rolling features before writing them to the Feature Store online store for low-latency retrieval.

A. Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use a SageMaker Processing job to aggregate the data and to load the results into SageMaker Feature Store as an online feature group. — Firehose buffering and a Processing batch introduce delay before feature updates. They are less suitable than continuous windowed processing for near-real-time rolling averages.

B. Write the data directly from the data stream into SageMaker Feature Store as an online feature group. Calculate the rolling averages in place within SageMaker Feature Store by using the SageMaker GetRecord API operation. — GetRecord retrieves a stored feature record. It does not calculate rolling averages over historical stream events inside Feature Store.

C. Consume the data stream by using an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics SQL application that calculates the rolling averages. Generate a result stream. Consume the result stream by using a custom AWS Lambda function that publishes the results to SageMaker Feature Store as an online feature group. — Historically, a Kinesis SQL application could calculate the rolling window and Lambda could write the result to the online store. The retired SQL service must be replaced with a supported stream processor in a new implementation.

D. Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use a SageMaker Processing job to load the data into SageMaker Feature Store as an offline feature group. Compute the rolling averages at query time. — The offline store is designed for analytical and training access, not near-real-time online feature serving. Computing each rolling average at query time also adds latency.

text: Each morning, a data scientist at a rental car company creates insights about the previous day’s rental car reservation demands. The company needs to automate this process by streaming the data to Amazon S3 in near real time. The solution must detect high-demand rental cars at each of the company’s locations. The solution also must create a visualization dashboard that automatically refreshes with the most recent data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development time?

choices.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using Amazon QuickSight ML Insights. Visualize the data in QuickSight.
choices.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using the Random Cut Forest (RCF) trained model in Amazon SageMaker. Visualize the data in Amazon QuickSight.
choices.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using the Random Cut Forest (RCF) trained model in Amazon SageMaker. Visualize the data in Amazon QuickSight.
choices.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using Amazon QuickSight ML Insights. Visualize the data in QuickSight.

explanation:
Key Concept: Managed S3 delivery plus built-in dashboard anomaly detection reduces custom ingestion and modeling work. Dataset refresh and anomaly-analysis schedules still need configuration.

A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using Amazon QuickSight ML Insights. Visualize the data in QuickSight. — Firehose delivers reservations to S3, and QuickSight ML Insights provides anomaly detection within the visualization workflow, avoiding a separately trained outlier model.

B. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using the Random Cut Forest (RCF) trained model in Amazon SageMaker. Visualize the data in Amazon QuickSight. — This adds a retained stream and a custom RCF training and inference workflow. Those components require more development than delivery plus built-in dashboard insights.

C. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using the Random Cut Forest (RCF) trained model in Amazon SageMaker. Visualize the data in Amazon QuickSight. — Firehose is appropriate, but a separate SageMaker RCF model adds model preparation, deployment or batch scoring, and integration with the dashboard.

D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the reservation data directly to Amazon S3. Detect high-demand outliers by using Amazon QuickSight ML Insights. Visualize the data in QuickSight. — Data Streams introduces stream retention and delivery configuration when S3 delivery is the main ingestion need. Modern Data Streams supports managed S3 deliveries, so this option should not be rejected on an absolute claim that S3 delivery is impossible.

text: A company is planning a marketing campaign to promote a new product to existing customers. The company has data for past promotions that are similar. The company decides to try an experiment to send a more expensive marketing package to a smaller number of customers. The company wants to target the marketing campaign to customers who are most likely to buy the new product. The experiment requires that at least 90% of the customers who are likely to purchase the new product receive the marketing materials. The company trains a model by using the linear learner algorithm in Amazon SageMaker. The model has a recall score of 80% and a precision of 75%. How should the company retrain the model to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Set the target_recall hyperparameter to 90%. Set the binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria hyperparameter to recall_at_target_precision.
choices.B: Set the target_precision hyperparameter to 90%. Set the binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria hyperparameter to precision_at_target_recall.
choices.C: Use 90% of the historical data for training. Set the number of epochs to 20.
choices.D: Set the normalize_label hyperparameter to true. Set the number of classes to 2.

explanation:
Key Concept: Reaching at least 90% of likely purchasers is a recall constraint. Linear Learner should use target_recall=0.9 with precision_at_target_recall, but no option gives that pair.

A. Set the target_recall hyperparameter to 90%. Set the binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria hyperparameter to recall_at_target_precision. — The target_recall value matches the goal, but recall_at_target_precision selects the wrong optimization criterion and expects a precision target.

B. Set the target_precision hyperparameter to 90%. Set the binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria hyperparameter to precision_at_target_recall. — The precision_at_target_recall criterion is appropriate, but target_precision specifies the wrong target parameter. It must be paired with target_recall.

C. Use 90% of the historical data for training. Set the number of epochs to 20. — A training split and epoch count do not impose a minimum recall or select the decision threshold needed to meet it.

D. Set the normalize_label hyperparameter to true. Set the number of classes to 2. — Label normalization and the number of classes do not implement a recall constraint. This option cannot guarantee that 90% of likely purchasers receive the campaign.

text: A wildlife research company has a set of images of lions and cheetahs. The company created a dataset of the images. The company labeled each image with a binary label that indicates whether an image contains a lion or cheetah. The company wants to train a model to identify whether new images contain a lion or cheetah. Which Amazon SageMaker algorithm will meet this requirement?

choices.A: XGBoost
choices.B: Image Classification - TensorFlow
choices.C: Object Detection - TensorFlow
choices.D: Semantic segmentation - MXNet

explanation:
Key Concept: Image-level species labels support image classification; localization and pixel segmentation require more detailed target annotations.

A. XGBoost — XGBoost is designed for tabular features. Using it on images would require an additional feature-extraction pipeline rather than directly using a suitable image model.

B. Image Classification - TensorFlow — Image Classification - TensorFlow can learn to assign lion or cheetah labels from whole-image training examples, matching the available binary labels.

C. Object Detection - TensorFlow — Object Detection predicts object locations and classes. Bounding-box annotations are not provided, and the task does not require localization.

D. Semantic segmentation - MXNet — Semantic segmentation assigns a class to each pixel and requires pixel-level labels. That is unnecessary for identifying the species in the whole image.

text: A data scientist for a medical diagnostic testing company has developed a machine learning (ML) model to identify patients who have a specific disease. The dataset that the scientist used to train the model is imbalanced. The dataset contains a large number of healthy patients and only a small number of patients who have the disease. The model should consider that patients who are incorrectly identified as positive for the disease will increase costs for the company. Which metric will MOST accurately evaluate the performance of this model?

choices.A: Recall
choices.B: F1 score
choices.C: Accuracy
choices.D: Precision

explanation:
Key Concept: Precision measures the fraction of positive predictions that are actually positive, making it relevant when false positive predictions carry the emphasized cost.

A. Recall — Recall measures how many actual positive cases are found. It focuses on missed cases rather than the stated cost of incorrectly flagging healthy records.

B. F1 score — F1 balances precision and recall, but the question specifically emphasizes false positives rather than assigning equal importance to both error types.

C. Accuracy — Accuracy can be dominated by the large healthy class, masking a poor positive-prediction quality on this imbalanced dataset.

D. Precision — Precision equals TP divided by TP plus FP, so it directly describes the reliability of the model's positive predictions. It should not be treated as a complete clinical evaluation by itself.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist is training a linear regression model. The specialist notices that the model is overfitting. The specialist applies an L1 regularization parameter and runs the model again. This change results in all features having zero weights. What should the ML specialist do to improve the model results?

choices.A: Increase the L1 regularization parameter. Do not change any other training parameters.
choices.B: Decrease the L1 regularization parameter. Do not change any other training parameters.
choices.C: Introduce a large L2 regularization parameter. Do not change the current L1 regularization value.
choices.D: Introduce a small L2 regularization parameter. Do not change the current L1 regularization value.

explanation:
Key Concept: An excessively strong L1 penalty can shrink every feature coefficient to zero, producing an underfit model.

A. Increase the L1 regularization parameter. Do not change any other training parameters. — Increasing the penalty pushes coefficients toward zero even more strongly and worsens the reported problem.

B. Decrease the L1 regularization parameter. Do not change any other training parameters. — Reducing L1 lets useful coefficients become nonzero while retaining some regularization. The strength should be selected using validation performance.

C. Introduce a large L2 regularization parameter. Do not change the current L1 regularization value. — A large L2 penalty adds further shrinkage without removing the excessive L1 pressure responsible for the zero coefficients.

D. Introduce a small L2 regularization parameter. Do not change the current L1 regularization value. — Adding a small L2 penalty still leaves the problematic L1 setting unchanged. The direct fix is to reduce the existing L1 penalty.

text: A machine learning (ML) engineer is integrating a production model with a customer metadata repository for real-time inference. The repository is hosted in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. The engineer wants to retrieve only the latest version of the customer metadata record for a single customer at a time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use the SageMaker Feature Store BatchGetRecord API with the record identifier. Filter to find the latest record.
choices.B: Create an Amazon Athena query to retrieve the data from the feature table.
choices.C: Create an Amazon Athena query to retrieve the data from the feature table. Use the write_time value to find the latest record.
choices.D: Use the SageMaker Feature Store GetRecord API with the record identifier.

explanation:
Key Concept: Feature Store's online store serves the latest record for an identifier with low latency; historical records belong to the offline store.

A. Use the SageMaker Feature Store BatchGetRecord API with the record identifier. Filter to find the latest record. — BatchGetRecord can retrieve online records, but batching and then filtering for a version is unnecessary for a single identifier. The online result is already the latest stored record.

B. Create an Amazon Athena query to retrieve the data from the feature table. — Athena queries the offline data and is not the low-latency API intended for retrieving one customer's current online features.

C. Create an Amazon Athena query to retrieve the data from the feature table. Use the write_time value to find the latest record. — An offline SQL query adds latency and version-selection logic. Write time also should not be assumed equivalent to the feature event time that determines record recency.

D. Use the SageMaker Feature Store GetRecord API with the record identifier. — GetRecord takes the feature group and record identifier and directly retrieves that customer's current online feature values.

text: A company’s data scientist has trained a new machine learning model that performs better on test data than the company’s existing model performs in the production environment. The data scientist wants to replace the existing model that runs on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint in the production environment. However, the company is concerned that the new model might not work well on the production environment data. The data scientist needs to perform A/B testing in the production environment to evaluate whether the new model performs well on production environment data. Which combination of steps must the data scientist take to perform the A/B testing? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Create a new endpoint configuration that includes a production variant for each of the two models.
choices.B: Create a new endpoint configuration that includes two target variants that point to different endpoints.
choices.C: Deploy the new model to the existing endpoint.
choices.D: Update the existing endpoint to activate the new model.
choices.E: Update the existing endpoint to use the new endpoint configuration.

explanation:
Key Concept: A SageMaker endpoint configuration can define multiple production variants, with traffic weights controlling an A/B test between model versions.

A. Create a new endpoint configuration that includes a production variant for each of the two models. — A configuration containing both models as production variants preserves the existing model while enabling controlled traffic to the candidate.

B. Create a new endpoint configuration that includes two target variants that point to different endpoints. — TargetVariant is an invocation parameter selecting a production variant within an endpoint. Endpoint configurations do not define target variants pointing to other endpoints as described.

C. Deploy the new model to the existing endpoint. — Deploying the new model alone does not specify that both models remain available or how traffic is split for the A/B test.

D. Update the existing endpoint to activate the new model. — Merely activating a replacement model does not define a concurrent comparison against the existing model.

E. Update the existing endpoint to use the new endpoint configuration. — Updating the endpoint to the two-variant configuration applies the A/B setup. The team can then monitor each variant and adjust traffic weights.

text: A data scientist wants to build a financial trading bot to automate investment decisions. choices.A: Supervised learning

explanation:
Key Concept: Reinforcement learning models sequential decisions whose actions affect later rewards, optimizing an expected cumulative objective.

A. Supervised learning — Supervised learning predicts labeled targets such as future prices, but does not by itself learn an action policy that optimizes a sequence of trading rewards.

B. Unsupervised learning — Unsupervised learning discovers patterns without target labels or reward-driven action selection. It does not directly optimize a trading policy.

C. Semi-supervised learning — Semi-supervised learning combines labeled and unlabeled examples. It does not address the central requirement to choose actions based on long-term rewards.

D. Reinforcement learning — Reinforcement learning represents trades as actions and evaluates their cumulative reward over time. Appropriate simulation, transaction costs, and risk constraints are still needed; the formulation does not guarantee profit.

text: A data scientist wants to improve the fit of a machine learning (ML) model that predicts house prices. The data scientist makes a first attempt to fit the model, but the fitted model has poor accuracy on both the training dataset and the test dataset. Which steps must the data scientist take to improve model accuracy? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Increase the amount of regularization that the model uses.
choices.B: Decrease the amount of regularization that the model uses.
choices.C: Increase the number of training examples that that model uses.
choices.D: Increase the number of test examples that the model uses.
choices.E: Increase the number of model features that the model uses.
choices.F: Decrease the number of model features that the model uses.

explanation:
Key Concept: Poor training and test performance suggests underfitting, although data quality and optimization must also be checked. Only two listed changes directly address insufficient model capacity.

A. Increase the amount of regularization that the model uses. — Stronger regularization further restricts the model and can worsen underfitting when both training and test performance are poor.

B. Decrease the amount of regularization that the model uses. — Reducing excessive regularization allows the model to fit more of the training signal and can reduce high bias.

C. Increase the number of training examples that that model uses. — More training examples can help data coverage or variance, but do not necessarily fix a model that already cannot fit its training data. The prompt does not justify this as a required third step.

D. Increase the number of test examples that the model uses. — More test examples improve the reliability of evaluation, not the fitted model's ability to learn the house-price relationship.

E. Increase the number of model features that the model uses. — Adding informative features or suitable nonlinear features can increase the model's ability to represent the relationship and reduce underfitting.

F. Decrease the number of model features that the model uses. — Removing features generally reduces available predictive information and does not directly fix insufficient model capacity. The requested three-answer key is therefore unresolved.

text: A car company is developing a machine learning solution to detect whether a car is present in an image. The image dataset consists of one million images. Each image in the dataset is 200 pixels in height by 200 pixels in width. Each image is labeled as either having a car or not having a car. Which architecture is MOST likely to produce a model that detects whether a car is present in an image with the highest accuracy?

choices.A: Use a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier with the images as input. Include a linear output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car.
choices.B: Use a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier with the images as input. Include a softmax output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car.
choices.C: Use a deep multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier with the images as input. Include a linear output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car.
choices.D: Use a deep multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier with the images as input. Include a softmax output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car.

explanation:
Key Concept: CNNs exploit image locality and shared visual patterns; a two-class softmax converts output logits into a normalized class-probability vector.

A. Use a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier with the images as input. Include a linear output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car. — A linear output produces unconstrained scores, not probabilities by itself. A probability transformation and compatible loss are needed for the stated output.

B. Use a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier with the images as input. Include a softmax output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car. — A CNN is well suited to the spatial structure of car images, and a two-unit softmax produces car and no-car probabilities. A single sigmoid output would also be a valid binary-classification design.

C. Use a deep multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier with the images as input. Include a linear output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car. — Flattening images into an MLP discards the CNN's spatial inductive bias, and a linear output alone does not produce valid probabilities.

D. Use a deep multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier with the images as input. Include a softmax output layer that outputs the probability that an image contains a car. — Softmax supplies valid class probabilities, but a fully connected MLP lacks the parameter sharing and local pattern extraction that make CNNs effective for images.

text: A company is creating an application to identify, count, and classify animal images that are uploaded to the company’s website. The company is using the Amazon SageMaker image classification algorithm with an ImageNetV2 convolutional neural network (CNN). The solution works well for most animal images but does not recognize many animal species that are less common. The company obtains 10,000 labeled images of less common animal species and stores the images in Amazon S3. A machine learning (ML) engineer needs to incorporate the images into the model by using Pipe mode in SageMaker. Which combination of steps should the ML engineer take to train the model? (Choose two.)

choices.B: Use an Inception model that is available with the SageMaker image classification algorithm.
choices.C: Create a .lst file that contains a list of image files and corresponding class labels. Upload the .lst file to Amazon S3.
choices.D: Initiate transfer learning. Train the model by using the images of less common species.
choices.E: Use an augmented manifest file in JSON Lines format.

explanation:
Key Concept: Transfer learning adapts learned visual features to new species, and an augmented manifest can stream image files and labels through Pipe mode.

A. Use a ResNet model. Initiate full training mode by initializing the network with random weights. — Random initialization discards existing visual knowledge and usually needs more data and compute than fine-tuning for the added rare species.

B. Use an Inception model that is available with the SageMaker image classification algorithm. — Changing to an Inception model does not address the missing species examples, and it is not the stated built-in algorithm's required transfer-learning configuration.

C. Create a .lst file that contains a list of image files and corresponding class labels. Upload the .lst file to Amazon S3. — A plain image-list file is associated with other input preparation paths. It does not supply the augmented-manifest Pipe-mode workflow requested for individual image files.

D. Initiate transfer learning. Train the model by using the images of less common species. — Fine-tuning with the new labeled images adapts pretrained visual features to less common species. Include suitable existing-class data and validation to limit forgetting.

E. Use an augmented manifest file in JSON Lines format. — A JSON Lines augmented manifest pairs each S3 image reference with its label, allowing supported image-classification training to consume image files in Pipe mode without first building RecordIO files.

text: A music streaming company is building a pipeline to extract features. The company wants to store the features for offline model training and online inference. The company wants to track feature history and to give the company’s data science teams access to the features. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to store features for model training and inference. Create an online store for online inference. Create an offline store for model training. Create an IAM role for data scientists to access and search through feature groups.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to store features for model training and inference. Create an online store for both online inference and model training. Create an IAM role for data scientists to access and search through feature groups.
choices.C: Create one Amazon S3 bucket to store online inference features. Create a second S3 bucket to store offline model training features. Turn on versioning for the S3 buckets and use tags to specify which tags are for online inference features and which are for offline model training features. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket for online inference. Connect the S3 bucket for offline model training to a SageMaker training job. Create an IAM policy that allows data scientists to access both buckets.
choices.D: Create two separate Amazon DynamoDB tables to store online inference features and offline model training features. Use time-based versioning on both tables. Query the DynamoDB table for online inference. Move the data from DynamoDB to Amazon S3 when a new SageMaker training job is launched. Create an IAM policy that allows data scientists to access both tables.

explanation:
Key Concept: Feature Store separates low-latency access to current feature values from historical storage used for training and analysis.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to store features for model training and inference. Create an online store for online inference. Create an offline store for model training. Create an IAM role for data scientists to access and search through feature groups. — The online store serves current features, while the offline store retains history for training. IAM-controlled feature groups make the same definitions discoverable and reusable by teams.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to store features for model training and inference. Create an online store for both online inference and model training. Create an IAM role for data scientists to access and search through feature groups. — The online store does not replace the offline historical dataset. Using it alone loses the required training-oriented feature history.

C. Create one Amazon S3 bucket to store online inference features. Create a second S3 bucket to store offline model training features. Turn on versioning for the S3 buckets and use tags to specify which tags are for online inference features and which are for offline model training features. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket for online inference. Connect the S3 bucket for offline model training to a SageMaker training job. Create an IAM policy that allows data scientists to access both buckets. — S3 and Athena suit offline analytics, but Athena queries are not a low-latency online feature lookup service. This design also requires custom feature catalog and synchronization logic.

D. Create two separate Amazon DynamoDB tables to store online inference features and offline model training features. Use time-based versioning on both tables. Query the DynamoDB table for online inference. Move the data from DynamoDB to Amazon S3 when a new SageMaker training job is launched. Create an IAM policy that allows data scientists to access both tables. — DynamoDB can serve features quickly, but versioning, historical export, discovery, and synchronization must be built and operated separately. Feature Store provides those specialized capabilities.

text: A beauty supply store wants to understand some characteristics of visitors to the store. The store has security video recordings from the past several years. The store wants to generate a report of hourly visitors from the recordings. The report should group visitors by hair style and hair color. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

choices.A: Use an object detection algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an ResNet-50 algorithm to determine hair style and hair color.
choices.B: Use an object detection algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an XGBoost algorithm to determine hair style and hair color.
choices.C: Use a semantic segmentation algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an ResNet-50 algorithm to determine hair style and hair color.
choices.D: Use a semantic segmentation algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an XGBoost algorithm to determine hair style and hair.

explanation:
Key Concept: Hair localization followed by image classification is plausible, but the prompt does not specify available labels, accuracy needs, or visitor tracking. Those omissions prevent a unique complete solution.

A. Use an object detection algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an ResNet-50 algorithm to determine hair style and hair color. — Bounding-box detection plus a fine-tuned ResNet can classify cropped hair regions with relatively economical box annotations. It still needs labeled hair attributes and a tracking/counting stage to avoid counting the same visitor repeatedly.

B. Use an object detection algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an XGBoost algorithm to determine hair style and hair color. — XGBoost would require suitable extracted visual features from each crop. It is not a direct substitute for a pretrained image classifier operating on raw hair images.

Pass the identified hair to an ResNet-50 algorithm to determine hair style and hair color. — Segmentation can isolate hair more precisely before ResNet classification, but generally requires more detailed annotations. It may be preferable if background contamination matters, which the question does not resolve.

D. Use a semantic segmentation algorithm to identify a visitor’s hair in video frames. Pass the identified hair to an XGBoost algorithm to determine hair style and hair. — Pixel segmentation adds annotation effort, and XGBoost still needs a feature representation. The truncated final requirement and missing visitor-tracking step further weaken this option.

text: A financial services company wants to automate its loan approval process by building a machine learning (ML) model. Each loan approval prediction must come with a report that contains an explanation for why the customer was approved for a loan or was denied for a loan. choices.A: Use SageMaker Model Debugger to automatically debug the predictions, generate the explanation, and attach the explanation report.
choices.B: Use AWS Lambda to provide feature importance and partial dependence plots. Use the plots to generate and attach the explanation report.
choices.C: Use SageMaker Clarify to generate the explanation report. Attach the report to the predicted results.
choices.D: Use custom Amazon CloudWatch metrics to generate the explanation report. Attach the report to the predicted results.

explanation:
Key Concept: A local feature-attribution explanation describes how an individual's input features contribute to the model's output relative to a baseline.

A. Use SageMaker Model Debugger to automatically debug the predictions, generate the explanation, and attach the explanation report. — Debugger focuses on training issues and captured tensors. It does not automatically attach an individual explanation report to every hosted prediction.

B. Use AWS Lambda to provide feature importance and partial dependence plots. Use the plots to generate and attach the explanation report. — Lambda can orchestrate custom explanation code, but global importance and partial-dependence plots do not directly provide a per-customer explanation without additional implementation.

Attach the report to the predicted results. — Clarify computes feature attributions for individual predictions, which can be included in the application's decision report. This avoids building the attribution calculation from scratch; new-customer service availability must be checked.

D. Use custom Amazon CloudWatch metrics to generate the explanation report. Attach the report to the predicted results. — CloudWatch metrics report operational or custom measurements. They do not calculate the model-specific feature contributions needed to explain an approval or denial.

text: A social media company wants to develop a machine learning (ML) model to detect inappropriate or offensive content in images. The company has collected a large dataset of labeled images and plans to use the built-in Amazon SageMaker image classification algorithm to train the model. The company also intends to use SageMaker pipe mode to speed up the training. The company splits the dataset into training, validation, and testing datasets. The company stores the training and validation images in folders that are named Training and Validation, respectively. The folders contain subfolders that correspond to the names of the dataset classes. The company resizes the images to the same size and generates two input manifest files named training.lst and validation.lst, for the training dataset and the validation dataset, respectively. Finally, the company creates two separate Amazon S3 buckets for uploads of the training dataset and the validation dataset. Which additional data preparation steps should the company take before uploading the files to Amazon S3?

choices.A: Generate two Apache Parquet files, training.parquet and validation.parquet, by reading the images into a Pandas data frame and storing the data frame as a Parquet file. Upload the Parquet files to the training S3 bucket.
choices.B: Compress the training and validation directories by using the Snappy compression library. Upload the manifest and compressed files to the training S3 bucket.
choices.C: Compress the training and validation directories by using the gzip compression library. Upload the manifest and compressed files to the training S3 bucket.
choices.D: Generate two RecordIO files, training.rec and validation.rec, from the manifest files by using the im2rec Apache MXNet utility tool. Upload the RecordIO files to the training S3 bucket.

explanation:
Key Concept: The built-in MXNet image classifier can consume RecordIO through Pipe mode; im2rec packages images and labels from image-list files into that format.

A. Generate two Apache Parquet files, training.parquet and validation.parquet, by reading the images into a Pandas data frame and storing the data frame as a Parquet file. Upload the Parquet files to the training S3 bucket. — Parquet is a tabular storage format and is not the built-in image classifier's expected Pipe-mode image-training format.

B. Compress the training and validation directories by using the Snappy compression library. Upload the manifest and compressed files to the training S3 bucket. — Snappy compression does not convert the directory and labels into the RecordIO stream structure required by this proposed input path.

C. Compress the training and validation directories by using the gzip compression library. Upload the manifest and compressed files to the training S3 bucket. — Compressing directories with gzip does not provide the image-and-label RecordIO records expected by the algorithm.

D. Generate two RecordIO files, training.rec and validation.rec, from the manifest files by using the im2rec Apache MXNet utility tool. Upload the RecordIO files to the training S3 bucket. — im2rec converts the existing list files and images into RecordIO files suitable for Pipe mode. The training and validation records must still be assigned to their respective channels, regardless of whether one or two buckets hold them.

text: A pharmaceutical company performs periodic audits of clinical trial sites to quickly resolve critical findings. The company stores audit documents in text format. explanation:

C. Neural topic modeling (NTM) — NTM learns latent document topics and their associated words, helping auditors interpret and allocate the discovered themes. Adverse-event prioritization still requires identifying the relevant topic or adding explicit rules.

D. Linear support vector machine — A linear SVM is a supervised classifier when used for these categories and needs labeled training targets that are not provided.

E. Linear regression — Linear regression predicts a numeric target. It does not discover unlabeled themes or produce topic-word distributions.

text: A company is deploying a new machine learning (ML) model in a production environment. The company is concerned that the ML model will drift over time, so the company creates a script to aggregate all inputs and predictions into a single file at the end of each day. The company stores the file as an object in an Amazon S3 bucket. The total size of the daily file is 100 GB. The daily file size will increase over time. Four times a year, the company samples the data from the previous 90 days to check the ML model for drift. After the 90-day period, the company must keep the files for compliance reasons. The company needs to use S3 storage classes to minimize costs. The company wants to maintain the same storage durability of the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Store the daily objects in the S3 Standard-InfrequentAccess (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days.
choices.B: Store the daily objects in the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days.
choices.C: Store the daily objects in the S3 Standard-InfrequentAccess (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days.
choices.D: Store the daily objects in the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days.

explanation:
Key Concept: Infrequently read recent data fits Standard-IA, while long-term archival data with no fast-retrieval requirement can move to Glacier Deep Archive.

A. Store the daily objects in the S3 Standard-InfrequentAccess (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days. — Standard-IA fits the first 90 days, but Flexible Retrieval generally costs more to store than Deep Archive when the older data only needs long-term retention.

B. Store the daily objects in the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days. — One Zone-IA lacks the multi-AZ resilience of the original storage, and Flexible Retrieval is not the lowest-cost listed long-term archive tier.

C. Store the daily objects in the S3 Standard-InfrequentAccess (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days. — Standard-IA preserves multi-AZ storage for quarterly sampling, and a lifecycle transition to Deep Archive reduces ongoing storage cost after 90 days. Retrieval delay and minimum storage duration must fit the compliance retention policy.

D. Store the daily objects in the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days. — Deep Archive fits the old data, but One Zone-IA stores recent data in one Availability Zone. Its nominal durability target does not provide the same protection against loss of that zone.

The audit solution must generate a report that analyzes the metadata. The solution also must be able to set the data sensitivity and authorship of features. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to select the features. Create a data flow to perform feature-level metadata analysis. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store feature-level metadata. Use Amazon QuickSight to analyze the metadata.
choices.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to set feature groups for the current features that the ML models use. Assign the required metadata for each feature. Use SageMaker Studio to analyze the metadata.
choices.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Features Store to apply custom algorithms to analyze the feature-level metadata that the company requires. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store feature-level metadata. Use Amazon QuickSight to analyze the metadata.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist uploads a dataset to an Amazon S3 bucket that is protected by server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). The ML specialist needs to ensure that an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance can read the dataset that is in Amazon S3. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Define security groups to allow all HTTP inbound and outbound traffic. Assign the security groups to the SageMaker notebook instance.
choices.B: Configure the SageMaker notebook instance to have access to the VPC. Grant permission in the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy to the notebook’s VPC.
choices.C: Assign an IAM role that provides S3 read access for the dataset to the SageMaker notebook. Grant permission in the KMS key policy to the IAM role.
choices.D: Assign the same KMS key that encrypts the data in Amazon S3 to the SageMaker notebook instance.

explanation:
Key Concept: Reading an SSE-KMS S3 object requires both authorization to read the object and permission to decrypt with its KMS key.

A. Define security groups to allow all HTTP inbound and outbound traffic. Assign the security groups to the SageMaker notebook instance. — Security groups control network traffic. Allowing HTTP traffic does not grant S3 object permissions or KMS decryption rights.

B. Configure the SageMaker notebook instance to have access to the VPC. Grant permission in the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy to the notebook’s VPC. — A VPC is not the execution identity that decrypts an object. The KMS policy must authorize the relevant principal, such as the notebook execution role.

C. Assign an IAM role that provides S3 read access for the dataset to the SageMaker notebook. Grant permission in the KMS key policy to the IAM role. — The notebook assumes its execution role to read S3. Granting that role the required S3 and KMS permissions, with a compatible key policy, permits access to the encrypted dataset.

D. Assign the same KMS key that encrypts the data in Amazon S3 to the SageMaker notebook instance. — Encrypting the notebook's own storage with the same key does not automatically authorize its role to read and decrypt objects in S3.

text: A company has a podcast platform that has thousands of users. The company implemented an algorithm to detect low podcast engagement based on a 10-minute running window of user events such as listening to, pausing, and closing the podcast. A machine learning (ML) specialist is designing the ingestion process for these events. The ML specialist needs to transform the data to prepare the data for inference. How should the ML specialist design the transformation step to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.A: Use an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster to ingest event data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.
choices.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest event data. Store the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use AWS Lambda to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.
choices.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest event data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.
choices.D: Use an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster to ingest event data. Use AWS Lambda to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference.

explanation:
Key Concept: A managed stream-processing application can maintain a running event-time window and transform it continuously before inference.

A. Use an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster to ingest event data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — MSK can feed a stream processor, but a Kafka cluster adds broker-related configuration and capacity considerations when no Kafka-specific requirement is given.

B. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest event data. Store the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use AWS Lambda to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — Firehose delivery to S3 introduces buffering, and Lambda would need custom logic to reconstruct the latest ten-minute window from stored objects.

C. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest event data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — Kinesis Data Streams plus managed stream processing provides a direct ingestion and windowing path. For a current implementation, use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink rather than the retired Kinesis SQL service.

D. Use an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster to ingest event data. Use AWS Lambda to transform the most recent 10 minutes of data before inference. — MSK plus Lambda adds Kafka operations and custom stateful-window handling, whereas a stream-processing engine already provides window semantics.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist is training a multilayer perceptron (MLP) on a dataset with multiple classes. The target class of interest is unique compared to the other classes in the dataset, but it does not achieve an acceptable recall metric. The ML specialist varies the number and size of the MLP's hidden layers, but the results do not improve significantly. Which solution will improve recall in the LEAST amount of time?

choices.A: Add class weights to the MLP's loss function, and then retrain.
choices.B: Gather more data by using Amazon Mechanical Turk, and then retrain.
choices.C: Train a k-means algorithm instead of an MLP.
choices.D: Train an anomaly detection model instead of an MLP.

explanation:
Key Concept: Class-weighted loss increases the training penalty for errors on an important class, potentially improving that class's recall without collecting more data.

A. Add class weights to the MLP's loss function, and then retrain. — Increasing the target class's loss weight makes its missed examples more costly during training. This is a small configuration change that can shift the model toward better recall, with a possible precision tradeoff.

B. Gather more data by using Amazon Mechanical Turk, and then retrain. — Collecting and labeling more data can help, but takes longer than reweighting the existing training objective.

C. Train a k-means algorithm instead of an MLP. — K-means discovers clusters rather than learning the supplied class labels. It does not directly optimize recall for the target class.

D. Train an anomaly detection model instead of an MLP. — An anomaly detector changes the task formulation and requires separate calibration. A distinct class is not necessarily an anomaly, and reweighting the current classifier is more direct.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist uploads 5 TB of data to an Amazon SageMaker Studio environment. The ML specialist performs initial data cleansing. Before the ML specialist begins to train a model, the ML specialist needs to create and view an analysis report that details potential bias in the uploaded data. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to automatically detect data bias
choices.B: Turn on the bias detection option in SageMaker Ground Truth to automatically analyze data features.
choices.C: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to generate a bias drift report.
choices.D: Configure SageMaker Data Wrangler to generate a bias report.
choices.E: Use SageMaker Experiments to perform a data check

explanation:
Key Concept: Pretraining bias analysis examines the dataset before any model exists, using configured sensitive facets and outcome definitions.

A. Use SageMaker Clarify to automatically detect data bias — Clarify computes pretraining bias metrics from the prepared data after the team specifies the relevant facets and labels. It does not decide the appropriate fairness definition automatically.

B. Turn on the bias detection option in SageMaker Ground Truth to automatically analyze data features. — Ground Truth manages labeling workflows. It does not provide the described general switch for automatically analyzing a dataset's bias.

C. Use SageMaker Model Monitor to generate a bias drift report. — Bias drift monitoring compares behavior over time in a monitoring workflow. The team instead needs an initial pretraining dataset assessment.

D. Configure SageMaker Data Wrangler to generate a bias report. — Data Wrangler provides a bias-analysis interface and report for inspecting the configured metrics. At this scale, the analyzed sample or managed job must be explicit so a preview is not mistaken for analysis of all 5 TB.

E. Use SageMaker Experiments to perform a data check — Experiments tracks runs, parameters, and metrics. It is not the service that computes the required dataset bias report.

text: A network security vendor needs to ingest telemetry data from thousands of endpoints that run all over the world. The data is transmitted every 30 seconds in the form of records that contain 50 fields. Each record is up to 1 KB in size. The security vendor uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. The vendor requires hourly summaries of the records that Kinesis Data Streams ingests. The vendor will use Amazon Athena to query the records and to generate the summaries. The Athena queries will target 7 to 12 of the available data fields. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of customization to transform and store the ingested data?

choices.A: Use AWS Lambda to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
choices.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using a short-lived Amazon EMR cluster.
choices.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
choices.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using AWS Lambda.

explanation:
Key Concept: Stateful stream windowing computes hourly summaries, while Firehose handles delivery to S3; columnar output helps Athena scan only the requested fields.

A. Use AWS Lambda to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. — Lambda needs custom buffering, state, and window-completion logic to aggregate an hour of events, increasing implementation effort.

B. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using a short-lived Amazon EMR cluster. — Firehose buffering does not calculate hourly aggregate values by itself. Adding a short-lived EMR cluster also adds orchestration for a stream-processing task.

C. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. — A stream analytics application can compute the hourly windows and send results to Firehose for S3 delivery. A current implementation should use managed Flink where the historical question assumed Kinesis SQL.

D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read and aggregate the data hourly. Transform the data and store it in Amazon S3 by using AWS Lambda. — Firehose does not itself perform the stated hourly aggregation. A Lambda stage would require custom aggregation and state handling rather than only a simple record transformation.

text: A medical device company is building a machine learning (ML) model to predict the likelihood of device recall based on customer data that the company collects from a plain text survey. One of the survey questions asks which medications the customer is taking. The data for this field contains the names of medications that customers enter manually. Customers misspell some of the medication names. The column that contains the medication name data gives a categorical feature with high cardinality but redundancy. What is the MOST effective way to encode this categorical feature into a numeric feature?

choices.A: Spell check the column. Use Amazon SageMaker one-hot encoding on the column to transform a categorical feature to a numerical feature.
choices.B: Fix the spelling in the column by using char-RNN. Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler one-hot encoding to transform a categorical feature to a numerical feature.
choices.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler similarity encoding on the column to create embeddings of vectors of real numbers.
choices.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler ordinal encoding on the column to encode categories into an integer between 0 and the total number of categories in the column.

explanation:
Key Concept: Similarity encoding represents string categories using similarity among their character patterns, which can reduce fragmentation from spelling variants in high-cardinality text fields.

A. Spell check the column. Use Amazon SageMaker one-hot encoding on the column to transform a categorical feature to a numerical feature. — Spell checking needs a reliable domain dictionary, and one-hot encoding can still create a very wide feature space after correction.

B. Fix the spelling in the column by using char-RNN. Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler one-hot encoding to transform a categorical feature to a numerical feature. — Training or configuring a character-level correction model adds work, and one-hot encoding retains the high-cardinality dimensionality problem.

C. Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler similarity encoding on the column to create embeddings of vectors of real numbers. — Similarity encoding places related string values into a numeric representation that reflects spelling similarity, making it appropriate for redundant medication-name variants. Clinical equivalence must not be inferred from spelling similarity alone.

D. Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler ordinal encoding on the column to encode categories into an integer between 0 and the total number of categories in the column. — Ordinal encoding assigns arbitrary integer order to unrelated categories. It neither resolves spelling redundancy nor represents meaningful distances between medication names.

text: A machine learning (ML) engineer has created a feature repository in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store for the company. The company has AWS accounts for development, integration, and production. The company hosts a feature store in the development account. The company uses Amazon S3 buckets to store feature values offline. The company wants to share features and to allow the integration account and the production account to reuse the features that are in the feature repository. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Create an IAM role in the development account that the integration account and production account can assume. Attach IAM policies to the role that allow access to the feature repository and the S3 buckets.
choices.B: Share the feature repository that is associated the S3 buckets from the development account to the integration account and the production account by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
choices.C: Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) from the integration account and the production account to retrieve credentials for the development account.
choices.D: Set up S3 replication between the development S3 buckets and the integration and production S3 buckets.
choices.E: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint in the development account for SageMaker.

explanation:
Key Concept: Cross-account role assumption provides temporary authorized access to a shared feature repository and its underlying offline S3 data without copying the data.

A. Create an IAM role in the development account that the integration account and production account can assume. Attach IAM policies to the role that allow access to the feature repository and the S3 buckets. — A development-account role with the right trust policy and feature/S3 permissions defines what the consuming accounts may access.

B. Share the feature repository that is associated the S3 buckets from the development account to the integration account and the production account by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). — AWS RAM supports relevant Feature Store sharing capabilities, but sharing feature resources alone does not automatically grant access to the associated offline S3 objects and encryption keys.

C. Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) from the integration account and the production account to retrieve credentials for the development account. — STS AssumeRole lets authorized integration and production principals obtain temporary credentials for the development role, completing the cross-account access path.

D. Set up S3 replication between the development S3 buckets and the integration and production S3 buckets. — Replication creates extra copies and synchronization responsibilities. It does not directly share the original feature repository or its catalog metadata.

E. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint in the development account for SageMaker. — PrivateLink changes the network path to a service. It does not grant cross-account IAM access to feature groups or S3 data.

text: A company is building a new supervised classification model in an AWS environment. The company's data science team notices that the dataset has a large quantity of variables. All the variables are numeric. The model accuracy for training and validation is low. The model's processing time is affected by high latency. The data science team needs to increase the accuracy of the model and decrease the processing time. What should the data science team do to meet these requirements?

choices.A: Create new features and interaction variables.
choices.B: Use a principal component analysis (PCA) model.
choices.C: Apply normalization on the feature set.
choices.D: Use a multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) model.

explanation:
Key Concept: PCA compresses correlated numeric features into fewer components, potentially reducing computational cost and noise; predictive benefit must be validated.

A. Create new features and interaction variables. — Adding features increases dimensionality and can further increase processing time. It does not directly address the large existing feature set.

B. Use a principal component analysis (PCA) model. — PCA reduces the numeric feature dimension before classification, which can lower latency and remove redundancy. Retain enough predictive information and validate accuracy, since high variance is not always the same as predictive value.

C. Apply normalization on the feature set. — Normalization can improve numerical conditioning but leaves the number of variables unchanged, so it does not directly solve high-dimensional processing cost.

D. Use a multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) model. — MCA is intended for categorical variables. The question explicitly states that all input variables are numeric.
