text: An exercise analytics company wants to predict running speeds for its customers by using a dataset that contains multiple health-related features for each customer. Some of the features originate from sensors that provide extremely noisy values. The company is training a regression model by using the built-in Amazon SageMaker linear learner algorithm to predict the running speeds. While the company is training the model, a data scientist observes that the training loss decreases to almost zero, but validation loss increases. Which technique should the data scientist use to optimally fit the model?

choices.A: Add L1 regularization to the linear learner regression model.
choices.B: Perform a principal component analysis (PCA) on the dataset. Use the linear learner regression model.
choices.C: Perform feature engineering by including quadratic and cubic terms. Train the linear learner regression model.
choices.D: Add L2 regularization to the linear learner regression model.

explanation:
Key Concept: Falling training loss with rising validation loss indicates overfitting. Sparse regularization can reduce reliance on irrelevant or noisy sensor features.

A. Add L1 regularization to the linear learner regression model. — L1 can set unhelpful feature coefficients to zero, addressing the noisy-variable problem while regularizing the regression model.

B. Perform a principal component analysis (PCA) on the dataset. Use the linear learner regression model. — PCA preserves directions of high variance, which may include strong sensor noise. It does not directly select features for their relationship with running speed.

C. Perform feature engineering by including quadratic and cubic terms. Train the linear learner regression model. — Quadratic and cubic terms increase model flexibility and can worsen the observed overfitting to noisy inputs.

D. Add L2 regularization to the linear learner regression model. — L2 can also reduce overfitting, but usually retains all features with smaller coefficients. L1 is the more direct listed choice when removing noisy variables is the intended remedy.

text: A company's machine learning (ML) specialist is building a computer vision model to classify 10 different traffic signs. The company has stored 100 images of each class in Amazon S3, and the company has another 10,000 unlabeled images. All the images come from dash cameras and are a size of 224 pixels × 224 pixels. After several training runs, the model is overfitting on the training data. Which actions should the ML specialist take to address this problem? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label the unlabeled images.
choices.B: Use image preprocessing to transform the images into grayscale images.
choices.C: Use data augmentation to rotate and translate the labeled images.
choices.D: Replace the activation of the last layer with a sigmoid.
choices.E: Use the Amazon SageMaker k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) algorithm to label the unlabeled images.

explanation:
Key Concept: More independently labeled examples and realistic, label-preserving augmentation can reduce overfitting on a small image dataset.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label the unlabeled images. — Ground Truth can label the 10,000 additional images, expanding the supervised dataset beyond only 100 examples per traffic-sign class.

B. Use image preprocessing to transform the images into grayscale images. — Converting to grayscale can remove color cues that distinguish traffic signs. It does not necessarily improve generalization and may discard useful information.

C. Use data augmentation to rotate and translate the labeled images. — Appropriate rotations and translations increase training variation while preserving the sign's label. Transformations must remain realistic and must not change the sign's meaning.

D. Replace the activation of the last layer with a sigmoid. — Changing the output activation does not address the shortage of varied examples. A sigmoid is also not the usual replacement for a mutually exclusive ten-class softmax.

E. Use the Amazon SageMaker k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) algorithm to label the unlabeled images. — Automatically assigning labels with an unvalidated k-NN model can propagate mistakes. It does not supply the reliable additional labels provided by a labeling workflow.

The company has set both the enableDnsHostnames attribute and the enableDnsSupport attribute of the VPC to true. The company's DNS resolvers point to the VPC DNS. The company does not allow the ML team to access Amazon SageMaker notebooks through connections that use the public internet. The connection must stay within a private network and within the AWS internal network. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

choices.A: Create a VPC interface endpoint for the SageMaker notebook in the VPC. Access the notebook through a VPN connection and the VPC endpoint.
choices.B: Create a bastion host by using Amazon EC2 in a public subnet within the VPC. Log in to the bastion host through a VPN connection. Access the SageMaker notebook from the bastion host.
choices.C: Create a bastion host by using Amazon EC2 in a private subnet within the VPC with a NAT gateway. Log in to the bastion host through a VPN connection. Access the SageMaker notebook from the bastion host.
choices.D: Create a NAT gateway in the VPC. Access the SageMaker notebook HTTPS endpoint through a VPN connection and the NAT gateway.

explanation:

D. Create a NAT gateway in the VPC. Access the SageMaker notebook HTTPS endpoint through a VPN connection and the NAT gateway. — A NAT gateway provides outbound access to public endpoints. It does not convert the notebook HTTPS endpoint into the required PrivateLink connection.

text: A data scientist is using Amazon Comprehend to perform sentiment analysis on a dataset of one million social media posts. Which approach will process the dataset in the LEAST time?

choices.A: Use a combination of AWS Step Functions and an AWS Lambda function to call the DetectSentiment API operation for each post synchronously.
choices.B: Use a combination of AWS Step Functions and an AWS Lambda function to call the BatchDetectSentiment API operation with batches of up to 25 posts at a time.
choices.C: Upload the posts to Amazon S3. Pass the S3 storage path to an AWS Lambda function that calls the StartSentimentDetectionJob API operation.
choices.D: Use an AWS Lambda function to call the BatchDetectSentiment API operation with the whole dataset.

explanation:
Key Concept: Comprehend asynchronous analysis jobs process large document collections stored in S3 without requiring a client to coordinate one synchronous request per document.

A. Use a combination of AWS Step Functions and an AWS Lambda function to call the DetectSentiment API operation for each post synchronously. — One synchronous call per post creates a million API requests and substantial client orchestration and quota-management overhead.

B. Use a combination of AWS Step Functions and an AWS Lambda function to call the BatchDetectSentiment API operation with batches of up to 25 posts at a time. — Batches of 25 reduce request count but still require coordinating many small synchronous requests for the million-post dataset.

C. Upload the posts to Amazon S3. Pass the S3 storage path to an AWS Lambda function that calls the StartSentimentDetectionJob API operation. — An asynchronous sentiment-detection job processes the S3 collection through the service's bulk workflow. Lambda only needs to submit the job, not remain running until it completes.

D. Use an AWS Lambda function to call the BatchDetectSentiment API operation with the whole dataset. — BatchDetectSentiment cannot accept the entire million-document dataset in one request; its document-count and document-size limits still apply inside Lambda.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist at a retail company must build a system to forecast the daily sales for one of the company's stores. The company provided the ML specialist with sales data for this store from the past 10 years. The historical dataset includes the total amount of sales on each day for the store. Approximately 10% of the days in the historical dataset are missing sales data. The ML specialist builds a forecasting model based on the historical dataset. The specialist discovers that the model does not meet the performance standards that the company requires. Which action will MOST likely improve the performance for the forecasting model?

choices.A: Aggregate sales from stores in the same geographic area.
choices.B: Apply smoothing to correct for seasonal variation.
choices.C: Change the forecast frequency from daily to weekly.
choices.D: Replace missing values in the dataset by using linear interpolation.

explanation:
Key Concept: A daily forecasting series needs an explicit strategy for missing days; otherwise missing observations can distort the learned time structure.

A. Aggregate sales from stores in the same geographic area. — Combining nearby stores changes the target series and may mix different demand patterns without resolving gaps in this store's history.

B. Apply smoothing to correct for seasonal variation. — Smoothing can suppress meaningful seasonal variation instead of teaching the model to predict it. It does not directly repair the missing daily observations.

C. Change the forecast frequency from daily to weekly. — Weekly aggregation changes the forecast granularity and sacrifices the daily predictions requested by the task.

D. Replace missing values in the dataset by using linear interpolation. — Interpolation provides estimated values for missing training days and restores a regular daily series. It is a baseline to validate, especially around holidays, and must not use future validation data during training preparation.

text: A company is building custom deep learning models in Amazon SageMaker by using training and inference containers that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to reduce training costs but does not want to change the current architecture. The SageMaker training job can finish after interruptions. The company can wait days for the results. Which combination of resources should the company use to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

choices.A: On-Demand Instances
choices.B: Checkpoints
choices.C: Reserved Instances
choices.D: Incremental training
choices.E: Spot instances

explanation:
Key Concept: Interruption-tolerant training can use discounted Spot capacity and resume from saved checkpoints instead of repeating all completed work.

A. On-Demand Instances — On-Demand capacity avoids Spot interruption risk but does not provide the same cost savings for a workload that can wait and resume.

B. Checkpoints — Checkpoints preserve model and optimizer state so training can recover after interruption, reducing repeated computation.

C. Reserved Instances — EC2 Reserved Instance discounts do not directly replace SageMaker's managed training pricing model, and a long-term commitment is unnecessary for the stated flexible workload.

D. Incremental training — Incremental training updates a model using additional data. It is distinct from preserving execution state so an interrupted training job can resume.

E. Spot instances — Spot instances reduce compute cost, and the ability to wait days makes their variable availability acceptable when combined with checkpointing.

explanation:

text: A data engineer is evaluating customer data in Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. The data engineer will use the customer data to create a new model to predict customer behavior. The engineer needs to increase the model performance by checking for multicollinearity in the dataset. Which steps can the data engineer take to accomplish this with the LEAST operational effort? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to refit and transform the dataset by applying one-hot encoding to category-based variables.
choices.B: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler diagnostic visualization. Use principal components analysis (PCA) and singular value decomposition (SVD) to calculate singular values.
choices.C: Use the SageMaker Data Wrangler Quick Model visualization to quickly evaluate the dataset and to produce importance scores for each feature.
choices.D: Use the SageMaker Data Wrangler Min Max Scaler transform to normalize the data.
choices.E: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler diagnostic visualization. Use least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) to plot coefficient values from a LASSO model that is trained on the dataset.

explanation:
Key Concept: Multicollinearity diagnostics examine redundant predictor directions or coefficient behavior; ordinary scaling and feature importance do not directly diagnose it.

A. Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to refit and transform the dataset by applying one-hot encoding to category-based variables. — One-hot encoding represents categorical values but does not test for multicollinearity and can introduce exact dependencies if all dummy columns and an intercept are retained.

B. Use SageMaker Data Wrangler diagnostic visualization. Use principal components analysis (PCA) and singular value decomposition (SVD) to calculate singular values. — PCA and SVD diagnostics reveal small singular values or redundant directions, indicating that some numeric feature combinations contain little independent information.

C. Use the SageMaker Data Wrangler Quick Model visualization to quickly evaluate the dataset and to produce importance scores for each feature. — Quick Model feature importance measures predictive usefulness, which is different from diagnosing linear dependence among predictors.

D. Use the SageMaker Data Wrangler Min Max Scaler transform to normalize the data. — Min-max scaling changes feature ranges but does not remove or diagnose linear dependence between columns.

E. Use SageMaker Data Wrangler diagnostic visualization. Use least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) to plot coefficient values from a LASSO model that is trained on the dataset. — LASSO coefficient paths show how features enter or leave as regularization changes, helping identify groups of redundant predictors through the built-in diagnostic visualization.

text: A company processes millions of orders every day. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB tables to store order information. When customers submit new orders, the new orders are immediately added to the DynamoDB tables. New orders arrive in the DynamoDB tables continuously. A data scientist must build a peak-time prediction solution. The data scientist must also create an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to display near real-time order insights. The data scientist needs to build a solution that will give QuickSight access to the data as soon as new order information arrives. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST delay between when a new order is processed and when QuickSight can access the new order information?

choices.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to export the data from Amazon DynamoDB to Amazon S3. Configure QuickSight to access the data in Amazon S3.

choices.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to export the data from Amazon DynamoDB to Amazon S3. Configure QuickSight to access the data in Amazon S3.

explanation:

A Kinesis or Lambda ingestion bridge and a defined QuickSight refresh strategy are missing, so this key remains unresolved.

text: A company operates large cranes at a busy port The company plans to use machine learning (ML) for predictive maintenance of the cranes to avoid unexpected breakdowns and to improve productivity. The company already uses sensor data from each crane to monitor the health of the cranes in real time. The sensor data includes rotation speed, tension, energy consumption, vibration, pressure, and temperature for each crane. The company contracts AWS ML experts to implement an ML solution. Which potential findings would indicate that an ML-based solution is suitable for this scenario? (Choose two.)

choices.A: The historical sensor data does not include a significant number of data points and attributes for certain time periods.
choices.B: The historical sensor data shows that simple rule-based thresholds can predict crane failures.
choices.C: The historical sensor data contains failure data for only one type of crane model that is in operation and lacks failure data of most other types of crane that are in operation.
choices.D: The historical sensor data from the cranes are available with high granularity for the last 3 years.
choices.E: The historical sensor data contains most common types of crane failures that the company wants to predict.

explanation:
Key Concept: Predictive-maintenance models need representative sensor history and examples of the failures they must recognize before they occur.

A. The historical sensor data does not include a significant number of data points and attributes for certain time periods. — Missing periods and sparse attributes reduce the evidence available to learn reliable precursors and can bias the training dataset.

B. The historical sensor data shows that simple rule-based thresholds can predict crane failures. — If simple thresholds already predict failures adequately, a more complex ML system may add cost without improving the required outcome.

C. The historical sensor data contains failure data for only one type of crane model that is in operation and lacks failure data of most other types of crane that are in operation. — Failure examples from only one crane type may not generalize to the other types in operation, leaving important deployment cases unsupported.

D. The historical sensor data from the cranes are available with high granularity for the last 3 years. — Three years of high-granularity sensor history provides temporal detail and operating variation that can support learning early failure signals.

E. The historical sensor data contains most common types of crane failures that the company wants to predict. — Examples covering the common target failure modes let a supervised model learn and validate the events the company actually wants to predict.

text: A company wants to create an artificial intelligence (AI) yoga instructor that can lead large classes of students. The company needs to create a feature that can accurately count the number of students who are in a class. The company also needs a feature that can differentiate students who are performing a yoga stretch correctly from students who are performing a stretch incorrectly. Determine whether students are performing a stretch correctly, the solution needs to measure the location and angle of each student’s arms and legs. A data scientist must use Amazon SageMaker to access video footage of a yoga class by extracting image frames and applying computer vision models. Which combination of models will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Image Classification
choices.B: Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
choices.C: Object Detection
choices.D: Pose estimation
choices.E: Image Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)

explanation:
Key Concept: Person detection identifies individual people, while pose estimation locates body joints for geometric analysis of movement and posture.

A. Image Classification — Image classification assigns labels to an image but does not directly locate every student or provide arm and leg joint coordinates.

B. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) — OCR reads text and does not count people or estimate their body posture.

C. Object Detection — Object detection can locate each visible student with a person bounding box, providing the basis for a per-frame count.

D. Pose estimation — Pose estimation predicts body keypoints, allowing the application to calculate joint angles and compare the observed stretch with an appropriate reference.

E. Image Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) — An image GAN generates or transforms images. It is not the direct model for counting people or measuring their limb positions.

text: An ecommerce company has used Amazon SageMaker to deploy a factorization machines (FM) model to suggest products for customers. The company’s data science team has developed two new models by using the TensorFlow and PyTorch deep learning frameworks. The company needs to use A/B testing to evaluate the new models against the deployed model. The required A/B testing setup is as follows: • Send 70% of traffic to the FM model, 15% of traffic to the TensorFlow model, and 15% of traffic to the PyTorch model. • For customers who are from Europe, send all traffic to the TensorFlow model. Which architecture can the company use to implement the required A/B testing setup?

choices.A: Create two new SageMaker endpoints for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models in addition to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer. Create a target group for each endpoint. Configure listener rules and add weight to the target groups. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, create an additional listener rule to forward traffic to the TensorFlow target group.
choices.B: Create two production variants for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models. Create an auto scaling policy and configure the desired A/B weights to direct traffic to each production variant. Update the existing SageMaker endpoint with the auto scaling policy. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, set the TargetVariant header in the request to point to the variant name of the TensorFlow model.
choices.C: Create two new SageMaker endpoints for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models in addition to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer. Create a target group for each endpoint. Configure listener rules and add weight to the target groups. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, create an additional listener rule to forward traffic to the TensorFlow target group.
choices.D: Create two production variants for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models. Specify the weight for each production variant in the SageMaker endpoint configuration. Update the existing SageMaker endpoint with the new configuration. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, set the TargetVariant header in the request to point to the variant name of the TensorFlow model.

explanation:
Key Concept: Production-variant weights define default traffic allocation, and TargetVariant overrides that allocation for requests requiring a particular model.

A. Create two new SageMaker endpoints for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models in addition to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer. Create a target group for each endpoint. Configure listener rules and add weight to the target groups. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, create an additional listener rule to forward traffic to the TensorFlow target group. — SageMaker managed endpoints are not directly registered as the proposed ALB target groups. An additional proxy design would add work and is unnecessary for native variant routing.

B. Create two production variants for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models. Create an auto scaling policy and configure the desired A/B weights to direct traffic to each production variant. Update the existing SageMaker endpoint with the auto scaling policy. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, set the TargetVariant header in the request to point to the variant name of the TensorFlow model. — Autoscaling controls variant capacity, not the A/B traffic percentages. The weights belong in the endpoint variant configuration or its weight-update operation.

C. Create two new SageMaker endpoints for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models in addition to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer. Create a target group for each endpoint. Configure listener rules and add weight to the target groups. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, create an additional listener rule to forward traffic to the TensorFlow target group. — An NLB does not provide the described application-level listener rules for geographic routing, and managed endpoints are not direct NLB targets in this design.

D. Create two production variants for the TensorFlow and PyTorch models. Specify the weight for each production variant in the SageMaker endpoint configuration. Update the existing SageMaker endpoint with the new configuration. To send traffic to the TensorFlow model for customers who are from Europe, set the TargetVariant header in the request to point to the variant name of the TensorFlow model. — The endpoint can retain FM and add TensorFlow and PyTorch variants with 70/15/15 relative weights. Requests identified by the application as European can explicitly target TensorFlow; the weights then describe the default-routed traffic, not necessarily the final global mix.

text: A data scientist stores financial datasets in Amazon S3. The data scientist uses Amazon Athena to query the datasets by using SQL. The data scientist uses Amazon SageMaker to deploy a machine learning (ML) model. The data scientist wants to obtain inferences from the model at the SageMaker endpoint. However, when the data scientist attempts to invoke the SageMaker endpoint, the data scientist receives SQL statement failures. The data scientist’s IAM user is currently unable to invoke the SageMaker endpoint. Which combination of actions will give the data scientist’s IAM user the ability to invoke the SageMaker endpoint? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Attach the AmazonAthenaFullAccess AWS managed policy to the user identity.
choices.B: Include a policy statement for the data scientist's IAM user that allows the IAM user to perform the sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint action.
choices.C: Include an inline policy for the data scientist’s IAM user that allows SageMaker to read S3 objects.
choices.D: Include a policy statement for the data scientist’s IAM user that allows the IAM user to perform the sagemaker:GetRecord action.
choices.E: Include the SQL statement "USING EXTERNAL FUNCTION ml_function_name'' in the Athena SQL query.
choices.F: Perform a user remapping in SageMaker to map the IAM user to another IAM user that is on the hosted endpoint.

explanation:
Key Concept: Athena ML inference requires permission to run Athena queries, permission to invoke the referenced SageMaker endpoint, and an external-function declaration in SQL.

A. Attach the AmazonAthenaFullAccess AWS managed policy to the user identity. — AmazonAthenaFullAccess supplies Athena permissions for the proposed user workflow. A suitably scoped custom policy can also work; the managed policy is not the only valid way to grant access.

B. Include a policy statement for the data scientist's IAM user that allows the IAM user to perform the sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint action. — The querying IAM principal needs sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint on the model endpoint so Athena can request inference on its behalf.

C. Include an inline policy for the data scientist’s IAM user that allows SageMaker to read S3 objects. — An identity policy on the user does not grant permissions to the SageMaker service execution role, and S3 read access does not authorize endpoint invocation.

D. Include a policy statement for the data scientist’s IAM user that allows the IAM user to perform the sagemaker:GetRecord action. — GetRecord retrieves Feature Store data. It does not invoke a hosted prediction model.

E. Include the SQL statement "USING EXTERNAL FUNCTION ml_function_name'' in the Athena SQL query. — USING EXTERNAL FUNCTION declares the ML function and its endpoint and data types before the query calls it. The full declaration is required, not just the abbreviated fragment shown.

F. Perform a user remapping in SageMaker to map the IAM user to another IAM user that is on the hosted endpoint. — SageMaker endpoints do not implement the proposed remapping from one IAM user to another. Authorization is provided through IAM policies.

text: A data scientist is building a linear regression model. The scientist inspects the dataset and notices that the mode of the distribution is lower than the median, and the median is lower than the mean. Which data transformation will give the data scientist the ability to apply a linear regression model?

choices.A: Exponential transformation
choices.B: Logarithmic transformation
choices.C: Polynomial transformation
choices.D: Sinusoidal transformation

explanation:
Key Concept: A mean above the median and mode suggests right skew, but linear regression does not require normally distributed input features. Transformation suitability depends on the modeled relationship and residuals.

A. Exponential transformation — An exponential transformation usually stretches large positive values and can increase right skew rather than reduce it.

B. Logarithmic transformation — A logarithm can compress a positive right tail and sometimes linearize a multiplicative relationship. It is plausible, but positivity and the response relationship are unspecified, so it is not a universal prerequisite for regression.

C. Polynomial transformation — Polynomial features can represent nonlinear relationships, but the summary of the marginal distribution alone does not establish that a polynomial is appropriate.

D. Sinusoidal transformation — A sinusoidal transform encodes periodic effects. Nothing in the stated ordering of mean, median, and mode establishes periodicity.

text: A data scientist receives a collection of insurance claim records. Each record includes a claim ID. the final outcome of the insurance claim, and the date of the final outcome. The final outcome of each claim is a selection from among 200 outcome categories. Some claim records include only partial information. However, incomplete claim records include only 3 or 4 outcome categories from among the 200 available outcome categories. The collection includes hundreds of records for each outcome category. The records are from the previous 3 years. The data scientist must create a solution to predict the number of claims that will be in each outcome category every month, several months in advance. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Perform classification every month by using supervised learning of the 200 outcome categories based on claim contents.
choices.B: Perform reinforcement learning by using claim IDs and dates. Instruct the insurance agents who submit the claim records to estimate the expected number of claims in each outcome category every month.
choices.C: Perform forecasting by using claim IDs and dates to identify the expected number of claims in each outcome category every month.
choices.D: Perform classification by using supervised learning of the outcome categories for which partial information on claim contents is provided. Perform forecasting by using claim IDs and dates for all other outcome categories.

explanation:
Key Concept: Predicting future monthly counts by outcome category is a time-series forecasting task, distinct from classifying the outcome of an individual claim.

A. Perform classification every month by using supervised learning of the 200 outcome categories based on claim contents. — A claim classifier predicts labels for known claims. It does not directly forecast how many claims will reach each category in future months.

B. Perform reinforcement learning by using claim IDs and dates. Instruct the insurance agents who submit the claim records to estimate the expected number of claims in each outcome category every month. — There is no sequential action-and-reward environment described for reinforcement learning. Asking agents to estimate volumes also does not create the requested automated forecasting model.

C. Perform forecasting by using claim IDs and dates to identify the expected number of claims in each outcome category every month. — Aggregate unique claims by outcome date, month, and category to form count series, then forecast those series. Claim IDs support deduplication and counting rather than serving as meaningful numeric predictors.

D. Perform classification by using supervised learning of the outcome categories for which partial information on claim contents is provided. Perform forecasting by using claim IDs and dates for all other outcome categories. — Mixing individual-claim classification for some categories with forecasting for others does not consistently estimate future monthly counts across all categories.

text: A retail company stores 100 GB of daily transactional data in Amazon S3 at periodic intervals. The company wants to identify the schema of the transactional data. The company also wants to perform transformations on the transactional data that is in Amazon S3. The company wants to use a machine learning (ML) approach to detect fraud in the transformed data. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

choices.A: Use Amazon Athena to scan the data and identify the schema.
choices.B: Use AWS Glue crawlers to scan the data and identify the schema.
choices.C: Use Amazon Redshift to store procedures to perform data transformations.
choices.D: Use AWS Glue workflows and AWS Glue jobs to perform data transformations.
choices.E: Use Amazon Redshift ML to train a model to detect fraud.
choices.F: Use Amazon Fraud Detector to train a model to detect fraud.

explanation:
Key Concept: Glue crawlers discover schema, Glue jobs transform data, and the historical Fraud Detector workflow supplied managed fraud-specific model training.

A. Use Amazon Athena to scan the data and identify the schema. — Athena queries data using table metadata. A crawler is the purpose-built service for automatically discovering and registering the source schema.

B. Use AWS Glue crawlers to scan the data and identify the schema. — Glue crawlers inspect the S3 records and populate the Data Catalog with their schema, reducing manual table-definition work.

C. Use Amazon Redshift to store procedures to perform data transformations. — Redshift stored procedures require a warehouse-based workflow and data movement that are unnecessary for transforming the existing S3 data with Glue.

D. Use AWS Glue workflows and AWS Glue jobs to perform data transformations. — Glue jobs implement the transformations, and Glue workflows coordinate their execution without a separately maintained ETL cluster.

E. Use Amazon Redshift ML to train a model to detect fraud. — Redshift ML can train predictive models, but adds a Redshift-centric setup for a fraud workflow already served by the historical specialized service.

F. Use Amazon Fraud Detector to train a model to detect fraud. — Fraud Detector offered managed fraud-model training with little custom modeling. It is closed to new customers, so this service-selection answer reflects the older exam context.

text: A data scientist uses Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to define and perform transformations and feature engineering on historical data. The data scientist saves the transformations to SageMaker Feature Store. The historical data is periodically uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data scientist needs to transform the new historic data and add it to the online feature store. The data scientist needs to prepare the new historic data for training and inference by using native integrations. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

choices.A: Use AWS Lambda to run a predefined SageMaker pipeline to perform the transformations on each new dataset that arrives in the S3 bucket.
choices.B: Run an AWS Step Functions step and a predefined SageMaker pipeline to perform the transformations on each new dataset that arrives in the S3 bucket.
choices.C: Use Apache Airflow to orchestrate a set of predefined transformations on each new dataset that arrives in the S3 bucket.
choices.D: Configure Amazon EventBridge to run a predefined SageMaker pipeline to perform the transformations when a new data is detected in the S3 bucket.

explanation:
Key Concept: EventBridge can start SageMaker Pipelines from S3 events, allowing a saved transformation and feature-ingestion workflow to run when new data arrives.

A. Use AWS Lambda to run a predefined SageMaker pipeline to perform the transformations on each new dataset that arrives in the S3 bucket. — A Lambda function can start the pipeline but introduces custom orchestration code where EventBridge supports the pipeline as a target directly.

B. Run an AWS Step Functions step and a predefined SageMaker pipeline to perform the transformations on each new dataset that arrives in the S3 bucket. — Step Functions adds another workflow layer when the required transformation sequence is already defined as a SageMaker pipeline.

C. Use Apache Airflow to orchestrate a set of predefined transformations on each new dataset that arrives in the S3 bucket. — Airflow adds an orchestration environment and DAG maintenance for a simple native event-to-pipeline integration.

Configure Amazon EventBridge to run a predefined SageMaker pipeline to perform the transformations when a new data is detected in the S3 bucket. — An EventBridge rule can match the configured S3 object event and start the predefined pipeline with the required role and input parameters, avoiding a custom intermediary.

text: An insurance company developed a new experimental machine learning (ML) model to replace an existing model that is in production. The company must validate the quality of predictions from the new experimental model in a production environment before the company uses the new experimental model to serve general user requests. New one model can serve user requests at a time. The company must measure the performance of the new experimental model without affecting the current live traffic. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: A/B testing
choices.B: Canary release
choices.C: Shadow deployment
choices.D: Blue/green deployment

explanation:
Key Concept: Shadow testing copies production requests to a candidate model for evaluation while returning only the existing production model's response to users.

A. A/B testing — A/B testing routes some real users to the candidate model, so its predictions affect live user responses.

B. Canary release — A canary release exposes a small share of live traffic to the new model and therefore does not meet the requirement that it serve no user responses during validation.

C. Shadow deployment — A shadow deployment evaluates the candidate on copied production traffic while the original model remains the response source. Shadow outputs can be compared offline with outcomes and baseline predictions.

D. Blue/green deployment — Blue/green deployment provides separate environments and a traffic-switching strategy. It does not inherently mirror requests for a no-impact prediction comparison.

text: A company deployed a machine learning (ML) model on the company website to predict real estate prices. Several months after deployment, an ML engineer notices that the accuracy of the model has gradually decreased. The ML engineer needs to improve the accuracy of the model. The engineer also needs to receive notifications for any future performance issues. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Perform incremental training to update the model. Activate Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to detect model performance issues and to send notifications.

explanation:

text: A university wants to develop a targeted recruitment strategy to increase new student enrollment. A data scientist gathers information about the academic performance history of students. The data scientist wants to use the data to build student profiles. The university will use the profiles to direct resources to recruit students who are likely to enroll in the university. Which combination of steps should the data scientist take to predict whether a particular student applicant is likely to enroll in the university? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to sort the data into two groups named "enrolled" or "not enrolled."
choices.B: Use a forecasting algorithm to run predictions.
choices.C: Use a regression algorithm to run predictions.
choices.D: Use a classification algorithm to run predictions.
choices.E: Use the built-in Amazon SageMaker k-means algorithm to cluster the data into two groups named "enrolled" or "not enrolled."

explanation:
Key Concept: Predicting whether an applicant enrolls is supervised binary classification, which requires accurate historical enrollment labels.

A. Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to sort the data into two groups named "enrolled" or "not enrolled." — A labeling workflow can attach enrolled or not-enrolled outcomes to historical applicant records when those outcomes are available. Annotators must use actual records rather than guess future enrollment.

B. Use a forecasting algorithm to run predictions. — Forecasting estimates future values over time, such as total enrollment counts, rather than the binary outcome for an individual applicant.

C. Use a regression algorithm to run predictions. — Ordinary regression predicts a continuous value. A binary classifier is the direct formulation for this yes-or-no enrollment target.

D. Use a classification algorithm to run predictions. — A classifier learns the relationship between applicant features and observed enrollment labels, producing a class or probability for a new applicant.

E. Use the built-in Amazon SageMaker k-means algorithm to cluster the data into two groups named "enrolled" or "not enrolled." — K-means finds similarity-based clusters without using the enrollment outcome. Two clusters do not automatically correspond to enrolled and not enrolled.

text: A machine learning (ML) specialist is using the Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm to train a model on CPU-based Amazon EC2 On-Demand instances. The model currently takes multiple hours to train. The ML specialist wants to decrease the training time of the model. Which approaches will meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Replace On-Demand Instances with Spot Instances.
choices.B: Configure model auto scaling dynamically to adjust the number of instances automatically.
choices.C: Replace CPU-based EC2 instances with GPU-based EC2 instances.
choices.D: Use multiple training instances.
choices.E: Use a pre-trained version of the model. Run incremental training.

explanation:
Key Concept: DeepAR supports GPU acceleration and distributed training, which can reduce computation time when the dataset and configuration make effective use of the extra resources.

A. Replace On-Demand Instances with Spot Instances. — Spot changes capacity pricing and availability, not the computational speed of an otherwise identical instance. Interruptions may increase elapsed time.

B. Configure model auto scaling dynamically to adjust the number of instances automatically. — Endpoint autoscaling adjusts inference capacity. It does not dynamically add training workers to an existing DeepAR training job.

C. Replace CPU-based EC2 instances with GPU-based EC2 instances. — GPU instances can accelerate the neural-network computation in DeepAR compared with CPU-only training, subject to workload size and batch configuration.

D. Use multiple training instances. — Multiple supported training instances can distribute the work and shorten training. Communication overhead and scaling efficiency must still be measured.

E. Use a pre-trained version of the model. Run incremental training. — The built-in DeepAR workflow does not provide the proposed general pretrained-model incremental-training shortcut. GPU and distributed training are the supported acceleration paths listed.

text: A chemical company has developed several machine learning (ML) solutions to identify chemical process abnormalities. The time series values of independent variables and the labels are available for the past 2 years and are sufficient to accurately model the problem. The regular operation label is marked as 0 The abnormal operation label is marked as 1. Process abnormalities have a significant negative effect on the company’s profits. The company must avoid these abnormalities. Which metrics will indicate an ML solution that will provide the GREATEST probability of detecting an abnormality?

choices.A: Precision = 0.91 - Recall = 0.6
choices.B: Precision = 0.61 - Recall = 0.98
choices.C: Precision = 0.7 - Recall = 0.9
choices.D: Precision = 0.98 - Recall = 0.8

explanation:
Key Concept: Recall is the proportion of actual abnormalities detected. When avoiding missed abnormalities is the explicit priority, compare the recall values.

A. Precision = 0.91 - Recall = 0.6 — Recall of 0.60 misses 40% of actual abnormalities. Its stronger precision does not compensate for that under the stated detection priority.

B. Precision = 0.61 - Recall = 0.98 — Recall of 0.98 detects the highest fraction of actual abnormalities among the options, missing about 2%. The lower precision implies more false alarms, which remain a separate operational tradeoff.

C. Precision = 0.7 - Recall = 0.9 — Recall of 0.90 detects fewer true abnormalities than the 0.98 alternative, despite a somewhat higher precision.

D. Precision = 0.98 - Recall = 0.8 — Precision of 0.98 makes alarms reliable, but recall of 0.80 still misses one fifth of actual abnormalities. It does not maximize detection probability.

text: An online delivery company wants to choose the fastest courier for each delivery at the moment an order is placed. The company wants to implement this feature for existing users and new users of its application. Data scientists have trained separate models with XGBoost for this purpose, and the models are stored in Amazon S3. There is one model for each city where the company operates. Operation engineers are hosting these models in Amazon EC2 for responding to the web client requests, with one instance for each model, but the instances have only a 5% utilization in CPU and memory. The operation engineers want to avoid managing unnecessary resources. Which solution will enable the company to achieve its goal with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.A: Create an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance for pulling all the models from Amazon S3 using the boto3 library. Remove the existing instances and use the notebook to perform a SageMaker batch transform for performing inferences offline for all the possible users in all the cities. Store the results in different files in Amazon S3. Point the web client to the files.
choices.B: Prepare an Amazon SageMaker Docker container based on the open-source multi-model server. Remove the existing instances and create a multi-model endpoint in SageMaker instead, pointing to the S3 bucket containing all the models. Invoke the endpoint from the web client at runtime, specifying the TargetModel parameter according to the city of each request.
choices.C: Keep only a single EC2 instance for hosting all the models. Install a model server in the instance and load each model by pulling it from Amazon S3. Integrate the instance with the web client using Amazon API Gateway for responding to the requests in real time, specifying the target resource according to the city of each request.
choices.D: Prepare a Docker container based on the prebuilt images in Amazon SageMaker. Replace the existing instances with separate SageMaker endpoints, one for each city where the company operates. Invoke the endpoints from the web client, specifying the URL and EndpointName parameter according to the city of each request.

explanation:
Key Concept: A multi-model endpoint shares serving capacity across compatible models and selects the requested model through TargetModel.

A. Create an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance for pulling all the models from Amazon S3 using the boto3 library. Remove the existing instances and use the notebook to perform a SageMaker batch transform for performing inferences offline for all the possible users in all the cities. Store the results in different files in Amazon S3. Point the web client to the files. — Offline scoring cannot reflect a newly placed order and its current courier conditions for arbitrary new users. A notebook also is not the appropriate production inference server.

B. Prepare an Amazon SageMaker Docker container based on the open-source multi-model server. Remove the existing instances and create a multi-model endpoint in SageMaker instead, pointing to the S3 bucket containing all the models. Invoke the endpoint from the web client at runtime, specifying the TargetModel parameter according to the city of each request. — A supported multi-model container can load the city-specific XGBoost models from S3 and serve them on shared managed instances. TargetModel selects the city model, reducing the many mostly idle hosts.

C. Keep only a single EC2 instance for hosting all the models. Install a model server in the instance and load each model by pulling it from Amazon S3. Integrate the instance with the web client using Amazon API Gateway for responding to the requests in real time, specifying the target resource according to the city of each request. — Consolidating on one EC2 host reduces resource duplication but leaves model loading, availability, scaling, and host maintenance with the operations team.

D. Prepare a Docker container based on the prebuilt images in Amazon SageMaker. Replace the existing instances with separate SageMaker endpoints, one for each city where the company operates. Invoke the endpoints from the web client, specifying the URL and EndpointName parameter according to the city of each request. — Separate managed endpoints remove host administration but retain one resource allocation per city, leaving much of the low-utilization problem unresolved.

text: A company builds computer-vision models that use deep learning for the autonomous vehicle industry. A machine learning (ML) specialist uses an Amazon EC2 instance that has a CPU:GPU ratio of 12:1 to train the models. The ML specialist examines the instance metric logs and notices that the GPU is idle half of the time. The ML specialist must reduce training costs without increasing the duration of the training jobs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Switch to an instance type that has only CPUs.
choices.B: Use a heterogeneous cluster that has two different instances groups.
choices.C: Use memory-optimized EC2 Spot Instances for the training jobs.
choices.D: Switch to an instance type that has a CPU:GPU ratio of 6:1.

explanation:
Key Concept: A heterogeneous training cluster can separate CPU-heavy input preparation from GPU model computation, avoiding payment for idle accelerators while improving data supply.

A. Switch to an instance type that has only CPUs. — Removing GPUs is likely to slow deep-learning computation and does not meet the requirement to preserve training duration.

B. Use a heterogeneous cluster that has two different instances groups. — Separate CPU and GPU instance groups allow independent sizing of preprocessing and training resources. This targets a likely input-pipeline bottleneck, which should be confirmed before changing the architecture.

C. Use memory-optimized EC2 Spot Instances for the training jobs. — Memory-optimized Spot capacity does not directly address GPU starvation and can introduce interruptions. The prompt does not identify memory as the bottleneck.

D. Switch to an instance type that has a CPU:GPU ratio of 6:1. — Reducing the CPU-to-GPU ratio can worsen a CPU-bound input pipeline that already leaves the GPU idle. It is not the indicated direction of improvement.

The company wants to use the sensor data to predict equipment malfunctions and reduce services outages. Machine learning (ML) specialist needs to gather the sensors data to train a model to predict device malfunctions. choices.A: Load the data into an Amazon SageMaker Studio notebook. Calculate the first and third quartile. Use a SageMaker Data Wrangler data flow to remove only values that are outside of those quartiles.
choices.B: Use an Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler bias report to find outliers in the dataset. Use a Data Wrangler data flow to remove outliers based on the bias report.
choices.C: Use an Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler anomaly detection visualization to find outliers in the dataset. Add a transformation to a Data Wrangler data flow to remove outliers.

explanation:

A. Load the data into an Amazon SageMaker Studio notebook. Calculate the first and third quartile. Use a Data Wrangler data flow to remove outliers based on the bias report. — A bias report compares group-related outcome or representation measures. Add a transformation to a Data Wrangler data flow to remove outliers. — Data Wrangler's anomaly visualization identifies unusual records, and a flow transformation can apply the chosen filtering rule. For predictive maintenance, confirm that the removed points are errors rather than useful failure precursors.

text: A data scientist obtains a tabular dataset that contains 150 correlated features with different ranges to build a regression model. The data scientist needs to achieve more efficient model training by implementing a solution that minimizes impact on the model’s performance. The data scientist decides to perform a principal component analysis (PCA) preprocessing step to reduce the number of features to a smaller set of independent features before the data scientist uses the new features in the regression model. Which preprocessing step will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Use the Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the dataset to transform the data.
choices.B: Load the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Scale the data with a Min Max Scaler transformation step. Use the SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the scaled dataset to transform the data.
choices.C: Reduce the dimensionality of the dataset by removing the features that have the highest correlation. Load the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Perform a Standard Scaler transformation step to scale the data. Use the SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the scaled dataset to transform the data.
choices.D: Reduce the dimensionality of the dataset by removing the features that have the lowest correlation. Load the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Perform a Min Max Scaler transformation step to scale the data. Use the SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the scaled dataset to transform the data.

explanation:
Key Concept: PCA is sensitive to feature scale, so numeric variables with different units should be scaled before their covariance structure is used for dimensionality reduction.

A. Use the Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the dataset to transform the data. — Applying PCA directly can let large-range variables dominate the components even when their larger numerical scale does not imply greater predictive importance.

B. Load the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Scale the data with a Min Max Scaler transformation step. Use the SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the scaled dataset to transform the data. — Min-max scaling places the variables on comparable ranges before PCA compresses their correlated information. Fit both preprocessing steps on training data only, and validate the retained component count.

C. Reduce the dimensionality of the dataset by removing the features that have the highest correlation. Load the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Perform a Standard Scaler transformation step to scale the data. Use the SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the scaled dataset to transform the data. — Standard scaling is reasonable, but deleting correlated features first can discard information that PCA is designed to combine. That extra removal is not required by the task.

D. Reduce the dimensionality of the dataset by removing the features that have the lowest correlation. Load the data into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Perform a Min Max Scaler transformation step to scale the data. Use the SageMaker built-in algorithm for PCA on the scaled dataset to transform the data. — Weakly correlated features may contain valuable independent signal. Removing them before PCA can unnecessarily damage regression performance.

text: A machine learning engineer is building a bird classification model. The engineer randomly separates a dataset into a training dataset and a validation dataset. During the training phase, the model achieves very high accuracy. However, the model did not generalize well during validation of the validation dataset. The engineer realizes that the original dataset was imbalanced. What should the engineer do to improve the validation accuracy of the model?

choices.A: Perform stratified sampling on the original dataset.
choices.B: Acquire additional data about the majority classes in the original dataset.
choices.C: Use a smaller, randomly sampled version of the training dataset.
choices.D: Perform systematic sampling on the original dataset.

explanation:
Key Concept: Stratified splitting preserves class proportions across training and validation sets, reducing misleading evaluation caused by underrepresented classes in a random split.

A. Perform stratified sampling on the original dataset. — Stratification makes both splits more representative of the original class distribution. It improves split quality, though imbalance and overfitting may still require additional modeling changes.

B. Acquire additional data about the majority classes in the original dataset. — Adding only majority-class images worsens the relative shortage of minority examples and does not correct an unrepresentative split.

C. Use a smaller, randomly sampled version of the training dataset. — A smaller random training subset can remove useful minority examples and reduce the information available for generalization.

D. Perform systematic sampling on the original dataset. — Systematic sampling selects records at intervals and does not explicitly preserve class proportions. Dataset ordering can also introduce bias.

text: A data scientist is trying to improve the accuracy of a neural network classification model. The data scientist wants to run a large hyperparameter tuning job in Amazon SageMaker. However, previous smaller tuning jobs on the same model often ran for several weeks. The ML specialist wants to reduce the computation time required to run the tuning job. Which actions will MOST reduce the computation time for the hyperparameter tuning job? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Use the Hyperband tuning strategy.
choices.B: Increase the number of hyperparameters.
choices.C: Set a lower value for the MaxNumberOfTrainingJobs parameter.
choices.D: Use the grid search tuning strategy.
choices.E: Set a lower value for the MaxParallelTrainingJobs parameter.

explanation:
Key Concept: Tuning time falls when unpromising trials stop early and the total trial budget is reduced, with a tradeoff in how extensively the search explores.

A. Use the Hyperband tuning strategy. — Hyperband allocates increasing resources to promising trials and stops weak ones early, avoiding full training for every configuration.

B. Increase the number of hyperparameters. — Adding hyperparameters enlarges the search space and usually requires more trials to explore effectively.

C. Set a lower value for the MaxNumberOfTrainingJobs parameter. — A smaller maximum number of training jobs limits the total search work, reducing time at the cost of exploring fewer configurations.

D. Use the grid search tuning strategy. — Grid search evaluates combinations without the same adaptive early resource allocation and can become expensive in a large search space.

E. Set a lower value for the MaxParallelTrainingJobs parameter. — Reducing parallel jobs generally lengthens wall-clock search time for a fixed workload, even though fewer instances run simultaneously.

text: An insurance company is creating an application to automate car insurance claims. A machine learning (ML) specialist used an Amazon SageMaker Object Detection - TensorFlow built-in algorithm to train a model to detect scratches and dents in images of cars. After the model was trained, the ML specialist noticed that the model performed better on the training dataset than on the testing dataset. Which approach should the ML specialist use to improve the performance of the model on the testing data?

choices.A: Increase the value of the momentum hyperparameter.
choices.B: Reduce the value of the dropout_rate hyperparameter.
choices.C: Reduce the value of the learning_rate hyperparameter
choices.D: Increase the value of the L2 hyperparameter.

explanation:
Key Concept: A strong training-to-test performance gap suggests overfitting; regularization limits the model's tendency to fit training-specific details.

A. Increase the value of the momentum hyperparameter. — Momentum changes optimizer dynamics. Increasing it does not directly penalize excessive model complexity or ensure better generalization.

B. Reduce the value of the dropout_rate hyperparameter. — Reducing dropout removes regularization and can make an overfitting model rely even more strongly on training-specific patterns.

C. Reduce the value of the learning_rate hyperparameter — A lower learning rate changes optimization speed but does not directly address the model's tendency to overfit after training.

D. Increase the value of the L2 hyperparameter. — Increasing L2 strengthens the penalty on large weights, which can reduce overfitting. Tune it on validation data and reserve the test set for final evaluation.

text: A company decides to use Amazon SageMaker to develop machine learning (ML) models. The company will host SageMaker notebook instances in a VPC. The company stores training data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Company security policy states that SageMaker notebook instances must not have internet connectivity. Which solution will meet the company’s security requirements?

choices.A: Connect the SageMaker notebook instances that are in the VPC by using AWS Site-to-Site VPN to encrypt all internet-bound traffic. Configure VPC flow logs. Monitor all network traffic to detect and prevent any malicious activity.
choices.B: Configure the VPC that contains the SageMaker notebook instances to use VPC interface endpoints to establish connections for training and hosting. Modify any existing security groups that are associated with the VPC interface endpoint to allow only outbound connections for training and hosting.
choices.C: Create an IAM policy that prevents access the internet. Apply the IAM policy to an IAM role. Assign the IAM role to the SageMaker notebook instances in addition to any IAM roles that are already assigned to the instances.
choices.D: Create VPC security groups to prevent all incoming and outgoing traffic. Assign the security groups to the SageMaker notebook instances.

explanation:
Key Concept: An isolated notebook needs direct internet access disabled and explicit private routes to required AWS services. None of the options describes a complete usable configuration.

A. Connect the SageMaker notebook instances that are in the VPC by using AWS Site-to-Site VPN to encrypt all internet-bound traffic. Configure VPC flow logs. Monitor all network traffic to detect and prevent any malicious activity. — Encrypting internet-bound traffic does not satisfy a policy that forbids internet connectivity. Flow logs also record traffic rather than automatically preventing it.

B. Configure the VPC that contains the SageMaker notebook instances to use VPC interface endpoints to establish connections for training and hosting. Modify any existing security groups that are associated with the VPC interface endpoint to allow only outbound connections for training and hosting. — Interface endpoints are useful, but their security groups must allow inbound HTTPS from the notebook. Assign the IAM role to the SageMaker notebook instances in addition to any IAM roles that are already assigned to the instances. — IAM policies authorize API operations; they do not remove network internet connectivity. A notebook also does not gain arbitrary multiple execution roles as proposed.

D. Create VPC security groups to prevent all incoming and outgoing traffic. Assign the security groups to the SageMaker notebook instances. — Blocking all traffic prevents access to the S3 training data and required services. It does not provide a functional private notebook configuration.

text: A machine learning (ML) engineer uses Bayesian optimization for a hyperpara meter tuning job in Amazon SageMaker. The ML engineer uses precision as the objective metric. explanation:
Key Concept: Warm-start tuning requires a compatible objective metric. Changing from precision to recall requires a fresh search, whose elapsed time can be reduced through parallel trials.

A. Use a warm start hyperparameter tuning job. — The objective changes from precision to recall, so the previous trials cannot be reused through the stated warm-start mechanism even though the new parameter ranges overlap.

B. Use a checkpointing hyperparameter tuning job. — Training checkpoints preserve a model's training state. They do not convert an earlier precision-based hyperparameter search into a recall-based one.

C. Use the same random seed for the hyperparameter tuning job. — Reusing a random seed supports reproducibility, not faster execution of a different tuning objective.

D. Use multiple jobs in parallel for the hyperparameter tuning job. — Running multiple training trials concurrently reduces the new search's wall-clock duration within the available capacity. Very high parallelism can reduce Bayesian search adaptivity, so it should be configured deliberately.

text: A news company is developing an article search tool for its editors. The search tool should look for the articles that are most relevant and representative for particular words that are queried among a corpus of historical news documents. The editors test the first version of the tool and report that the tool seems to look for word matches in general. The editors have to spend additional time to filter the results to look for the articles where the queried words are most important. A group of data scientists must redesign the tool so that it isolates the most frequently used words in a document. The tool also must capture the relevance and importance of words for each document in the corpus. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.A: Extract the topics from each article by using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling. Create a topic table by assigning the sum of the topic counts as a score for each word in the articles. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this topic count score is higher for the queried words.
choices.B: Build a term frequency for each word in the articles that is weighted with the article's length. Build an inverse document frequency for each word that is weighted with all articles in the corpus. Define a final highlight score as the product of both of these frequencies. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this highlight score is higher for the queried words.
choices.C: Download a pretrained word-embedding lookup table. Create a titles-embedding table by averaging the title's word embedding for each article in the corpus. Define a highlight score for each word as inversely proportional to the distance between its embedding and the title embedding. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this highlight score is higher for the queried words.
choices.D: Build a term frequency score table for each word in each article of the corpus. Assign a score of zero to all stop words. For any other words, assign a score as the word’s frequency in the article. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this frequency score is higher for the queried words.

explanation:
Key Concept: TF-IDF combines a term's frequency within a document with its rarity across the document collection, highlighting words that distinguish that document.

A. Extract the topics from each article by using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling. Create a topic table by assigning the sum of the topic counts as a score for each word in the articles. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this topic count score is higher for the queried words. — Topic counts summarize latent themes rather than directly measuring how distinctive a queried word is in a particular article.

B. Build a term frequency for each word in the articles that is weighted with the article's length. Build an inverse document frequency for each word that is weighted with all articles in the corpus. Define a final highlight score as the product of both of these frequencies. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this highlight score is higher for the queried words. — Length-aware term frequency captures local prominence, while inverse document frequency downweights words common across many articles. Their product supplies the requested document-specific relevance weight.

C. Download a pretrained word-embedding lookup table. Create a titles-embedding table by averaging the title's word embedding for each article in the corpus. Define a highlight score for each word as inversely proportional to the distance between its embedding and the title embedding. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this highlight score is higher for the queried words. — Similarity to a title embedding measures semantic proximity to the title, not how frequently and distinctively the queried word occurs in the full article.

D. Build a term frequency score table for each word in each article of the corpus. Assign a score of zero to all stop words. For any other words, assign a score as the word’s frequency in the article. Configure the tool to retrieve the articles where this frequency score is higher for the queried words. — Raw term counts with stop-word removal ignore corpus-wide frequency and can favor long articles or common non-stop words. They omit the inverse-document-frequency component.

text: A growing company has a business-critical key performance indicator (KPI) for the uptime of a machine learning (ML) recommendation system. The company is using Amazon SageMaker hosting services to develop a recommendation model in a single Availability Zone within an AWS Region. A machine learning (ML) specialist must develop a solution to achieve high availability. The solution must have a recovery time objective (RTO) of 5 minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

choices.A: Deploy multiple instances for each endpoint in a VPC that spans at least two Regions.
choices.B: Use the SageMaker auto scaling feature for the hosted recommendation models.
choices.C: Deploy multiple instances for each production endpoint in a VPC that spans least two subnets that are in a second Availability Zone.
choices.D: Frequently generate backups of the production recommendation model. Deploy the backups in a second Region.

explanation:
Key Concept: High availability requires independent failure domains and sufficient healthy capacity. Multiple subnets within one Availability Zone do not provide multi-AZ resilience or prove a five-minute RTO.

A. Deploy multiple instances for each endpoint in a VPC that spans at least two Regions. — A VPC cannot span AWS Regions. Multi-Region deployment requires separate regional resources and a routing or failover design.

B. Use the SageMaker auto scaling feature for the hosted recommendation models. — Autoscaling adjusts capacity in response to demand or metrics. It does not alone establish the required failure-domain placement or recovery guarantee.

C. Deploy multiple instances for each production endpoint in a VPC that spans least two subnets that are in a second Availability Zone. — Multiple instances across at least two Availability Zones are the likely intended design. As written, two subnets in the same second AZ do not clearly specify that design, and the recovery target remains unverified.

D. Frequently generate backups of the production recommendation model. Deploy the backups in a second Region. — Backups support recovery but do not provide a ready serving endpoint or a tested five-minute failover. Cross-Region recovery would need additional deployment and routing automation.

text: A global company receives and processes hundreds of documents daily. The documents are in printed .pdf format or .jpg format. A machine learning (ML) specialist wants to build an automated document processing workflow to extract text from specific fields from the documents and to classify the documents. The ML specialist wants a solution that requires low maintenance. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.A: Use a PaddleOCR model in Amazon SageMaker to detect and extract the required text and fields. Use a SageMaker text classification model to classify the document.
choices.B: Use a PaddleOCR model in Amazon SageMaker to detect and extract the required text and fields. Use Amazon Comprehend to classify the document.
choices.C: Use Amazon Textract to detect and extract the required text and fields. Use Amazon Rekognition to classify the document.
choices.D: Use Amazon Textract to detect and extract the required text and fields. Use Amazon Comprehend to classify the document.

explanation:

A. Use a PaddleOCR model in Amazon SageMaker to detect and extract the required text and fields. Use a SageMaker text classification model to classify the document. — A custom OCR model and custom classifier both require training or packaging, hosting, and maintenance that the managed services avoid.

B. Use a PaddleOCR model in Amazon SageMaker to detect and extract the required text and fields. Use Amazon Comprehend to classify the document. — Comprehend is suitable for classification, but operating PaddleOCR in SageMaker adds a custom OCR serving workflow unnecessarily.

text: A company wants to detect credit card fraud. The company has observed that an average of 2% of credit card transactions are fraudulent. A data scientist trains a classifier on a year's worth of credit card transaction data. The classifier needs to identify the fraudulent transactions. The company wants to accurately capture as many fraudulent transactions as possible. Which metrics should the data scientist use to optimize the classifier? (Choose two.)

choices.A: Specificity
choices.B: False positive rate
choices.C: Accuracy
choices.D: F1 score
choices.E: True positive rate

explanation:
Key Concept: For rare fraud, recall measures how much fraud is caught, while F1 balances that coverage with the precision of fraud alerts.

A. Specificity — Specificity measures correctly rejected legitimate transactions. It does not directly measure the fraction of fraud captured.

B. False positive rate — False positive rate measures how often legitimate transactions are flagged. It matters operationally but does not directly reward finding actual fraud.

C. Accuracy — With only 2% fraud, a classifier that always predicts legitimate reaches 98% accuracy while detecting no fraud at all.

D. F1 score — F1 combines precision and recall, discouraging a solution that achieves high recall only by flagging almost every transaction.

E. True positive rate — True positive rate is recall: the share of actual fraud detected. Maximizing it directly supports capturing as many fraudulent transactions as possible.

text: A data scientist is designing a repository that will contain many images of vehicles. The repository must scale automatically in size to store new images every day. The repository must support versioning of the images. The data scientist must implement a solution that maintains multiple immediately accessible copies of the data in different AWS Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.A: Amazon S3 with S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)
choices.B: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) with snapshots that are shared in a secondary Region
choices.C: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage that is configured with Regional availability
choices.D: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway

explanation:
Key Concept: Versioned S3 buckets with Cross-Region Replication maintain object versions in another Region without manually provisioning storage capacity.

A. Amazon S3 with S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) — S3 scales with the object collection, versioning preserves object history, and CRR creates accessible replicas in another Region. Replication is asynchronous, so newly uploaded objects are not instantly present in both Regions.

B. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) with snapshots that are shared in a secondary Region — EBS volumes require capacity management and are not an object-versioning repository. Snapshots must be restored into volumes before normal file access.

C. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage that is configured with Regional availability — Regional EFS storage spans Availability Zones within one Region, not multiple Regions as required by the question.

D. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway — Volume Gateway exposes block volumes and cloud-backed snapshots. It does not provide the requested automatic multi-Region object repository and version access.
